workflow: wave1031-owner-decisions-2, 16 batches, decider plus skeptic, over the owner buckets of wave1031-triage-2026-10-31.json

decisions.ruling: No public edge until I name a hostname on a domain I own and have delegated to Cloud DNS. No lane invents one, because a hostname in a tfvars file is the switch that allocates a global address and opens 443. The module and its refusals stay as built, and the row stays PARTIAL, as R12-API-8054 already decided for the same chain.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/public-edge/main.tf declares google_compute_security_policy.edge (:59), google_certificate_manager_certificate_map.edge (:404), google_compute_global_address.edge (:450) and google_compute_global_forwarding_rule.https (:462), all gated on hostnames. modules/public-edge/tests/public-edge.tftest.hcl::a_declared_hostname_creates_the_whole_edge_and_nothing_on_port_80 proves the plan. infrastructure/environments/dev/terraform.tfvars:596 leaves public_edge commented out, with the note that publishing a surface is the owner's decision. qip-acceptance tests/terraform_plan.rs:486 no_environment_opens_a_public_address holds that state in all four environments. ADR 0095 makes the portal's run.app URL behind IAP the path and the custom domain optional. The domain is an external registrar item. docs/ops/runbooks/dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5 prices no LB, Armor or CDN, so FUND_THEN_DEPLOY cannot name a figure. This ruling matches R12-API-8054 (STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL).
decisions.closure: The owner delegates a domain they own to Cloud DNS and approves the LB, Cloud Armor and CDN monthly cost in a priced ADR. A protected patch then sets public_edge.hostnames in infrastructure/environments/dev/terraform.tfvars. It narrows no_environment_opens_a_public_address to test, stage and prod and adds a dev plan assertion that the LB, the security policy, the CDN backend and the certificate map are created. The owner dispatches the plan.
decisions.skeptic: Every citation checks out. In public-edge/main.tf, security_policy.edge is at :59, certificate_map.edge at :404, global_address.edge at :450 and global_forwarding_rule.https at :462. public-edge.tftest.hcl:47 has the run a_declared_hostname_creates_the_whole_edge_and_nothing_on_port_80. In dev tfvars the public_edge block at :596 is commented out, and the note at :589 says publishing is the owner's decision. terraform_plan.rs:486 no_environment_opens_a_public_address checks all four environments. ADR 0095's title makes the run.app URL behind IAP the path and the custom domain optional. Readiness §5 prices no LB, Armor or CDN. The ruling matches R12-API-8054 (STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL). The closure narrows the test only after the owner decides, which is the place the test's own message names for recording that decision.

decisions.ruling: MFA is already mandatory, and the row's text saying ENABLED is corrected. Passkeys follow ADR 0038 as accepted: its one passkeyEnrollment:start probe against the dev project picks Shape A or Shape B. Until that probe runs I neither raise the provider pin nor change the tenant in the console, because either would pick a credential design on no evidence and the console change would put tenant state outside Terraform. The row stays PARTIAL until the probe runs on a billed, running dev project.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/identity/variables.tf::mfa_state defaults to "MANDATORY" and its validation admits nothing else. Root infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf:1442 identity_mfa_state validates the same. modules/identity/tests/mfa.tftest.hcl runs mfa_is_mandatory_by_default_with_a_factor_that_is_not_sms, optional_mfa_is_refused and mfa_off_is_refused. modules/identity/main.tf has no passkey block, and the google provider is pinned "~> 6.12" (infrastructure/terraform/main.tf:30). ADR 0038 decision 2 is accepted as a table with one activation step: the probe against algorik-dev, whose outcome selects the shape. The ADR stays deliberately open on the shape because no reading of the tree answers it. O23 is therefore answered by an existing ADR and needs no new one. Dev billing and the registry's state are UNVERIFIED (dev-redeploy-readiness.md).
decisions.closure: Now: correct the row's current text to cite variables.tf::mfa_state (MANDATORY only) and mfa.tftest.hcl. After the owner brings dev up: the owner runs ADR 0038's probe and quotes the HTTP status and code into ADR 0038's status line (a protected docs/adr edit, so it is the owner's act or a lane patch). A lane then implements the selected shape. It adds a plan or test assertion that MFA is MANDATORY and passkeys are enabled, with a mutation that drops the passkey setting.
decisions.skeptic: The MFA half is correct. modules/identity/variables.tf mfa_state defaults to MANDATORY and its validation admits nothing else. Root variables.tf:1442 identity_mfa_state does the same, mfa.tftest.hcl has the three runs, and the pin is ~> 6.12 at main.tf:30. The passkey half misreads ADR 0038. The 'deliberately still proposed, no reading of the tree answers it' passage is the superseded 2026-09-05 status. The current status (lines 3-8 and 431-487) records that the orchestrating session ran check 1's documentation half on 2026-09-19. The passkey methods are routed but absent from the v2 discovery document, the REST reference and the release notes. On that evidence the ADR selects table row three: stay on the password path and do not fall through to Shape B. It says explicitly that 'the keyed probe can no longer select Shape A', and that 'what reopens this is a documentation event, not a probe'. The trigger is a single uncredentialed curl of identitytoolkit $discovery/rest?version=v2 showing a passkey count above 0. So the blocker is a vendor publishing event, not a dev deploy. The closure must not have the owner run the keyed probe and quote it into ADR 0038 as the selecting act. Corrected closure: correct the row's current text to cite variables.tf::mfa_state (MANDATORY only) and mfa.tftest.hcl. Set the gap to ADR 0038's row-three outcome, with no pin raise and no console change. Reopen only when Google's v2 discovery document lists the passkey methods, quoting its revision string. Then follow ADR 0038's table.

decisions.ruling: The requirement stands as written: Spanner owns financial truth and Bigtable owns hot features. I will not map the fact classes onto today's local stores so the row passes. Both stores stay declined under decision 5 until the deploy has run and a store record states the measured need and a monthly ceiling, as R12-LEDGER-7009 and R12-DATA-9053 already decided. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: Financial truth today lives in backend/crates/apps/qip-ledgerd/src/store.rs (the local DurableStore) and the kernel ledger. Event history and offsets live in qip-streaming event_fabric/broker.rs::commit_offset. enable_spanner is false in every tfvars, and no Bigtable resource or adapter exists. R12-AMBIENT-9001 decided O02 narrowly: BigQuery is the one evidence store, and Bigtable, Spanner Graph and Knowledge Catalog stay declined. R12-LEDGER-7009 (STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY) keeps the ledger off Spanner until after the deploy, at $2,705-$8,140 a month (docs/blueprint/lanes/billed-plan-2026-10-19.md item 7). R12-DATA-9053 puts Bigtable at about $950 a month at the floor. Neither figure is in dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5, so this ruling funds nothing. A single-writer test written against the stores the requirement does not name would encode the wrong owners.
decisions.closure: Trigger: R12-LEDGER-7009's Spanner ledger and R12-DATA-9053's Bigtable are funded by their ADRs and deployed. A lane then writes the fact-class-to-store map in code (financial truth to Spanner, event history and offsets to the fabric, archives to GCS, hot features to Bigtable). It adds a qip-acceptance architecture test that fails when a second writer of any class exists, with the mutation of a second ledger-class writer.
decisions.skeptic: The decision rests on decision 5, R12-LEDGER-7009 (billed-plan item 7, $2,705-$8,140), R12-DATA-9053 (about $950) and R12-AMBIENT-9001, and it is consistent with all of them. enable_spanner is false in all four tfvars. broker.rs::commit_offset exists at :2120, and qip-ledgerd store.rs is the local durable store. The ruling does not restate the requirement to pass. One text fix is needed, and the decision does not turn on it. 'No Bigtable resource' is wrong: modules/data/main.tf:479 declares google_bigtable_instance.timeseries, gated by enable_bigtable, which is false in every tfvars. The rationale should say the resource is declared but off and no Rust adapter exists (qip-storage provider.rs stops at the gRPC client).

decisions.ruling: O24 is declined before the deploy, as ADR 0191 already decided for the world model. The three central brains, qip-api, qip-fastbrain and qip-deepbrain, stay the decomposition, each with its own RunService and scaling block. No cognitive library is split into its own Cloud Run service now. Each new service is an image, an identity and a bill, so the split takes its own ADR naming the services and their monthly cost once dev runs. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/Cargo.toml links qip-world-model, qip-reasoning-engine and qip-learning-engine in-process. Only infrastructure/gitops/envs/dev/{api,fastbrain,deepbrain}.yaml declare a RunService, and each has a scaling block (fastbrain.yaml:42 minInstanceCount 1). ADR 0191 decision 1 says no separate world-model service is built or deployed before the deployment phase, because a new Cloud Run service is billed infrastructure the owner put last. ADR 0191 decision 4 defers the split to its own ADR naming the store and its cost. The triage's reading that min-0 services fall outside decision 5 contradicts ADR 0191 decision 1, so it is not adopted. No cost for the new services is named in dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5.
decisions.closure: After the dev deploy: an ADR names each cognitive service to split, its min and max instances and its monthly ceiling. For each one, a lane then adds an apps/* binary, a catalogue.tf entry, a RunService manifest and a workload-register entry. It adds a qip-acceptance test that each named cognitive service has its own binary and scaling block, with the mutation of folding one back into qip-kernel.
decisions.skeptic: qip-kernel Cargo.toml links qip-world-model (:37), qip-reasoning-engine (:39) and qip-learning-engine (:45). The scaling blocks are at api/fastbrain/deepbrain.yaml:42, and fastbrain has min 1. ADR 0191 decision 1 does say a new Cloud Run service is billed infrastructure the owner put last, and decision 4 defers the split to its own priced ADR. Rejecting the triage's min-0 exemption is therefore consistent with ADR 0191 and decision 5. One text fix: 'only api, fastbrain and deepbrain declare a RunService' is inexact, because portal.yaml and openobserve.yaml also do. No cognitive library has its own RunService, which is the point the ruling needs.

decisions.ruling: Vertex AI Agent Engine is not admitted. It is a paid managed runtime that holds agent sessions and memory outside the event log, and decision 5 keeps new billed services out. From now on an agent manifest names its runtime, the in-process host is the only runtime admitted, and a manifest naming any other runtime is refused at load. I will not build a second runtime only to meet the count, so the row stays PARTIAL on 'two runtimes are supported'.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-agents/src/manifest.rs:88 AgentManifest has no runtime field. qip-agents/src/runtime.rs::AgentHost is the only host. It is used by qip-fastbrain/src/roster.rs, qip-deepbrain/src/roster.rs and qip-investment-agents/src/chief.rs. O25's costs are a managed paid runtime and a contract change to AgentManifest. AgentManifest is a serialized contract, so naming the runtime needs an ADR first. Refusing an unknown runtime adds a refusal and loosens nothing.
decisions.closure: After the ADR: add runtime: AgentRuntime to AgentManifest. AgentRuntime is an enum whose only variant is InProcess, with serde default InProcess so committed manifests still decode, and with no #[serde(other)] fallback. Test in qip-agents tests/agents.rs: a manifest naming a runtime other than the in-process host is refused at load, and every fastbrain and deepbrain roster manifest names the in-process host. Mutation: add a #[serde(other)] arm that maps an unknown runtime to InProcess; the test must fail. Agent Engine is reopened only by a priced ADR after the deploy.
decisions.adr_title: An agent manifest names its runtime, the in-process host is the only runtime admitted, and Vertex AI Agent Engine waits on a funded record
decisions.skeptic: manifest.rs:88 AgentManifest is a Serialize/Deserialize struct with no runtime field. runtime.rs:432 AgentHost is the only host, and fastbrain roster.rs, deepbrain roster.rs and investment-agents chief.rs reference it. A runtime enum with InProcess as its only variant, a serde default and no #[serde(other)] adds a refusal and loosens nothing. Declining the paid Agent Engine follows decision 5. The ruling keeps the row PARTIAL on 'two runtimes' and does not restate it. No prior ruling covers the agent runtime. When the ADR is written, it should state whether the new field changes any recorded manifest digest.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0147 decision 8 stands: no capital specialist agent is added, because a second control over the same RiskState would be a correlated second finding from one origin. The half that decision promised is built now. RiskControl reports the capital facts it already holds and covers a new Scope::CapitalPosition, so removing the control drops the scope. The requirement still names a Capital Brain covering grants, placement and compounding, and I do not restate it to pass. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0147 decision 8 and its rows-unblocked line say: feed plus capital facts and Scope::CapitalPosition on RiskControl, and no capital specialist agent. qip-investment-agents src/chief.rs:442 standard_agents has no capital agent. src/coverage.rs::Scope has no CapitalPosition, and a grep of backend/crates finds none. qip-risk src/limits.rs::RiskState already carries cash, funding_buffer, margin_utilisation and survival_gross_ceiling. Have RiskControl::analyse (src/control.rs) emit each label as a computed fact from desk.risk, only where the value is present. No veto, limit or figure changes. decisions.skeptic: Accepted ADR 0147 decision 8 (lines 141-148) and its rows-unblocked line (:306) prescribe exactly this: capital facts and Scope::CapitalPosition on RiskControl, and no capital specialist. coverage.rs::Scope has no CapitalPosition, and a grep of backend/crates finds none. chief.rs:442 standard_agents and control.rs RiskControl::analyse (:53) exist. RiskState in qip-risk limits.rs has cash, survival_gross_ceiling (:906), margin_utilisation (:920) and funding_buffer (:929), the last three as Options, which fits 'only where present'. The stale-premise correction holds: platform.rs:6106 'desk.book = book.gate', brief_the_desk_on_book at :11732 and desk_is_fed at :11688. The test removing_the_risk_control_drops_forecast_stress_and_recommendation_from_coverage exists at organisation.rs:2445. The change adds facts and coverage only, so it is tightens-only. decisions.ruling: I declare no yield shelf, no routed share and no ladder horizons. The share is a new capital limit whose only effect is to give up liquidity the confidence governor withheld, so it is not a tightening. Decision 7 keeps nothing new sized until a RISK record argues the numbers, and ADR 0159 left them to that record. The router stays built, called from DECIDE in all three roots and unarmed. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: data/datasets/yield-shelf.json has "instruments": [] and no routing block, so qip-capital src/bank.rs::route_idle_cash routes nothing. ADR 0159's status says it does not authorise any shelf capacity or any share of cash routed. Its decision 7 says the routed share is a limit with no default and that an unset share leaves routing unarmed. Its consequences say a placement reduces free cash for up to a day and the share is the only lever on liquidity given up. QIP_YIELD_SHELF_PATH is read at qip-api src/main.rs:877, qip-fastbrain :495 and qip-deepbrain :1394, and no manifest sets it. The requirement carries LIVE_CAPITAL and EXTERNAL_ACTION. The real-world sweep is refused under ADR 0021, and only the paper hold is built. This ruling matches R12-CAPITAL-4085 and R12-ASSET-4070: nothing new is sized.
decisions.closure: Reopened only by a RISK record under decision 7 that argues the shelf (cash, stable_value or short_duration instruments realised within 24 hours), max_share and ladder_horizons_hours. The figures are then committed to yield-shelf.json. A protected patch mounts the file and sets QIP_YIELD_SHELF_PATH (modules/cloudrun plus infrastructure/environments/dev). A test shows a default start routes only cash above the floor, dated on the ladder. After the owner's dev deploy, one journaled YieldRoutingEntry is quoted in the row.
decisions.skeptic: yield-shelf.json has "instruments": [] and no routing block. bank.rs:658 route_idle_cash exists. QIP_YIELD_SHELF_PATH is read at qip-api main.rs:877, fastbrain :495 and deepbrain :1394, and nothing under infrastructure sets it. ADR 0159's status explicitly does not authorise any shelf capacity or routed share, and its decision 7 (:114) makes the routed share a limit with no default. Declining to size anything is consistent with decision 7, R12-CAPITAL-4085 and R12-ASSET-4070. The ruling refuses the real-world sweep under ADR 0021 and says so.

decisions.ruling: Refused. An autonomous treasury transfer is money movement, and a corridor an intent could honestly use needs a real external destination, which only live capital has. No fabric command file is declared. The platform never mints a TransferIntent from its own pre-positioning plan, because a machine attesting its own enforcement points attests to itself. The veto-only gate stays as built and tested, ADR 0003 and ADR 0021 stand, and the row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: qip-capital-fabric src/gate.rs::TransferIntent and checks_passed, plus qip-kernel src/platform.rs:10356 Platform::decide_fabric, re-derive and veto. qip-api src/main.rs:1291 load_fabric_declaration is the only door, through QIP_CAPITAL_FABRIC_PATH. infrastructure/environments/dev/terraform.tfvars:427-456 keeps capital_fabric_file null on purpose, and test, stage and prod say the same. qip-api src/ledger_views.rs:86 GATE_NOTE says the gate is veto-only with no transfer engine behind it. qip-api tests/fabric.rs proves that an off-corridor or over-cap intent is vetoed whole. The requirement carries LIVE_CAPITAL and EXTERNAL_ACTION. This ruling does not contradict R12-RES-7099, whose custody-staleness veto in decide_fabric is one more refusal.
decisions.closure: None under any delegation. The gap opens with: refused under ADR 0003 and ADR 0021, because a declared corridor needs a real external destination that only live capital provides. It is reopened only if the owner accepts ADR 0108 in writing. Paper-side vetoes such as R12-RES-7099's may still be added. Nothing that builds or declares an intent may be added.
decisions.skeptic: gate.rs has TransferIntent at :113 and checks_passed at :705. platform.rs:10356 decide_fabric exists, as does qip-api main.rs:1291 load_fabric_declaration. ledger_views.rs:86 GATE_NOTE says the gate is veto-only. Dev tfvars:427-455 keep capital_fabric_file unset, and test, stage and prod carry the same note. qip-api tests/fabric.rs exists. The row's requirement is autonomous money movement, so REFUSE_LIVE under ADR 0003/0021 is correct, and refusing a self-minted intent is fail-closed. It is consistent with R12-RES-7099, whose custody veto is one more refusal in decide_fabric.

decisions.ruling: O15 is declined: quoting keeps no path to an order, on the simulator as everywhere else. Lifting quote_loop's no-path-to-an-order and the edge node's quoting refusal would remove two guards from the paper boundary. Quoting is order submission at every real venue, so no delegation opens it. The reservation table keeps holding every cell order, arbitrage legs included. The row stays PARTIAL on its market-making clause. If an ADR ever admits quoting, its quotes reserve through RegionTable and nowhere else.
decisions.rationale: The qip-kernel src/quote_loop.rs module doc says it is the most dangerous composition in the workspace and has no path to an order, a broker or a venue. ADR 0067 'What would make this wrong' names anything that gives a QuotePair a destination. qip-edge-node src/lib.rs:231-250 enables only OrderTaking and Routing in qip-execution-engine modes.rs::ModeGate, so ContinuousQuoting stays refused at Cell::send. qip-edge src/reservation.rs:121 RegionAllocation and :522 RegionTable hold every cell order today. The delegation does not lift 'no weakening of a guard or a paper-trading layer', as R12-MESH-5064 already applied to a risk ordering.
decisions.closure: None under this delegation, and the requirement's separate-ledger mutation stays unrunnable. The gap opens with the refusal. Any future ADR that admits quoting must route quote reservations through qip-edge RegionTable. It must carry the test that a quote and an arbitrage leg on the same capital cannot both reserve it, and a mutation that gives quoting a separate ledger must make that test fail.
decisions.skeptic: quote_loop.rs's module doc says it is the most dangerous composition and has no path to an order, a broker or a venue. ADR 0067 'What would make this wrong' names giving a QuotePair a destination. apps/qip-edge-node/src/lib.rs enables only OrderTaking and Routing on the ModeGate; the path is apps/, not edge/. ContinuousQuoting is a ModeGate mode that stays disabled. reservation.rs has RegionAllocation at :121 and RegionTable at :522. Lifting the two guards would weaken the paper boundary, so refusing is correct. The ruling matches R12-MESH-5064 and R12-AGENCY-6098. The conditional reservation clause is for any future ADR only and loosens nothing.

decisions.ruling: The Cloud Build private pool stays off, as R12-FINOPS-9189 already ruled. It bills per build minute, holds a private-service-access peering, and its monthly cost is named nowhere I can read, so decision 5 keeps it off until dev runs. The module, its mocked-plan tests and deploy.yml's --worker-pool submission stand as written. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/build-pool/main.tf declares google_cloudbuild_worker_pool.pool. infrastructure/terraform/tests/build-pool.tftest.hcl runs no_pool_is_planned_unless_the_build_environment_enables_one, an_enabled_pool_is_peered_into_the_engineering_network and a_pool_outside_the_build_environment_is_refused. infrastructure/environments/dev/terraform.tfvars:327 sets cloud_build_private_pool_enabled = false. .github/workflows/deploy.yml:663 reads that line, :885 submits with --worker-pool, and :891 stops when the pool is missing. dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5 prices no pool. R12-FINOPS-9189 says 'The Cloud Build private pool stays off.'
decisions.closure: Trigger: the dev deploy has run, and an ADR states the pool's monthly ceiling. The owner then flips the protected dev tfvars line to true, reads the plan, applies it and dispatches deploy.yml. The row closes on that run's images job logging the worker pool id, plus a check that a build on ubuntu-latest fails while the pool is on.
decisions.skeptic: build-pool/main.tf:60 google_cloudbuild_worker_pool.pool exists. build-pool.tftest.hcl has the three named runs (:57, :74, :104). Dev tfvars:327 sets the pool to false. deploy.yml reads the flag at :663, submits with --worker-pool at :885 and exits at :891 with nothing built on the runner. Readiness §5 prices no pool. The ruling matches R12-FINOPS-9189 ('stays off'), and R12-CICD-10160 and R12-CICD-8008 (turned on after dev serves, with its cost named first).

decisions.ruling: I choose a replica, not multi-region. The replica is a second Artifact Registry repository in another region, and deploy.yml copies each signed digest into it. Moving the existing repository to a multi-region location would replace it and delete the signed images. The replica is a new billed resource whose monthly cost is named nowhere, so under decision 5 it waits for the deploy and an ADR stating the ceiling. The row stays PARTIAL, and node-local copies wait on an execution node.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/registry/main.tf:22 declares google_artifact_registry_repository.images at var.region, with immutable_tags = true (:33). No replica or remote repository exists. qip-acceptance tests/infrastructure.rs:6732 the_image_registry_is_not_world_readable_and_nothing_can_delete_from_it holds the immutable, no-delete half; the row cites :4801, which has drifted. .github/workflows/deploy.yml is protected. dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5 prices no replica. The registry answered 403 on the last pushes (2026-10-31 decision 5), and no execution node exists to keep a local copy.
decisions.closure: After the dev deploy and an ADR naming the ceiling: add a replica repository to modules/registry with immutable tags, CMEK and no delete grant, covered by a tftest. Add a gate-adding deploy.yml patch under docs/blueprint/lanes/ that copies each signed digest to the replica and fails the deploy when a copy fails. Extend the_image_registry_is_not_world_readable_and_nothing_can_delete_from_it to require the replica. Node-local copies follow the first execution node.
decisions.skeptic: The rationale misreads the code and ignores R12-RES-9177. The replica already exists: infrastructure/terraform/modules/registry/secondary.tf declares google_artifact_registry_repository.images_secondary. It has immutable tags, its own CMEK key ring and key, CI as writer with no delete grant, and secondary_region defaults to null. modules/registry/tests/secondary.tftest.hcl covers it with 4 runs. The cost is named: billed-plan-2026-10-19.md item 9, 'Registry replica, CICD-10046, $0.50 to $3.10'. R12-RES-9177 (IMPLEMENT) already chose replica over multi-region. It also assigned the free half to a lane-written protected patch: a null-default root secondary_region passed to module.registry, plus a deploy.yml step that copies each promoted digest and fails unless the digest resolves. This closure tells a lane to build the replica module and tftest again, behind a dev deploy and a new ADR, which contradicts R12-RES-9177's 'free half lands now'. The bucket stays STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY, because naming a secondary_region bills and decision 5 holds it. Corrected closure: depend on R12-RES-9177's patch, which no docs/blueprint/lanes/*.patch carries yet. After the dev deploy and an ADR stating the ceiling (billed-plan item 9), the owner sets secondary_region in protected dev tfvars. Extend the_image_registry_is_not_world_readable_and_nothing_can_delete_from_it (infrastructure.rs:6732) to require the secondary when declared. Node-local copies follow the first execution node.

decisions.ruling: O19 is answered: provenance is a gcloud-only SLSA statement attached to the pushed digest with Google's own tooling, and no third-party action enters the supply chain. As R12-CICD-9108 already decided, it ships in the same deploy.yml patch as the SBOM. That patch is written only after dev's registry answers again, and a failed attach fails the deploy. The row stays PARTIAL until a deploy run shows every pushed digest attested.
decisions.rationale: .github/workflows/deploy.yml:1118 'gcloud beta container binauthz attestations sign-and-create' is the only attestation, and a grep for slsa or provenance in deploy.yml finds no step. The Makefile has an sbom target. qip-acceptance tests/gitops.rs:4598 the_pipeline_no_longer_moves_a_service_and_still_signs_attests_and_refuses_prod covers the signature only. R12-CICD-9108 (STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY) attaches SBOM, scan and provenance with gcloud and Artifact Analysis, admits no new tool without an ADR, and holds the patch until the registry stops answering 403 (2026-10-31 decision 5). gcloud is not a new tool, so no ADR is needed. No provenance patch exists under docs/blueprint/lanes/.
decisions.closure: After dev's registry answers: a lane writes one patch under docs/blueprint/lanes/ with R12-CICD-9108's. The patch adds a deploy.yml step that generates an in-tree SLSA provenance statement for each pushed digest, attaches it with gcloud (Artifact Analysis) and reads it back, failing the deploy on any error. It also adds a gitops.rs test that fails when the step or its needs-wiring is removed. The owner applies the patch. The row closes on a deploy run in which every pushed digest carries provenance.
decisions.skeptic: deploy.yml:1118 'gcloud beta container binauthz attestations sign-and-create' is the only attestation, and a grep finds no slsa or provenance step. Makefile:123 has the sbom target. gitops.rs:4598 the_pipeline_no_longer_moves_a_service_and_still_signs_attests_and_refuses_prod exists. No lane patch carries SLSA provenance; the deploy_provenance.rs hits in the cicd-9106, l6-cicd-7116-7119 and l6-cicd-9066 patches are the ci-run provenance test, not SLSA. The ruling matches R12-CICD-9108 (STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY): gcloud and Artifact Analysis only, the patch held until the registry stops answering 403, and a failed attach fails the deploy. gcloud is not a new tool, so needing no ADR does not contradict 9108's 'no new tool without an ADR'.

decisions.ruling: The tests/ directory exclusion goes. A fixture passes only if its path and its exact matched text are both on a list in a protected file, which only a person can lengthen. No fake-key marker is honoured, because a marker pasted beside a real key reads the same as one beside a fake. The history scan uses the same list. Any other historical finding is rotated, or recorded in scripts/secrets-reviewed.txt with its reason.
decisions.rationale: scripts/check-secrets.sh::EXCLUDE_PATHS (:51-58) still holds ':(exclude)*/tests/*'. Both the history scan's git log (:109) and the tree scan's git grep (:141) use it, so a key under any tests/ directory passes both scans and the check 'committing a key fixture must fail CI' is unmet. Hole (1) is closed: secrets-scan-protected.patch is applied, -e is at :141, and pipeline_scripts.rs::a_private_key_left_in_the_tree_fails_the_tree_scan covers it. A git grep of the seven patterns over */tests/* on 2026-10-31 finds exactly seven fixture lines: qip-data-finder/tests/tiers.rs:420-421, qip-market-ingestion/tests/connector_manifest.rs:69, qip-acceptance/tests/security.rs:1130 and :1145, frontend/portal/tests/compliance.spec.ts:100 and data-sources-health.spec.ts:74. scripts/check-secrets.sh and scripts/secrets-reviewed.txt are protected globs in scripts/agent-policy.json. A seven-entry list in place of a directory exclusion widens the scanner, so this is a tightening and not the scanner narrowing that the permission layer refuses.
decisions.closure: A lane writes the patch over four files. (1) scripts/check-secrets.sh: delete ':(exclude)*/tests/*' from EXCLUDE_PATHS. Add a readonly FIXTURES array of '<path><TAB><exact matched text>' entries for the seven lines above. The tree scan drops a match only when both path and text equal an entry, and the history scan skips an added line only on the same equality. (2) scripts/secrets-reviewed.txt: one '<commit> <path> <reason>' line for each historical fixture finding outside the list, found by a full-history run (fetch-depth 0). Quote that run's output in the patch's commit message to show no real key is admitted. (3) backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/pipeline_scripts.rs: add test a_key_fixture_under_a_tests_directory_fails_both_scans. It plants a runtime-built PEM header in crate/tests/fixture.rs, commits it, and requires exit 1 from the tree scan and from --history. (4) In the same file, add test a_listed_fixture_passes_only_at_its_own_path: the listed text copied to another path fails. Mutation: restore the */tests/* exclusion and the first test fails. Match the list on text alone and the second test fails. Decision 3 of 2026-10-31 covers it, because it adds a refusal and loosens nothing, so the parent applies it on the integration branch. The row stays PARTIAL until the patch is applied and ci's tree and history scans pass on it.
decisions.skeptic: The citations check out. scripts/check-secrets.sh:51-58 still holds ':(exclude)*/tests/*'. The history scan uses it at :109 and the tree scan at :141. ci.yml:709-711 runs both scans with fetch-depth 0. check-secrets.sh and scripts/secrets-reviewed.txt match protected globs in agent-policy.json. Replacing the directory exclusion with an exact (path, text) list makes the scanner wider, so this is a tightening. The two notes below are for the lane. (1) With the exclusion removed, the tree scan reports 6 lines, not 7: security.rs:1145 is a cert-manager.io/inject-ca-from-secret comment, and the existing filter already drops it. The list needs only 6 entries. (2) Matching on path and text alone would still admit a second identical line in the same file. For example, a real PEM pasted into qip-data-finder/tests/tiers.rs with the same header line would pass. That is the ruling's own marker objection. Each entry should admit one occurrence per path, and test (4) should also plant a duplicate at the listed path.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0114 D4 stands and I do not supersede it. As R12-CICD-10160 and R12-CICD-8008 already ruled, Config Sync and Argo Rollouts do not go on the control plane, and no fifth controller does. I also do not narrow the requirement to the controllers ADR 0114 admits. Config Connector carries the baseline layer, as it does for R12-CICD-10087. The Rollouts mechanism stays declined, and its canary capability is to be evidenced at R12-CICD-9116. The row stays PARTIAL, with both declined mechanisms named in its gap.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0114 (:29) says the control plane 'runs Config Connector, Argo CD, Kargo and cert-manager and nothing else'. D4's table keeps R12-CICD-9113 (Argo Rollouts) in 'Stays BLOCKED (the mechanism is the requirement)'. qip-acceptance gitops.rs::the_control_plane_bootstrap_installs_only_the_controllers_adr_0114_names (:7230) refuses RootSync (:7202) and Rollout (:7210). infrastructure/gitops/bootstrap holds only argocd, cert-manager, config-connector, config-connector-operator, gateway and kargo. The triage's closure would replace that guard test, which weakens a guard. It would also add two controllers to a billed cluster before dev serves, against decision 5. R12-GCP-8116 set the same pattern: the requirement text stands and the row stays PARTIAL under D4. R12-CICD-9116 is still MISSING, so the canary capability is not evidenced yet either.
decisions.closure: Regrade the gap. Open it with this ruling, name Config Sync and Argo Rollouts as declined by ADR 0114 D4, and leave gitops.rs's guard test unchanged. The row stays PARTIAL until two things are shown. First, a running dev control plane where Argo CD, Kargo and Config Connector each reconcile only their own layer: no_object_is_rendered_by_both_an_argo_cd_application_and_the_bootstrap (gitops.rs:7374) must hold against the live sync. Second, a run on dev of R12-CICD-9116's traffic-split canary. Both wait on the owner's dev deploy.
decisions.skeptic: The code citations check out. ADR 0114:29 says 'and nothing else'. gitops.rs refuses RootSync at :7202 and Rollout at :7210 (test at :7230), and the no-double-render test is at :7374. infrastructure/gitops/bootstrap holds only the six directories named. This is consistent with R12-CICD-10160 and 8008. The closure contradicts the ruling, though. The ruling says the requirement is not narrowed and both declined mechanisms stay named in the gap. The closure then says the row 'stays PARTIAL until' Argo CD, Kargo and Config Connector reconcile on dev and the 9116 canary runs. That lets the row close on the equivalents, which restates the requirement so it passes. The requirement says Config Sync must own baseline/policy/CRDs and Argo Rollouts must own progressive rollout, and each controller must be installed. ADR 0114 D4 (:172-182) puts R12-CICD-9113 (Argo Rollouts) in the column 'Stays BLOCKED (the mechanism is the requirement)'. R12-CICD-10087 is no precedent: its requirement reads 'Config Sync / Argo CD', so Argo CD alone meets it. Corrected closure: keep the ruling and leave gitops.rs unchanged. Record the dev reconciliation and the 9116 canary run as evidence only. The row stays PARTIAL while ADR 0114 D4 declines Config Sync and Argo Rollouts, and reopens only if an ADR admits them.

decisions.ruling: Every agent commit names its role and its model, from the same instant that R12-CICD-9083's lane trailer becomes required. A commit missing either is refused. A reviewer-role commit that names a model used by any coder-role commit in the same change stays refused, as today. The agent definitions pin every coder's model, and no reviewer agent may share a model with any coder agent. code-reviewer therefore moves off claude-opus-5-5, the model the coders run on.
decisions.rationale: scripts/agent-guard.mjs::judgeChange step 1a (:298-320, applied in 4c0afbde) judges model independence only when one change carries both an Agent-Role coder commit and an Agent-Role reviewer commit. In the last 200 commits, none carries Agent-Role or Agent-Model, and 73 carry 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5'. So the rule binds nothing today. .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md pins model claude-opus-5-5, the same model that wrote those commits, and no coder agent file pins a model. That is exactly the dependence the requirement forbids. Step 1c (:345-375) already has the switch to reuse: policy.lane_manifest.trailer_required_after, under which an unparseable instant refuses everything. scripts/agent-guard.mjs, agent-guard.test.mjs and .claude/** are protected, and the permission layer refuses .claude/** to agents.
decisions.closure: A lane writes the patch over four files. (1) scripts/agent-guard.mjs: in judgeChange, under lane_manifest.trailer_required_after, refuse every non-merge agent commit at or after the instant that lacks Agent-Role or Agent-Model. Step 1a's same-model refusal stays. (2) scripts/agent-guard.test.mjs: tests that a post-instant agent commit with no Agent-Model is refused, that one with no Agent-Role is refused, and that a pre-instant one is not judged. Mutation: drop the new filter and the first two tests fail. (3) .claude/agents/*.md: add 'model: claude-opus-5-5' to backend-, frontend-, data-ai-, cloud-platform-engineer, sre-release-engineer, test-engineer, technical-writer and ux-designer. Move code-reviewer.md to claude-sonnet-5-5, the model security-engineer already uses. (4) backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/cicd_gates.rs: extend code_reviewer_and_security_engineer_have_distinct_models with a test that no reviewer-kind agent shares a model with any coder-kind agent and that every coder pins one. Mutation: set code-reviewer back to claude-opus-5-5. The .claude/agents hunk is the owner's to git apply, because the permission layer refuses it to an agent. The rest is applied under decision 3 of 2026-10-31. The row stays PARTIAL until the whole patch is applied.
decisions.skeptic: The closure breaks an existing guard test. backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/cicd_gates.rs:23 code_reviewer_and_security_engineer_have_distinct_models asserts that the two models differ (assert_ne!, :41-45). .claude/agents/security-engineer.md:3 already pins claude-sonnet-5-5. Moving code-reviewer to claude-sonnet-5-5 'the model security-engineer already uses' fails that test, or forces someone to weaken it. agent-policy.json:65-74 has two reviewer kinds (code-reviewer, security-engineer) and eight coder kinds. The closure pins all coders to claude-opus-5-5, so the two reviewers need two different models, both different from the coders' model. The test's valid list (:48-52) leaves claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 for code-reviewer. Corrected closure: same four-part patch, but code-reviewer.md moves to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. code_reviewer_and_security_engineer_have_distinct_models stays unchanged, and the new reviewer-vs-coder test sits beside it. Everything else verifies: judgeChange step 1a at agent-guard.mjs:298-320, trailer_required_after at :348-360, no Agent-Role or Agent-Model trailer in the last 200 commits (78, not 73, carry 'Claude Opus 5.5' at this HEAD), and consistency with R12-CICD-9083. Minor: agent-guard.test.mjs is not itself a protected glob.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0102 is not amended, as R12-CICD-10168 ruled, and no development-agent task moves into a fleet worker. A development agent's task runs in agent-sandbox.yml's ephemeral hosted job under that job's own contents:read token (R12-FINOPS-9189). A fleet task runs as an ephemeral Cloud Run Job task under the keyless fleet-worker account. IAM conditions hold that account to reading packets/ and HALT and to writing output/ and ledger/. I mint no per-task credential in the dispatcher, because a token handed through a Job's configuration is a worse credential than the metadata server's. The fleet bills up to ADR 0102's $25 a day and comes after the deploy (decision 5). The row stays PARTIAL, with the shared account named against 'task-scoped', and the requirement is not narrowed to fit it.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/fleet/main.tf declares google_service_account.worker (:102) with no key. Every task of google_cloud_run_v2_job.fleet (:274) runs as it (service_account :290). locals.worker_reads_condition and worker_writes_condition (:73-81) bound it by object prefix, not by task. scripts/fleet/worker.mjs (:1-11) makes one chat call with 'no shell, no checkout, no tool', per ADR 0102. .github/workflows/agent-sandbox.yml grants 'permissions: contents: read' and no id-token (:9, :60-61) on ubuntu-latest runners. infrastructure/fleet/variables.tf::daily_usd_ceiling refuses anything above 25 (ADR 0102 decision 5). No plan or apply of the fleet root is recorded. The triage's closure amends ADR 0102, which R12-CICD-10168 declined.
decisions.closure: Open the gap with this ruling, dated 2026-10-31. It names the shared fleet-worker account as unmet against the task-scoped clause and the agent-sandbox job token as the development agents' worker identity. Nothing is built now. The trigger is set: after dev serves, the owner funds the fleet at ADR 0102's ceiling of at most $25 a day and plans and applies infrastructure/fleet. The row stays PARTIAL until that plan and apply are recorded and the identity on it is task-scoped.
decisions.skeptic: The fleet facts check out. The worker account is at fleet/main.tf:102, the Job at :274 runs as it (:290), and the prefix conditions are at :73-81. worker.mjs:1-11 is one call with no tool, and daily_usd_ceiling is capped at 25 (variables.tf:85). Not amending ADR 0102 is consistent with R12-CICD-10168. But one claim misreads the code. The ruling says 'a development agent's task runs in agent-sandbox.yml's ephemeral hosted job under that job's own contents:read token' and names that token as 'the development agents' worker identity'. agent-sandbox.yml:1-7 says it runs only a lane's acceptance commands, on a branch an agent already wrote. The agent's own work (model calls, edits, commits, push) runs in the owner's sessions under the owner's identity. That is ADR 0098, and the agent-policy.json markers comment: 'An agent session that pushes as its user... is invisible'. Writing the sandbox token into the gap as the agents' scoped identity would mark the requirement as met for development agents, which restates it so it passes. Also, the closure requires a task-scoped identity that the ruling itself refuses to build, so the row cannot close under this ruling. Corrected gap: name the shared fleet-worker account as unmet. State that development-agent tasks run in the owner's sessions with no ephemeral, task-scoped identity, and that only their acceptance runs in the sandbox. Keep the funding trigger at the $25/day ceiling after dev serves. The row stays PARTIAL until a task-scoped identity exists, which needs a later ADR.

decisions.ruling: Every lane is metered. The sandbox reads the lane's own model-gateway ledger, committed on the lane branch at docs/blueprint/lanes/spend/<lane>.jsonl. It runs the trusted copy of agent-lanes.mjs spend and fails the lane in three cases: tokens or USD past the manifest's budget, a line it cannot read, or no ledger. The ledger is the lane's own report. It bounds an honest lane and refuses one that reports nothing. It does not prove a lane spent nowhere else, and the row's gap says so.
decisions.rationale: scripts/agent-lanes.mjs::judgeSpend (:208) and the spend mode (:294-307, which errors on an unreadable ledger) are tested in agent-lanes.test.mjs. No workflow calls them: agent-sandbox.yml runs only validate and budget (:108-109), check-diff (:141) and accept (:186), and ci.yml:740 runs only validate. scripts/model-gateway.mjs writes ALGORIK_WORKER_LEDGER, which defaults to .worker-spend.jsonl. .gitignore:32-33 keeps that file out of git, so a lane's ledger needs a committed path. agent-sandbox.yml, scripts/agent-lanes.mjs and agent-policy.json lane_limits are protected. R12-CICD-10116 keeps model egress out of the sandbox, and this step reads a file and calls no model.
decisions.closure: A lane writes the patch over four files. (1) .github/workflows/agent-sandbox.yml: after the accept step in the accept job, run 'node trusted/scripts/agent-lanes.mjs spend --policy trusted/scripts/agent-policy.json --manifest "trusted/$MANIFEST" --lane "$LANE" --ledger "lane/docs/blueprint/lanes/spend/$LANE.jsonl"', with no continue-on-error. (2) scripts/agent-lanes.mjs: check-diff admits exactly the lane's own docs/blueprint/lanes/spend/<lane>.jsonl and refuses another lane's. (3) scripts/agent-lanes.test.mjs: tests that a lane with no ledger file is refused and that check-diff admits a lane's own ledger but not another's. (4) backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/pipeline_scripts.rs: test the_sandbox_meters_the_lanes_model_spend_from_the_trusted_script_and_a_missing_ledger_fails_it. It asserts the step exists after accept, calls trusted/scripts, and has no '|| true' or continue-on-error. Mutation: delete the step or append '|| true' and the test fails. The parent applies it under decision 3 of 2026-10-31, because it adds a gate. The row stays PARTIAL until one dispatched sandbox run has metered a lane. Making the sandbox required for merge remains the owner's ruleset setting.
decisions.skeptic: The citations check out: judgeSpend at agent-lanes.mjs:208, spend mode at :294-311, sandbox steps at :108-109, :141 and :186, ci.yml:740 runs validate only, model-gateway.mjs:82 writes .worker-spend.jsonl, and .gitignore:32-33 keeps it out of git. Adding the step is a tightening. But two claims do not hold. (1) The ruling says the meter 'refuses one that reports nothing'. In fact judgeSpend skips blank lines and lines for other agents, then passes zero tokens and zero USD with no problems (:212-246). So an empty or foreign-only spend/<lane>.jsonl passes, and only a missing file fails (:303-306). (2) scripts/model-gateway.mjs:1-8 is the worker gateway for delegated tasks. The lane session's own model calls never enter that ledger. So 'Every lane is metered', and closing the row after 'one dispatched sandbox run has metered a lane', would meet 'a budget that is enforced' on a meter that misses the lane's main spend. That restates the requirement so it passes. Corrected closure: same four parts. In addition, spend refuses a ledger with no billed line attributed to the lane, as the fail-closed reading already used for unreadable lines, and agent-lanes.test.mjs gets a test for it. Mutation: drop the check and an empty ledger passes. The row's gap names the session's own model spend as unmetered, and the row stays PARTIAL after a metered run until that spend is read.

decisions.ruling: O22 is declined: no libfuzzer-sys and no nightly toolchain enter the build. A second toolchain and a new crate would be a standing cost and an exception to ADR 0109, for a gate the in-tree generator can carry. CI's fuzz gate is a seeded random-input test over the decoders that read bytes from outside the process. It runs in the existing test job on every pull request. Any panic fails it, and the seed and the input are printed so the crash reproduces. A coverage-guided engine is reopened only by an ADR that names a crash class this gate missed.
decisions.rationale: qip-acceptance tests/property_fuzz.rs uses qip_core::Xoshiro256 and qip_core::testing::Property, 'avoiding the need for an external fuzzing dependency'. Its thirteen cases test only Decimal, Duration and Rng algebra, never a parser, so the requirement's rationale ('Parsers fail on inputs nobody wrote by hand') is unmet. The tree has decoders that take outside bytes: qip-peer src/lib.rs::decode(frame, max_frame) (:566), qip-contracts src/knowledge_pack.rs::KnowledgePack::decode (:128), qip-kernel src/breadth.rs::BreadthPlan::from_json (:171) and qip-storage src/lake_codec.rs decode (:136). The requirement asks for a fuzz job that runs on pull requests and fails on a crash, and does not ask for coverage guidance. This adds a check, admits no dependency, and touches no protected path.
decisions.closure: Add one fuzz test per decoder crate, each using qip_core::Xoshiro256. The tests: qip-peer tests/fuzz_decode.rs a_peer_frame_of_random_or_mutated_bytes_is_refused_or_decoded_and_never_panics; qip-contracts tests/fuzz_decode.rs a_knowledge_pack_of_random_or_mutated_bytes_is_refused_or_decoded_and_never_panics; qip-kernel tests/fuzz_breadth_plan.rs a_breadth_plan_of_random_or_mutated_json_is_refused_or_parsed_and_never_panics; qip-storage likewise for the lake codec. Each runs a fixed regression seed set plus a bounded batch of fresh cases. The fresh seed derives from GITHUB_SHA when set and is fixed otherwise. Inputs are mutations of a valid encoding as well as uniform bytes. Each call is wrapped in std::panic::catch_unwind, and a panic fails the test with the seed and the hex input. Mutation: in qip-peer decode, replace one bounds-checked length read with a direct slice index; the test panics and fails. Regrade the row once a ci run on a pull request shows the tests ran. Status stays PARTIAL until the lane's mutation report is recorded.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. property_fuzz.rs has 13 tests on Decimal, Duration and Rng only, and uses qip_core::Xoshiro256 and testing::Property (:8-15). The decoders exist at the cited lines: qip-peer decode (:566), KnowledgePack::decode (:128), BreadthPlan::from_json (:171) and lake_codec decode (:136). All four crates already depend on qip-core, so no dependency is added and ADR 0109 is not engaged. Declining libfuzzer-sys and nightly is the conservative choice. The requirement is 'A fuzz job runs on PRs and fails on a crash', with no coverage guidance, so random and mutation-based inputs in the PR test job meet it without restating it. panic = "abort" is set only in [profile.release] (backend/Cargo.toml:202), and ci runs these crates under nextest's default profile, so catch_unwind works. No protected path is touched.

decisions.ruling: Publish to the two repositories; do not remove them. Deleting them would be a destructive apply and would rewrite the waiver test, and the requirement names both. For the commit it built, deploy.yml uploads two things. The workspace's packaged crates go to qip-rust-<env>. The rendered deployment bundle, an OCI image-layout tarball, goes to qip-deployments-<env>. Each is a version named by the sha256 of its bytes. A failed upload fails the deploy. An existing version with the same digest counts as success, as the image step already treats an existing tag. No new tool enters the pipeline, as R12-CICD-9108 requires.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/registry/main.tf declares google_artifact_registry_repository.rust_packages (:154) and deployment_bundles (:206) as GENERIC. Both carry CI writer grants (rust_packages_ci_push, deployment_bundles_ci_push), and roles/artifactregistry.writer cannot delete. qip-acceptance pipeline_waivers.rs:185-212 asserts both are declared. A grep of .github/workflows and scripts for qip-rust, qip-deployments, rust_packages or deployment_bundles finds nothing, so nothing publishes. deploy.yml (:705-730) already pushes images by an immutable tag and treats an existing one as the commit's own. The repositories already exist, so publishing creates no new billed resource under decision 5. deploy.yml is a protected path.
decisions.closure: A lane writes the patch over two files. (1) .github/workflows/deploy.yml: after the image is signed, package the workspace crates and build the gitops render plus images.tfvars digests as an OCI image-layout tarball (index.json and blobs/sha256/, made with tar and sha256sum). Upload each with 'gcloud artifacts generic upload' to qip-rust-<env> and qip-deployments-<env>, with the version set to its sha256. A describe that finds the same version is success, and any other failure fails the job. (2) backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/infrastructure.rs: add test every_registry_repository_has_a_workflow_that_publishes_to_it. Mutation: delete the bundle upload and the test fails. pipeline_waivers.rs stays unchanged. The owner applies the patch, because it is a deploy.yml step and not a gate. The row stays PARTIAL until a dev deploy.yml run shows both versions by digest, which also waits on the registry answering again (R12-CICD-9108).
decisions.skeptic: Verified. rust_packages (:154) and deployment_bundles (:206) are GENERIC and carry writer grants for the CI account (:173-178, :224-229). pipeline_waivers.rs asserts both exist. Nothing in .github/workflows or scripts publishes to them. deploy.yml:709-730 already treats an existing image tag as the commit's own. Publishing and not deleting follows the requirement, deploy.yml is protected, and the owner applies the patch. This is consistent with R12-CICD-9108 (no new tool). Two notes for the lane. (1) `cargo package` refuses a non-dev path dependency that has no version. backend/Cargo.toml:116 declares `qip-core = { path = ... }` with none, so packaging the workspace crates also needs versions on the workspace path dependencies, a third, unprotected file. (2) Both repositories set cleanup_policy_dry_run = true (:165, :216), so every deploy's upload accumulates. State the storage cost in the closure: Artifact Registry storage above the 0.5 GB free tier, cents a month at this size.

decisions.ruling: O21 is admitted narrowly. A release is refused before traffic moves when the plane's error budget is spent. After traffic moves, the same deploy.yml run that a person dispatched reads the plane's release decision. If the decision refuses, or cannot be read, the run moves traffic back to the previous promoted revision, rebuilds nothing, and fails. The incident is a drafted record for a person and is never sent outside (ADR 0213, R12-OBS-9158). No standing controller, no agent and no new credential rolls anything back.
decisions.rationale: qip-observability src/aiops.rs::release_gate (:541) and qip-kernel src/blueprint_objectives.rs::release_decision (:450) are tested, behind platform.rs::Platform::release_decision (:11523), in qip-kernel tests/self_observation.rs. No crate under backend/crates/apps or services calls release_decision. deploy.yml (:705-730) makes a rollback a person's re-dispatch of an earlier commit. ADR 0114 D4 keeps Argo Rollouts refused and puts rollback to the previous promoted digest (ADR 0115) at R12-CICD-9116. R12-OBS-9158 and ADR 0213 decision 2 refuse the SRE agent any rollback credential. deploy.yml is already in scripts/agent-policy.json dispatch_refused_for_agents and already holds the identity that moves revisions, so a revert inside that run adds no actor and no credential. Returning to a digest that already passed promotion, and treating an unreadable decision as a refusal, only removes exposure. This changes the release contract and ADR 0114's position on automated rollback, so it needs an ADR first.
decisions.adr_title: A dispatched deploy reverts its own release to the previous promoted revision when the plane's release decision refuses or cannot be read, drafts the incident for a person, and no controller or agent rolls back
decisions.closure: The lane first claims the ADR in docs/adr/README.md under the title above, in its own pushed commit. Then three changes. (1) qip-api serves the plane's Platform::release_decision read-only. Test: a_spent_error_budget_reads_as_a_refused_release. (2) Add scripts/release-revert.sh. It takes the decision URL, the service and the previous revision. On a refused or unreadable decision it runs 'gcloud run services update-traffic <svc> --to-revisions=<previous>=100', writes an incident draft to the job summary and exits 1. On an allowed decision it moves nothing. (3) qip-acceptance pipeline_scripts.rs test, with a fake gcloud on PATH: a_refused_or_unreadable_release_decision_moves_traffic_back_to_the_previous_revision_and_fails_the_run_and_an_allowed_one_moves_nothing. Mutation: read a non-200 response as allowed, and the unreadable case fails. A lane writes the deploy.yml step as the protected patch named here: a pre-traffic gate on the decision, then release-revert.sh after traffic moves. The owner applies it. The row stays PARTIAL until a dev deploy.yml run records a decision read.
decisions.skeptic: The citations verify: release_gate at aiops.rs:541, release_decision at blueprint_objectives.rs:450 and platform.rs:11523, and no app or service calls it. deploy.yml is in dispatch_refused_for_agents. This is consistent with R12-OBS-9158, since no agent and no new credential are involved. But the post-deploy revert rests on a misread of what the decision measures. Platform::release_decision reads 'this process's own error budgets' (platform.rs:11520-11521). release_gate states 'An objective nothing measured never blocks' (aiops.rs:538-540). Right after traffic moves, the qip-api revision being read has a fresh ObjectiveLedger, so it returns Proceed. The revert therefore cannot fire on a regression the new revision introduced. It also reads one instance of one service, not 'the plane'. The fake-gcloud test and the close condition 'a dev run records a decision read' would let the row pass without showing the requirement's 'a regression triggers rollback'. That restates it so it passes. Corrected: keep the ADR and the scope (person-dispatched run, previous promoted revision, incident drafted only). The ADR must name where the decision is read from: the series pushed per ADR 0121, over a stated soak window. It must also say that a plane with nothing observed in that window reads as unreadable, so traffic is reverted. ADR 0114 D4 names the same source for R12-CICD-9116. The row closes only on a dev run in which an induced regression moved traffic back and drafted the incident.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0153 decision 8 is amended in its chargeback clause only; its ledger clause stands. A commerce plan must declare a paper chargeback rate beside its fees, and a plan without one is refused at load. Each unit's payment_chargeback_risk is that rate applied to the unit's sale value. Feasibility deducts it from expected resale, so it can only lower a margin. The simulated merchant still takes no payment network, so no chargeback is raised or booked, and the ledger keeps to facts a producer observed.
decisions.rationale: qip-kernel src/commerce_research.rs::unit_attributes (:1060) sets payment_chargeback_risk to Attr::Absent (:1122-1127), because 'a simulated merchant takes no payment network'. The plan already declares its other synthetic economics in the same way: CommercePlan::purchase_tax_rate (:277), and the terms.fees behind the marketplace_fees attribute (:1115-1119). ADR 0153 decision 7 refused booking a TaxCharge but left the declared purchase tax rate in feasibility. The same split applies here: a declared rate drives the attribute and feasibility, and nothing is booked. qip-financial src/commerce.rs::FeasibilityInput::assess (:291) refuses a missing input through need() (:282), so a required chargeback input fails closed. This changes ADR 0153's text and the plan contract, so it needs an ADR first. The plane runs on the default path only through R12-COMMERCE-5091's patch.
decisions.adr_title: A commerce plan declares a paper chargeback rate, a unit's chargeback risk is read from it and reserved against its resale, and no chargeback is booked
decisions.closure: The lane claims the ADR, amending ADR 0153 decision 8's chargeback sentence, in its own pushed commit. Then: in qip-kernel commerce_research.rs, add chargeback_rate to the plan's terms, validated to [0, 1), with a missing value refused at load. unit_attributes sets payment_chargeback_risk to a value of rate times the unit's sale value, with the rate named. In qip-financial commerce.rs, FeasibilityInput gains the chargeback reserve, which need() refuses when missing and assess subtracts from expected resale. Tests: a_units_chargeback_risk_is_the_plans_declared_rate_on_its_sale_value_and_lowers_its_expected_resale, and a_commerce_plan_without_a_chargeback_rate_is_refused_at_load. Mutation: return Attr::Absent again, or add the reserve instead of subtracting it. Update the existing plan fixtures to declare the rate. The committed dev plan in R12-COMMERCE-5091's patch carries it. The row stays PARTIAL until that patch is applied.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. unit_attributes is at commerce_research.rs:1060, payment_chargeback_risk is Attr::Absent at :1122-1127, purchase_tax_rate is at :277 and the fees attribute at :1115-1119. FeasibilityInput::assess is at qip-financial commerce.rs:291 and need() at :282. ADR 0153 d8 (:96-102) declines the attribute only for want of a settlement term. A declared paper rate that can only lower expected resale, with a plan refused when the rate is missing, is fail-closed and books nothing. ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT is right because it changes ADR 0153 and the plan contract. Notes. (1) The ADR must be a new record amending d8. Editing docs/adr/0153-*.md itself is protected and needs a person. (2) Unit attributes are set at receipt, before any sale, so the risk should apply the rate to the candidate's expected resale. (3) Its default-path dependency is the commerce dev mount, which now waits on its own ADR (see R12-COMMERCE-5091).

decisions.ruling: R12-ASSET-4073 stands: the commerce-only breadth plan ships on in dev's committed configuration, and only in dev. The patch carries four parts together: a root variable that is null everywhere but dev, the catalogue's optional-file rule, a seeded secret, and dev's deep-brain manifest. No compiled-in default is added. with_the_breadth_plan_unset_no_commerce_plane_runs and the cloudrun module's _PATH validation stay as they are. decisions.rationale: qip-financial src/commerce.rs::scout (:83) runs in qip-kernel commerce_research.rs DISCOVER. It runs only once qip-deepbrain src/breadth.rs::install loads PLAN_VARIABLE 'QIP_DEEPBRAIN_BREADTH_PLAN' (:26), and load returns None when that is unset (:30-33). (2) catalogue.tf optional_config_files (:59-85) mounts a file only where a root variable names it. (3) infra.yml:866's committed seed list writes the config secrets. (9) manifest_wiring.rs: move the entry from unset to set-in-dev. Add test the_committed_dev_plan_installs_a_commerce_plane_whose_scout_emits_candidates in qip-deepbrain tests/commerce.rs. In gitops, deepbrain.yaml:78-84 and :151-166 project universe.json from one single-payload secret (qip-universe-catalogue-dev) mounted at that hash directory. gitops.rs:2966-2971 requires that mount point to equal the directory QIP_UNIVERSE_PATH names. A second secret volume cannot share that mountPath. Elsewhere it would break parity with the module's computed env path. Part (8), 'a secret volume, as universe.json has', therefore fails. gitops.rs:5793 every_hash_named_path_a_manifest_mounts_is_the_name_terraform_publishes_the_committed_bytes_under also refuses any tfvars that sets an optional config-file variable (:5822-5832), and requires exactly one /etc/qip path per RunService. Neither appears in the closure. Lane L1 hit exactly this, and the owner recorded it as decision 13 of 2026-10-31 (commit 7e9a5e0d): 'the commerce dev mount waits on its own ADR'. The rest checks out: scout at :83, PLAN_VARIABLE and load at breadth.rs:26-33, the _PATH regex at cloudrun variables.tf:329, optional_config_files, the unset guard at tests/commerce.rs:186, and ADR 0153:184. Corrected: an ADR first, titled like 'A workload's committed configuration files mount one per file under their own content-hash path, so a second file never moves the universe's path'. Then the one protected patch: the _PATH rename, variables.tf, dev tfvars, the infra.yml seed list, catalogue.tf, deepbrain.yaml and manifest_wiring. The gitops.rs:5793 test is extended to derive each file's path, not weakened. No compiled-in default, and the regex is not loosened. The row stays PARTIAL until the patch is applied.

The rest is verified: into_plan :560, CommerceResearch::open building the draft at :493-512 (so a partial plan exits 78 at install), breadth.rs::load, the test at deepbrain tests/commerce.rs:209, ADR 0153 'Not decided here'. decisions.skeptic: It shares 5095's mount and so inherits the same flaw: the unprotected half cannot land before the patch (undeclared root variable in main.tf, a dev secret volume with no secret behind it, and the catalogue.tf arm that manifest_wiring :2509/:2659 requires). It also misreads the plan. The closure says 'the committed plan states at least two simulated resale venues with distinct fees and carry'. But CommercePlan and ResaleEntry are #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] (commerce_research.rs:259-288), and ResaleEntry holds only floor_per_unit, markdown_after_days and markdown_rate.
