Verified: route_resale :146, ResaleDesk::new :488, imports :51-52, tests/commerce_resale.rs :184/:215/:249, and with_the_breadth_plan_unset_no_commerce_plane_runs (:186) unchanged.

decisions.ruling: A connector's claim reaches the world model only as an EvidencePacket. The connector already forms the packet as a gate and then drops it. From now on it hands that packet to the kernel's evidence intake, and the intake admits nothing the contract's decode refuses. The packet is still not journaled: evidence.admitted stays the journal (ADR 0152 decision 2), and links stay derived by replay. I do not switch a connector on in dev's tfvars to make the row pass. The row stays PARTIAL until a committed environment polls one after dev runs.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/evidence_packet.rs::EvidencePacket refuses on construction and on decode (tests/section27_contracts.rs::an_evidence_packet_round_trips_and_refuses_a_missing_unknown_or_foreign_field). qip-market-ingestion src/connector/evidence.rs::CheckedEvidence::packet (:126) documents itself as 'the §27 EvidencePacket another brain receives'. ConnectorRuntime::poll (runtime.rs:926-940) forms the packet and drops it, under ADR 0152 decision 3. qip-kernel src/evidence_intake.rs::Platform::admit_world_records / absorb_evidence (:323, :349) take qip_market_ingestion's CheckedEvidence (:53) instead of the contract. So the seam where a claim crosses into UNDERSTAND is typed by an ingestion-internal struct, and the §27 contract has no receiver. Giving the packet a receiver changes ADR 0152 d3, so an ADR comes first. Journaling the packet is refused: its contradiction links would be a second claim beside d2's derived links, which d2's dissent rules out. The tfvars flip is not written. infrastructure/environments/dev/terraform.tfvars:505-530 keeps deepbrain_connector null: the egress proxy has never been applied, and decision 5 of 2026-10-31 puts dev's base deploy first. Adding a refusal at intake is a tightening.
decisions.adr_title: The world model takes a connector's claim only as an EvidencePacket: the kernel's evidence intake receives the §27 packet instead of CheckedEvidence, amending ADR 0152 decision 3, and the packet is still not journaled
decisions.closure: Lane L2 claims the ADR number in docs/adr/README.md first. Then ConnectorRuntime::poll hands on the packet it forms, beside the record it rests on. Platform::admit_world_records and absorb_evidence take EvidencePacket plus the document hash and decode it through the contract before admission. The fast brain's feed.rs connector arm and the deep brain's connector arm pass packets. EvidenceAdmittedRecord stays the journal, with no packet journal. tests/evidence_stage.rs::a_poll_report_carries_no_packet_until_a_consumer_asks_for_one is replaced, not deleted, by a test that the packet reaches the intake. New test: a claim handed to the kernel's evidence intake without its licence or content hash is refused there and never admitted to the fabric, and a complete packet is admitted with its source and licence intact. Mutation: build the admitted claim from the packet's fields without running its decode refusals; the test fails. The row stays PARTIAL until deepbrain_connector is set in a committed environment, which is a protected tfvars step after dev runs.
decisions.skeptic: The diagnosis is verified: CheckedEvidence::packet :126, poll forms the packet and drops it at runtime.rs:925-940, evidence_intake.rs imports CheckedEvidence at :53 with admit_world_records/absorb_evidence at :322/:349, ADR 0152 d2/d3, dev tfvars deepbrain_connector commented null. The closure, though, loosens guards. It has admit_world_records and absorb_evidence take 'EvidencePacket plus the document hash' instead of CheckedEvidence, and its mutation builds the admitted claim from the packet's fields. EvidencePacketFields (evidence_packet.rs:50-68) lacks EvidenceRecord fields the fabric needs. authenticity_signals drive the spoofed verdict and the withholding of spoofed claims (qip-evidence fabric.rs:223-232). metadata attribute/value feeds ClaimKey::of and so every knowledge delta (fabric.rs:364-367). claimed_at and caused_by drive the temporal-consistency check (evidence.rs:228-239). Built from the packet, spoof withholding stops firing and no claim yields a delta. Corrected: the ADR has the intake receive each CheckedEvidence together with its EvidencePacket. The intake decodes the packet through the contract and refuses on failure, an added refusal, while admission still runs on the full record. Mutation: skip the packet decode at intake. The closure also omits the third caller, qip-api routes.rs:2264 (and qip-api feed.rs), though compilation would force it. Refusing a packet journal and leaving tfvars unflipped stay correct.

decisions.ruling: The attribution chain is the producer's fact, so the cell carries it. Decision::Filled gains the intent and decision ids the cell already holds when it sends the order, and posting refuses a fill that lacks them. I do not choose a central lookup by order id. The owner of a fill is the cell that sent the order. I do not invent a strategy-to-mandate map: no record assigns strategies to mandates, and one would attribute paper P&L to user mandates nobody asked for. Events ledgerd already holds stay readable as schema 1 and are never rewritten.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0153 decision 1 says a fact books only when something observed it, and the producer journals the operation. A chain the centre rebuilds from the journal by order id is a fact no producer stated, and an incomplete journal would leave a gap in it that no one sees. backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/ledger.rs::LedgerEvent keeps owner and attribution as Option (:364-366), and Attribution (:374) names fill, order, intent and decision ids. backend/crates/libs/qip-portfolio/src/ledger.rs::PaperFill (:51) carries source, venue, object, side, quantity, price, fee and shares, with no intent or decision id. backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/src/cell.rs Decision::Filled (:8074) journals order_id but neither id. backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/desk_fabric.rs:104-105 is the one PaperFill::try_from plus post seam. qip-contracts ledger_operation.rs::LedgerOperationFields::owner (:630) names treasury or mandate and leaves every other kind None. Requiring the fields is a contract and journal-chain change, so an ADR comes first. Refusing an unattributed fill is a tightening.
decisions.adr_title: A fill books under the cell that sent it, with the fill, order, intent and decision ids the cell journals on Decision::Filled; LedgerEvent schema 2 requires owner and attribution, and schema 1 events decode as legacy and are never rewritten
decisions.closure: Lane L1b claims the ADR number first. Decision::Filled gains intent_id and decision_id, with a journal chain-version bump; old entries decode with none and are never posted as schema 2. OutcomeRecord and PaperFill carry both ids, and desk_fabric.rs posts the fill under owner = SourceEvent.cell with the full Attribution. LedgerEvent schema 2 refuses a fill event without owner or attribution. The ADR states an owner for every LedgerOperation kind, using the treasury where no cell or mandate is a party, and none stays unowned in schema 2. ledgerd refuses a new schema-1 event. It decodes stored schema-1 events as legacy, byte for byte. Test: a posted PaperFill books under the cell that sent it with its fill, order, intent and decision ids, and a fill missing any of them is refused at posting. Mutations: drop intent_id from Decision::Filled; let schema 2 decode without an owner. Each must fail the test.
decisions.skeptic: This rests on misreads. (a) 'Decision::Filled gains the intent and decision ids the cell already holds': grep finds no intent_id or decision_id anywhere in qip-edge. qip_contracts::intent::Intent (intent.rs:134) and NetIntent (:464) carry no id. A NetIntent nets several Contributors (:365) from different strategies, so one fill rests on many intents. A single Attribution.intent_id would pick one, the 'whichever party is named first' guess that ledger_operation.rs:625-629 refuses. (b) 'desk_fabric.rs:104-105 is the one PaperFill::try_from plus post seam' is wrong. The ledger of record books every cell's fills in qip-ledgerd store.rs (:926 PaperFill::try_from, :1028 post). desk_fabric only pre-checks the kernel desk's own records, so stating the owner there changes nothing ledgerd books. (c) owner = SourceEvent.cell conflicts with LedgerEvent::with_owner's contract, 'whose capital this event moved: a desk or mandate id' (ledger.rs:574). Corrected: an ADR first. It mints an intent id and a decision id (for example the OrderSent journal position), or makes Attribution a per-contributor list matching the shares map. It puts the requirement at qip-ledgerd's posting seam and in PaperFill, and it decides owner semantics explicitly. Kept: schema 1 read as legacy, never rewritten; a new unattributed fill refused (a tightening); no strategy-to-mandate map.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0151 decision 2 stands on the producer and the consumer. The edge builds a pack per pass over the market events it applied, and never over none. The tick desk's fusion may only remove a flagged instrument's input weight, never raise one. The carrier changes: the pack rides in the per-pass FeatureDigest the edge already ships on reflex.feature_digested, not in a FeatureSnapshot that nothing builds, so one pass writes one P2 record. I do not switch the tick desk on (ADR 0151 decision 3). The row stays PARTIAL until the edge-to-centre link and the tick desk run in a deployment.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/market_state.rs::MarketStatePack (:39-70) refuses zero events (tests/market_state.rs::a_pack_over_no_events_is_refused_rather_than_reported_as_a_clean_tape), and grep finds it nowhere outside qip-contracts. qip-contracts feature.rs::FeatureSnapshot has no producer (only qip-contracts and acceptance tests name it). R12-FABRIC-10102's lane instead shipped qip-contracts replay.rs::FeatureDigest (:117), built by qip-edge-node src/event_fabric/writer.rs and bound to Topic::ReflexFeatureDigested at P2MarketJournal (qip-events event_fabric/bindings.rs:133). It is routed FabricPath::LocalJournal (message_routing.rs:103). qip-edge-node event_fabric/drain.rs holds the applied MarketEvents (:943). backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/fusion.rs is the named consumer, inert while QIP_DEEPBRAIN_TICK_EVERY is unset. Moving the carrier named in ADR 0151 d2 is a contract change, so an ADR comes first. This is consistent with the R12-TICK-2041 ruling, under which MarketStatePack follows ADR 0151 decision 2 under this row. Downgrade-only fusion is a tightening.
decisions.adr_title: MarketStatePack rides in the pass's FeatureDigest on reflex.feature_digested, not an unbuilt FeatureSnapshot, amending ADR 0151 decision 2's carrier; the tick desk's fusion stays its only consumer and may only remove a weight
decisions.closure: Lane L1b (FABRIC) claims the ADR number first. FeatureDigest gains an optional per-instrument MarketStatePack, built over the pass's applied MarketEvents with the pass interval as horizon. It is absent when none were applied and never an empty pack. qip-kernel fusion.rs removes the input weight of an instrument whose latest pack carries an integrity flag, and it never raises a weight. Tests: (1) qip-edge-node: a pass that applied events ships a pack over exactly those events, and a pass that applied none ships no pack. (2) qip-kernel fusion: an instrument whose pack is flagged contributes no weight to the fused state, and an unflagged one keeps its weight unchanged. Mutations: drop the pack from the digest; ignore the flag in fusion. The ADR names how the record reaches the deep brain. That delivery, over ADR 0112's link, and the tick desk switch stay STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. MarketStatePack is found nowhere outside qip-contracts. FeatureSnapshot is named only in qip-contracts and two acceptance tests. FeatureDigest (replay.rs:117) is built per pass and bound to ReflexFeatureDigested on P2MarketJournal (bindings.rs:133), routed LocalJournal. writer.rs's Handoff already carries `applied: Vec<MarketEvent>` (:128) beside `digest: Option<FeatureDigest>` (:131), so a per-pass pack over the applied events is buildable at the writer. Moving the carrier ADR 0151 d2 names needs an ADR. The ruling is consistent with R12-TICK-2041. The delivery link and the tick desk switch stay deploy-gated. Downgrade-only fusion is a tightening. Notes for the lane: fusion.rs has no 'weight' field, so removal means excluding the flagged instrument's trace from fuse(). ADR 0151 d2 says an empty interval is 'no tape', not clean, so fusion must not keep an instrument's input on a stale clean pack once its tape goes silent. TICK-2041's pin of fusion input to MarketTrace/TracePoint must allow this downgrade-only side input.

decisions.ruling: I accept ADR 0146 decision 9's amendment. A goal carries no authority class. Authority lives on the action policy and starts at Shadow, and a goal document naming authority_class is refused. That is the tighter reading, because a goal that can ask for authority can ask for a live rung. I do not add a Shadow-only authority_class to the goal: a second place where authority is stated is a second claim about one fact. The requirement reads 'authority class on the action policy'. The rollback half stays as built: carried and validated, and executed by nothing.
decisions.rationale: docs/adr/0146 decision 9 records the departure and amends the requirement text. Under bar part 4, it waited only on owner acceptance, which this ruling gives. backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/expansion.rs:7 says 'A goal carries no authority at all'. tests/expansion.rs::a_goal_carries_no_authority_and_a_document_asking_for_one_at_any_level_is_refused (:332) and ::a_goal_without_rollback_conditions_is_refused_and_a_declared_one_survives_decoding (:632) hold both halves. The row cites :447, which is stale. qip-agency src/ambient_intake.rs declares the ambient goal's rollback at :406; the row cites :378. Consistent with R12-MODEL-4014, which accepted ADR 0146 decision 2's narrowing the same way.
decisions.closure: Amend R12-CONTRACT-7080's statement in docs/blueprint/requirements/R12-M7.json from 'authority class' on the goal to 'authority class on the action policy (ADR 0146 d9, accepted 2026-10-31)'. Correct the stale citations: expansion.rs tests now at :332 and :632, ambient_intake.rs rollback at :406. Regrade the row on those two tests, whose mutations are already recorded. No code. The status moves only through the register's grader against bar part 2, not through this ruling.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. ADR 0146 decision 9 (:207-211) amends the requirement to 'authority class on the action policy'. expansion.rs:7 says 'A goal carries no authority at all'. The tests are at expansion.rs:332 and :632, so the row's :447 is stale. ambient_intake.rs declares rollback at :406, so the row's :378 is stale. Accepting an ADR that already narrowed the text, in the tighter direction (a goal cannot ask for authority), matches R12-MODEL-4014. It is not a widening restatement. No code changes, and the grade moves only through the register's grader.

decisions.ruling: A basket or an index carries its constituents and their weights. It is valued only from those constituents' prices. A position in it counts against its constituents' limits as well as its own, never instead of them. One with a missing weight, weights that do not sum to one, or an unpriced constituent is refused, not valued at a guess. A corporate action books in the ledger of record exactly once: a cash dividend as cash received against dividend income, a split or stock dividend as a unit change on the lot at unchanged cost. Under ADR 0153 decision 1 the operation itself is journaled, so the event log and the ledger hold one claim. It is all paper; no real dividend is paid or received.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-financial/src/extensions.rs::IndexDetails (:859) holds methodology, constituent_count, rebalance_frequency, divisor and is_total_return, with no weights. StructuredProductDetails (:878) holds underlying_object_ids and no weights. backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs::apply_corporate_action (:14097) credits cash for a dividend and journals LotAdjusted, but pushes nothing onto desk_operations (:1052). backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/ledger_operation.rs::OperationKind has no corporate-action variant. ADR 0153 decision 1 sets the rule for keeping the ledger and the log one claim: the producer journals the operation. A new OperationKind and a weighted instrument extension are contract changes, so an ADR comes first. Look-through only adds limit checks, and refusing unweighted baskets adds refusals.
decisions.adr_title: A basket or an index is valued and risked through its weighted constituents, and an applied corporate action books one LedgerOperation that the book's LotAdjusted record carries, under ADR 0153 decision 1
decisions.closure: Lane L6 (kernel/COVERAGE) claims the ADR number first. Add constituent weights to IndexDetails and StructuredProductDetails, refused when absent, non-positive, duplicated or not summing to one. Value from constituents, and count each constituent against its limits in addition to the direct position. Add a corporate-action OperationKind. Platform::apply_corporate_action pushes it onto desk_operations, and LotAdjusted carries it, deduplicated by the action key so a replay books nothing twice. Update the fixture of tests/asset_classes.rs::a_repo_an_index_and_a_basket_assemble_trade_on_paper_and_are_refused_without_their_class to state weights; no assertion is removed. Tests: (1) an index is valued from its weighted constituents and refused when a constituent is unpriced; mutation: drop one weight from the valuation. (2) A cash dividend and a split each book exactly one ledger operation, and a restart that replays LotAdjusted books neither again; mutation: skip the push in apply_corporate_action.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. IndexDetails is at :859 and StructuredProductDetails at :878, neither with weights. platform.rs::apply_corporate_action (:14097) credits dividend cash and journals LotAdjusted with no desk_operations push (field at :1052). The push sites are elsewhere (:8025, :24879 and others). OperationKind has no corporate-action variant. ADR 0153 d1 has the producer journal the whole operation. The existing actions_taken key (:14164) supports booking once on replay. A new OperationKind and weighted extensions are contract changes, so ADR first is right. Look-through limits and refusing unweighted baskets are tightenings. No committed universe instrument is an index or basket, so the new refusal breaks no deployed load.

decisions.ruling: Decision 6 of 2026-10-25 stands: no hosted language-model vendor yet, so no large-model candidate class is admitted to the foundry. A deterministic template is not a large model and is not registered as one to pass the row. A self-hosted large model needs Vertex GPU, which decision 5 declines. When a vendor is under contract with its credential and attestation, the candidate enters through the deep brain's language gateway and climbs the same promotion ladder as every other candidate. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/central/foundry.rs joins qip-evolution's generated strategies to the promotion ladder and has no large-model candidate class. backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/language.rs reaches a hosted provider only under QIP_LANGUAGE_MODEL_PROVIDER/QIP_LANGUAGE_MODEL plus HF_TOKEN, which no environment supplies. O05 in docs/blueprint/lanes/design-decisions-2026-10-18.json prices it as a provider credential and per-token spend, both third-party and paid. Consistent with R12-MODEL-1085, R12-REASON-1024 and R12-QUANT-9007, which hold the same vendor line.
decisions.closure: No code. Record O05 as declined on 2026-10-31 under decision 6 in the row's gap, with blocked_by 'decision 6 of 2026-10-25: no hosted model vendor'. The row reopens only after the owner contracts a vendor with a credential and an attestation. Then register a large-model candidate class in central/foundry.rs, fed through qip-deepbrain src/language.rs, on the same promotion ladder. Test: a hosted large-model candidate is registered with its trial count and climbs only through the ladder's gates. Mutation: let it skip a gate.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. central/foundry.rs has no language, large-model or hosted candidate class. qip-deepbrain language.rs and config.rs alone read QIP_LANGUAGE_MODEL_PROVIDER/HF_TOKEN. O05 (design-decisions :312) maps to this row. Decision 6 of 2026-10-25 names no vendor. A vendor credential is STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL. This is consistent with R12-MODEL-1085, R12-REASON-1024 and R12-QUANT-9007, and refusing to register a template as a large model avoids a restated pass.

decisions.ruling: Independent operation is proven on the binary's default path. Peer communication is shown on two deployed nodes or not at all. A second node and its stable fronting address are billed, ADR 0035 authorises one node, and decision 5 of 2026-10-25 keeps both unbought. The peer_mesh object is in the root and null in every environment. No monthly cost is named in the runbook or the row, so nothing is funded. The row reopens with an ADR amending ADR 0035 for a second node, stating its monthly ceiling, after dev's first node runs.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/tests/degraded.rs:260 a_cell_cut_off_from_everything_keeps_placing_paper_orders_inside_its_envelope_and_journals_that_it_is_degraded proves the independent half. The peer mesh starts only with QIP_PEER_MESH_LISTEN and QIP_PEER_MESH_PEERS. infrastructure/terraform/modules/execution-node/variables.tf::peer_mesh (:848) defaults null. infrastructure/terraform/main.tf:773 passes each.value.peer_mesh, from l5b-peer-mesh-root.patch, applied under decision 3 of 2026-10-31 with no node and no cost. docs/ops/runbooks/dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5 prices no second node. Consistent with R12-MESH-5042's ruling: the distributed half waits on a second node that decision 5 keeps unbought.
decisions.closure: No code. The gap opens with this ruling: the deployed half waits on a second execution node and its fronting address, both unpriced and declined under decision 5, and on ADR 0035's one-node authorisation. Trigger: an ADR amending ADR 0035 that states the monthly ceiling for a second node, after dev's first node is up. Then set peer_mesh on both nodes in protected tfvars and show two deployed nodes joining one epoch and exchanging over the mesh.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. degraded.rs:260 holds the independent-operation test. execution-node variables.tf::peer_mesh is at :848. main.tf:773 passes each.value.peer_mesh. Dev tfvars has peer_mesh = null (:269). l5b-peer-mesh-root.patch is listed under decision 3 (owner-decisions :58). Runbook §5 (:312) prices no second node. decisions.ruling: I do not name the jurisdictions this platform may execute in. That is a legal determination, not a product call, and the platform holds no licence anywhere. No committed universe instrument names a governing jurisdiction, so any set I stated would do one of two things: license by assertion, or shadow the whole paper desk. The gate stays proven and unstated on every binary. The row waits on a compliance determination, recorded as a committed record a root reads.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/action.rs::ExecutableScope::with_jurisdictions makes an instrument executable only when it names governing jurisdictions and all of them are licensed. backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/executable_scope.rs::Platform::executable_scope (:72-95) applies it only when Platform::license_jurisdictions (platform.rs:24173) has been called. Only tests/executable_scope.rs:275 calls it. data/datasets/universe.json carries no jurisdiction field on any instrument, so stating any set today would route every committed instrument to Shadow. The row's notes record why unset is ungated. The instruction puts a licence under STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL, and stating one by delegation would restate the requirement to pass it.
decisions.closure: No code now. The gap names the missing input: a compliance determination of the jurisdictions the platform may execute in, supplied by a qualified party and committed as a record. After that: each universe instrument states its governing jurisdictions. The qip-api, qip-fastbrain and qip-deepbrain roots read QIP_LICENSED_JURISDICTIONS and refuse a malformed value at start. Then a binary-path test shows an instrument in an unlicensed jurisdiction shadowed and never queued. Mutation: return the scope before with_jurisdictions.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. license_jurisdictions is at platform.rs:24173, and its only caller is tests/executable_scope.rs:275. executable_scope.rs:72-92 returns the ungated scope when no licence is stated. universe.json has no jurisdiction field, so any stated set shadows every instrument. A licence determination is external input, and the instruction maps a licence to STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL. Declining to assert one avoids licensing by assertion. No guard is loosened.

decisions.ruling: O16 is declined, as I ruled for R12-AGENCY-1183, 6094 and 7028. ADR 0114 D8 stands, and no outbound channel, publication route, survey or public adapter is opened, nor any account or credential for one. That includes a qip-api publication route the platform controls, because publishing to the outside world is an external action surface. ConductGate's seven checks govern drafts. A person sends what an agent drafts, under their own identity. This is a refusal of an external action surface, which no delegation lifts, and the row stays PARTIAL on its channel clause.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/services/qip-agency/tests/conduct_brain.rs:61-410 shows each ConductGate check blocking on its own, and qip-cli src/agency.rs runs it on the operator path. qip-agency src/autonomy.rs holds Authority::External as Grant::Refused { by: "ADR 0114 D8" }. The only production adapter is outbox.rs::DraftingAdapter (ADR 0114 Amendment 1). docs/adr/0114 D8 refuses external-action surfaces, and ADR 0003 refuses any live path. The standing limits forbid an external action surface under any delegation. Consistent with R12-AGENCY-1183, R12-AGENCY-6092, R12-AGENCY-6094 and R12-AGENCY-7028.
decisions.closure: No code. Record O16 as declined on 2026-10-31 in the row and in docs/blueprint/lanes/design-decisions-2026-10-18.json. Set blocked_by to 'refused by ADR 0114 D8'. The gap reads: ConductGate's seven checks and the infeasible deceptive step govern drafts, and the external channel is refused, not pending. Only an ADR the owner writes reopening ADR 0114 D8 revives it.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. autonomy.rs:175 holds Grant::Refused { by: "ADR 0114 D8" }, and qip-cli agency.rs uses conduct_brain. An outbound channel, including an owned publication route, is an external action surface that no delegation lifts. REFUSE_LIVE is required, and the ruling says so. Consistent with R12-AGENCY-1183, 6092, 6094 and 7028, and it correctly rejects the triage closure's 'qip-api publication route' idea.

decisions.ruling: The archive, artifact and simulation buckets stay off until the change that lands their first writer, because the archive's seven-year lock cannot be undone. That writer is a deployed fabricd broker with a Cloud Storage archive target, and decision 5 keeps it unbought until after the base deploy. The fabricd half of the gap is out of date and is corrected: fabricd already opens a CloudStorageBlobStore. The bucket bill is about $0.30 to $6 a month by the lanes' billed plan, not the runbook, so it is named but not funded here. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-fabricd/src/lib.rs::open_archive (:155) builds CloudStorageBlobStore for ArchiveTarget::CloudStorage (:166-181) beside FileBlobStore (:165), so the row's '(2)' is stale. infrastructure/environments/{dev,test,stage,prod}/terraform.tfvars set enable_cloud_storage = false (dev:364), and event_fabric_broker is null everywhere, so no deployment writes an archive. infrastructure/terraform/modules/data/main.tf::google_storage_bucket.archive (:161) is locked-retention CMEK; artifacts is at :263. docs/blueprint/lanes/billed-plan-2026-10-19.md §2 prices the switch at $0.30 to $6 a month and says to defer until a writer lands. Consistent with R12-DATA-8125 (storage stays off until the first writer), and with R12-FABRIC-8091 and 8092 (archive waits on the broker deploy).
decisions.closure: Correct the gap: fabricd's composition root already archives to Cloud Storage when given ArchiveTarget::CloudStorage. What remains is the buckets, enable_cloud_storage, protected and billed at about $0.30 to $6 a month, and a deployed broker. Trigger: after dev's base deploy, one protected change does two things. It sets event_fabric_broker with a CloudStorage archive target, its bucket and workload identity (R12-FABRIC-8091/8092). It flips enable_cloud_storage in dev. Then run a plan showing the archive, artifact and evidence buckets with their lifecycle and retention rules, and record a sealed segment archived to GCS.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. qip-fabricd lib.rs::open_archive (:155) builds FileBlobStore (:165) and CloudStorageBlobStore (:181), so the row's half (2) is stale. enable_cloud_storage = false in all four tfvars (dev:364), and event_fabric_broker is set in none. modules/data archive is at :161 and artifacts at :263. billed-plan :65 prices $0.30 to $6 a month with 'defer until a writer lands'. STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY with the cost named but not funded follows decision 5. It is consistent with R12-DATA-8125 (storage off until the first writer; the irreversible lock) and with R12-FABRIC-8091/8092. The fabricd archive target is the landing-or-copy path DATA-8125 left open, which this ruling does not contradict.

AlloyDB stays refused under ADR 0113 and decision 5: no Postgres wire client is admitted and no cluster is created, because workflow state lives on the journal and nothing has measured a need for a relational store. I do not narrow the row to the constructor, because that would pass it by restating it. The production callers (qip-deepbrain/src/connectors.rs:509, qip-fastbrain/src/node.rs:159, qip-api/src/routes.rs:2242 reference_fetch) all sit behind deepbrain_connector or market_data_connector, which is null in every tfvars (dev :521 commented out). The deep brain runs in cognition (catalogue.tf:548, 'Its zone may hold no external-egress entry at all'), and that guard is not loosened. The outward fetch path is ADR 0144's scout, ruled IMPLEMENT under R12-DATA-8112 and deployed only once its cost is named. R12-CONTRACT-7089 already rules that a row with nothing left to code waits on deployed evidence.
decisions.closure: Rewrite the gap: 'Library half met (Acquisition::of_admission and acquisition_manifest.rs). Open only on deployment: no committed environment runs a connector arm. The fetch path is ADR 0144's scout (R12-DATA-8112), placed where a reviewed information-source egress route exists; the cognition zone gets none.' Drop the NAT/decision 5 premise from the reason. decisions.ruling: A revision a re-fetch finds is recorded the moment it is found, not left for a poll that may never ask for that extent again. Historical reasoning re-fetches its window through the manifest before it fits, as the requirement says. The deployed half waits on a connector arm like R12-DATA-1033, and the row stays PARTIAL until then.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/connectors.rs::ConnectorArm::refetch (539-590) acts only on RevisionCheck::Unretrievable, through Platform::mark_unretrievable. A RevisionCheck::Revised { was, now } is returned and never recorded. The kernel flags a revision only in qip-kernel/src/references.rs::Platform::record_reference (LedgerOutcome::Revised at :396, which journals SourceRevisionDetected, runs flag_closed_campaigns and counts DATA_REVISIONS_DETECTED). A /latest-style poll never re-references a historical extent, so a revision can sit unflagged indefinitely. qip-deepbrain/src/campaign.rs::assemble references the window serialised from the engine's own bars (locator_for), which is the private copy the rationale warns about, and it never calls the ReFetchDriver. qip-data-finder/src/refetch.rs::ReFetchOutcome::Fetched carries only content_hash, so the recording needs a hash-level seam. Both changes add flags and refusals and loosen nothing, and refetch still asks the licence first. EvolutionEngine::maybe_refetch keeps its operator cadence (refetch_every defaults to 0, connectors.rs:212). The deployment half shares R12-DATA-1033's trigger: ADR 0144's scout under R12-DATA-8112.
decisions.closure: (1) Add one kernel seam that records a re-fetched revision through record_reference's own revision branch, shared and not copied: SourceRevisionDetected journaled, closed campaigns flagged, metric counted. Call it from ConnectorArm::refetch for every Revised finding. Test 'a re-fetch that finds a revised extent leaves a SourceRevisionDetected on the log and flags the closed campaign that read it in the same pass, with no further poll'. Mutation: drop the call for Revised, and the assertion fails. (2) In the learning path, before campaign::assemble fits a Door::Admitted (not replayed) connector window, run that source's arm refetch over the held references the window covers, within REFETCH_BUDGET, and carry any Revised or Unretrievable finding onto the campaign manifest entry. Test 'a learning round over a connector-door window re-fetches its extents through the manifest locator before the fit, and a revised extent flags the campaign's manifest entry'. Mutation: skip the re-fetch, and the flag is absent. Correct the gap's decision 5/NAT premise as in R12-DATA-1033. The row stays PARTIAL until a deployed arm exists.
decisions.skeptic: Part (1) is sound. ConnectorArm::refetch (connectors.rs:539-590) acts only on RevisionCheck::Unretrievable, and record_reference's revision branch (references.rs:396) is the only place a revision is flagged. Recording Revised findings through a shared seam adds a flag and loosens nothing. Part (2) rests on a misread. The learning path calls campaign::assemble (evolution.rs:734/1032) on self.adapter. main.rs:508-612 builds only three own streams: a tape (tape.rs:795, Replayed), a ReplayAdapter (Replayed) or the synthetic exchange (Generated). So Door::Admitted { replayed: false } is never reached from the binary. The window's reference is a bars:// locator serialised from the engine's own bars (campaign.rs:223), and no transport can re-fetch it. ConnectorArm::refetch filters to Discovered and CatalogueAdmitted references, so a replayed window's extents are never among the arm's held references. The proposed test would run only on a configuration main.rs never builds. It would also send vendor requests while QIP_DEEPBRAIN_REFETCH_EVERY is unset or 0, which is documented to disable the re-fetch pass (connectors.rs:200-213). Corrected closure: build part (1) only, with its test and mutation as written. Drop part (2). Historical reasoning that re-fetches through a manifest needs a connector-backed historical window, which waits on a deployed arm or scout (R12-DATA-8112) and a licensed historical API. The row stays PARTIAL.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0157 decision 5 stands, and I do not supersede it: candidates are written by an operator or not at all. A stage that manufactures candidates nobody reviewed a route for is a control assessing its own inputs, and whether crawling a publisher is lawful is a reading of that publisher's terms and robots policy that nobody has made. The requirement text stands and is not restated to the operator list, so the row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/discovery.rs (module doc :19-26) builds no CRAWL stage. DiscoveryDesk only orders operator CandidateEntry items, and qip-data-finder/src/discovery_targets.rs::locations_for returns only catalogued candidates for a DiscoveryQuery. ADR 0157 decision 5 refuses crawl and search because a candidate must name a reviewed egress_route (ADR 0060). Its 'Not decided here' leaves the legality of crawling a publisher to the owner's reading of terms. Superseding decision 5 would remove a standing refusal, which loosens a guard. A search API is a vendor under ADR 0157's BILLED clause. This is consistent with R12-DATA-2006 ('Both need someone to read the terms, and none is invented here') and R12-TICK-2046 ('No agent accepts a venue's terms in my name'). A proposal file ADR 0157 d5 allows is never loaded by load_source_candidates, so it does not meet 'without a human adding them'.
decisions.closure: Write into the gap: 'ADR 0157 d5 stands (2026-10-31); the triage's supersession proposal is refused. No crawl or search stage exists.' The row reopens only through an ADR written after one of two things: a terms-and-robots reading of each publisher a crawler would touch, or a search vendor contracted under an ADR 0157 record, in either case with a reviewed egress route per host. Then build a generator whose output passes the same record, route and registration gates. Test it with 'a discovery pass with an empty operator list yields generated candidates, and each is refused until it holds a record and a route'.
decisions.skeptic: discovery.rs:19-27 states that no CRAWL stage is built. locations_for (discovery_targets.rs:271) filters the catalogue it is given. ADR 0157 decision 5 refuses crawl and search, says a proposal file 'is never loaded by load_source_candidates', and leaves crawl legality to a reading of each publisher's terms. Superseding decision 5 would lift a standing refusal. Refusing to supersede it is the conservative reading. The ruling also declines ADR 0157's 'Register: restate' hint and keeps the requirement text, so the row does not pass by restatement. The closure keeps the gates and is consistent with R12-DATA-2006 and R12-TICK-2046.

decisions.rationale: backend/crates/services/qip-market-ingestion/src/connector_feed.rs::KNOWN_SOURCES (:51-59) covers exchange ticker and trades (coinbase), quotes (kalshi), bars (alpaca) and rates (ECB, NY Fed, frankfurter). Options have four quoted refusals in qip-data-finder/src/admission.rs::refusals(), and each RefusedSource must carry terms_url, terms_dated and the clause verbatim. Funding, borrow and venue status have neither a record nor a refusal. qip-market-ingestion depth.rs DepthFeedAdapter is constructed only in qip-cli demo/mod.rs:121. decisions.closure: A lane may add a qip-acceptance inspection now as a shrink-only ratchet. decisions.skeptic: The outcome (no vendor, no invented refusal, PARTIAL) is right, but the coverage claims misread the code. coinbase_ticker.rs:14-28 says it emits a Tick and explicitly 'does not produce a trade' or a Quote: trades lack a TradeCondition and quotes lack sizes. So coinbase covers exchange feeds, not trades. KNOWN_SOURCES lists Kalshi and Alpaca, but its own comment (connector_feed.rs:46-48) says 'Being named here is not being admitted'. admission.rs:383-400 gives both an ambiguous posture, so admit refuses them, and neither has a RefusedSource. Quotes therefore have neither an admitted connector nor a documented refusal. The closure's ratchet treats 'a KNOWN_SOURCES entry' as coverage. That is weaker than the requirement's 'admitted connector' and would pass trades and quotes by decree. Corrected closure: the shrink-only inspection maps each §6.1 class to a source that admission::admit admits (a catalogue() entry admit passes) or a refusals() RefusedSource. Covered today: exchange feeds (coinbase-spot-ticker), options surfaces (the four quoted refusals, admission.rs:565+) and rates (ECB, NY Fed, frankfurter). Uncovered: order books, trades, quotes, funding, borrow and venue status. Each closes on an ADR 0157 record with its connector, manifest, KNOWN_SOURCES entry and route, or on a quoted RefusedSource. Note: demo/mod.rs:121 is the import line; the constructor is at :813.

decisions.ruling: No news, press, expert, public-web, deep-web database, social or community source is admitted, and no refusal is written without a clause read. A deep-web database needs a Licensed declaration or an enclave, and none exists. ADR 0157 decision 7 fixes the rule for social and community sources (surface web only, author identifiers dropped, text untrusted) but admits none, and it lists news and social vendors as BILLED. decisions.skeptic: NarrativeAdapter is constructed only in qip-cli demo/mod.rs:808 and in tests. KNOWN_SOURCES (connector_feed.rs:51-59) holds no news, social or community source. decisions.closure: Keep the status PARTIAL. Write into the gap: 'No commerce vendor (2026-10-31); ADR 0157 d6 is a deferral; the class is not refused by preference.' decisions.closure: Make the journal search in data_infrastructure_guards.rs byte-aware. decisions.skeptic: Verified. envelope.rs:98-101 has RawPayload { sha256, bytes: Option<Vec<u8>> }. The test should assert as a premise that the served fixture is under that cap, or the mutation would write None and survive. (2) R12-WORLD-3045 says only that the connector comes on at the deploy. decisions.decision: ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT: same ADR. fabricd writes each sealed segment to the regional landing, then writes the same local sealed bytes a second time into the locked archive under one content address. There is no server-side copy from the landing and no transfer service. A segment counts as archived only after an objects.get of the archive object returns the expected hash. archive_target refuses a landing bucket given with no archive target. The delete-based start-up probe is replaced by one that never deletes: probe the landing, whose 30-day rule expires the object, and prove the archive by reading the object back after its first write. In Terraform, fabric.tf passes segment_bucket and archive_bucket (count stays 0) and grants fabricd roles/storage.objectCreator plus roles/storage.objectViewer on both buckets, never objectAdmin or delete. Update segment_bucket's output description and cite zone-model.tftest.hcl:564 for PGA. Test against a Cloud Storage double that refuses deletes within retention: a sealed segment ends up in both buckets under one address, the broker starts against retention buckets, and a broker with a landing bucket but no archive refuses to start. Mutations: skip the archive write, accept a landing with no archive, or mark a segment archived without the read-back; each fails the test. The row stays PARTIAL on enable_cloud_storage ($0.30-$6 a month) and event_fabric_broker (unpriced).

decisions.skeptic: The ADR route is right and matches R12-DATA-8125's decision. The closure, though, misreads fabricd and cannot run as written. (1) It grants fabricd 'objectCreator only on both buckets'. But qip-fabricd src/lib.rs:138-149 prove_archive_writable (called at :695) puts, gets and deletes a probe object at start-up, and the closure's own read-back of the archive hash needs storage.objects.get. roles/storage.objectCreator grants neither get nor delete, so a deployed broker would refuse to start and no segment would ever count as archived. (2) Both buckets carry retention: segments has an unlocked 7-day hold and the archive a locked 2557-day one. GCS refuses the probe's delete whatever the IAM. The closure ignores this, and an in-process double that does not model retention will not catch it. (3) 'Copies it server-side' takes the archive object from the landing bucket. R12-DATA-8125's ruling says the archive receives each segment 'from fabricd's own archive path, never from a landing bucket', and its decision names 'fabricd's own second write'. (4) The PGA tftest already exists: trust-zones/tests/zone-model.tftest.hcl:564 asserts private_ip_google_access on every zone subnet, including control-fabric (fabric.tf:123). Cite it instead of adding a duplicate. The other citations verify: config.rs:43-46 documents the landing and archive_target is at :418, outputs.tf:23 has the warning, segments expire at 30 days, there is no google_storage_transfer_job, and fabric.tf:23 has count 0.

The only test of that seam is kernel tests/evidence_intake.rs::the_world_record_seam_releases_only_what_the_fabric_stood_behind, which runs at the seam. The deep brain is trust_zone 'cognition' (infrastructure/terraform/catalogue.tf:548) with egress ALL_TRAFFIC (infrastructure/gitops/envs/dev/deepbrain.yaml:34). cognition has no entry in modules/trust-zones/main.tf::sanctioned_egress_purposes (:141), and catalogue.tf:543 says the zone 'may hold no external-egress entry at all'. decisions.closure: Add qip-deepbrain tests/world_fabric_arms.rs. Build two ConnectorArm::over_transport arms over qip-market-ingestion connector/emulator.rs transports and poll them into one Platform; one arm forwards a claim forged against the other's provenance. Test: 'a forged claim one connector arm forwards is withheld from observation, its finding is recorded on the arm, and the honest arm's record is released' (assert ConnectorArm::last_withheld and the intake finding). Mutation: in ConnectorArm::poll, hand up the identified records without Platform::admit_world_records, and the test fails. The row stays PARTIAL until all three happen: an ADR opens a cognition-zone information-source route with its added monthly NAT cost named, the owner sets deepbrain_connector in dev tfvars (protected), and a deployed deep brain records one withheld claim.
decisions.skeptic: The closure cannot be built as written. The world seam withholds a record only when the claim is inadmissible or spoofed (evidence_intake.rs:406-408). admissible depends only on the record's own timeline checks, ViolatesPhysicalTimeline and PostdatesSource (fabric.rs:836-839). The connector runtime already quarantines on those same two conditions before records are identified (runtime.rs:1027-1052). So an honest arm's ConnectorArm::last_withheld cannot rise, and the fast brain's test asserts withheld == 0 for that reason (registrations.rs:605). A 'forged claim withheld on last_withheld' never reaches admit_world_records as an identified record, so the bypass mutation cannot bite. The rationale is also wrong that 'No qip-deepbrain test builds a ConnectorArm; over_transport has no caller outside src'. evolution.rs builds arms in its unit tests (coinbase_arm :3796, nws_arm, frankfurter_arm :4225), and a_connector_poll_forwards_its_checked_evidence_into_the_world_fabric (:4728) polls into a Platform. qip-acceptance data_infrastructure_guards.rs:566 also calls ConnectorArm::over_transport. Corrected closure: a binary-path test that shows what the arm path really does. First, two arms polled into one Platform leave each claim linked claim, document, source in the world provenance graph, with the cross-arm link recorded on both claims. Second, a body on an impossible timeline is not handed up, and its forwarded evidence is held inadmissible with weight 0. Mutation: bypass admit_world_records, or stop forwarding refused_evidence, and the graph and held assertions fail. The release-gate proof stays at the kernel seam (evidence_intake.rs:736). The deployment half (cognition egress ADR naming the NAT cost, owner sets deepbrain_connector) and PARTIAL stand.

Test: 'two connector arms disagreeing on one print leave the contested claim withheld on ConnectorArm::last_withheld and the contest held in the world fabric'. decisions.skeptic: This rests on a misread. A contested claim is not withheld. absorb_evidence withholds only when !verdict.admissible or the claim is spoofed (evidence_intake.rs:406-408), and a contest is only counted as 'contested' (:412-416). admissible ignores contradictions (fabric.rs:836-839). In the kernel test the two disagreeing claims both count as admitted == 2 with contested == 1 (tests/evidence_intake.rs:91-117). So the test 'leave the contested claim withheld on ConnectorArm::last_withheld' fails on unmutated code. The mutation 'bypass admit_world_records and the contested record is released' changes nothing, because it is already released. The rationale's 'No deep-brain test drives ConnectorArm::poll' is also false (evolution.rs:4728, :4255). Corrected closure: two arms state different values for one subject at one instant. Assert that the arm's last_evidence().contested == 1, that both held claims carry the Contradicts link, and that both records are handed up, because a contest is recorded, not withheld. Mutation: bypass admit_world_records, and contested is 0. Withholding contested claims would be a new refusal and would need its own ADR. The deployment trigger and PARTIAL stand.

No qip-deepbrain test drives it through ConnectorArm::poll. deepbrain_connector is null in dev tfvars (:521), and the cognition zone has no egress purpose (trust-zones/main.tf:141). A test only tightens.
decisions.closure: In qip-deepbrain tests/world_fabric_arms.rs, poll an arm whose emulator declares a Content-Digest that does not match its body. Test: 'a connector body whose declared digest does not match is marked spoofed in the world fabric and its record is not handed up by ConnectorArm::poll'. decisions.skeptic: Verified, and this is the one closure in the group the arm path can actually produce. evidence.rs:322 takes declared_digest, and :367 attaches HashVerified{declared} only when !digest.matched. The runtime quarantines a spoofed claim (runtime.rs:1032-1052) and still forwards its evidence, because connector_feed.rs:589 chains refused_evidence into the drain. The world fabric marks a mismatching sha256 as spoofed (fabric.rs:233-260). fabric.rs:314 refuses SignatureVerified, and emulator.rs:114 with_content_digest exists. So 'marked spoofed in the world fabric and not handed up by ConnectorArm::poll' holds. Dropping the comparison removes the signal, and the record is then handed up, so the mutation bites. The only existing test is at feed or kernel level (kernel tests/evidence_intake.rs a_body_that_is_not_what_its_source_declared_is_quarantined_and_found_spoofed), with none through ConnectorArm. Signatures stay with R12-EVID-2034 and ADR 0139, egress stays closed under decision 5, and the cost correction is accurate: main.tf:165 github_egress, and runbook section 5 puts NAT inside $400-$490. Test-only change.

decisions.skeptic: This rests on a misread. A geographic inconsistency does not withhold anything. admissible looks only at the temporal checks (fabric.rs:836-839), and absorb_evidence withholds only inadmissible or spoofed claims (evidence_intake.rs:406). So 'marked geographically inconsistent and withheld by ConnectorArm::poll' fails on unmutated code. The mutation 'skip check_geographic_consistency and the claim is released' changes nothing, because it is released either way. The test sentence also contradicts its own setup. A second arm is a different source, which yields ContradicsLocation, while 'its own source's earlier claim' yields InternalGeographicConflict (evidence.rs:358-365). Both require the same subject and a claim instant within GEO_SAME_PLACE_KM rules. The stale-gap correction is right: published_location is at nws_station_observations.rs:601, and fabric.rs:832-833 runs both checks. Corrected closure: poll an NWS emulator arm and a second arm that places the same station elsewhere at the same instant. Assert that the held record's geographic_consistency is ContradicsLocation and that the disagreement is recorded. Mutation: skip check_geographic_consistency, and the verdict reads Unverifiable. If withholding is wanted, that is a new refusal and needs its own ADR. The deployment trigger (cognition route ADR with NAT cost, NWS envoy listener, owner sets tfvars) and PARTIAL stand.

decisions.ruling: Copies of one origin count once on every path that weighs evidence, not only in the fabric. The reasoning engine's update folds each origin's items into one before applying them, because its sqrt(distinct/items) discount still lets n copies move a belief sqrt(n) times as far as one. The fabric's cap of two corroborating origins is an existing limit and I do not raise it by delegation. The row stays PARTIAL on 'a new origin raises it' past the second origin; that clause is not read down.
decisions.rationale: qip-evidence src/fabric.rs::EvidenceFabric::admit credits authenticity once per independent origin, capped at MAX_CORROBORATING_ORIGINS = 2 (:76, :895-900) and clamped at 1.0. A third origin therefore raises nothing, so a true property sweep of the requirement fails. qip-reasoning-engine src/bayes.rs::update applies discount sqrt(distinct/items) to every item: n same-origin items contribute sqrt(n) times one item's log-odds, which is a per-copy increment. That path runs on the default kernel REASON stage through Platform's self.reasoning.reason (platform.rs:19155) and hypothesis.rs's use of update. No crate depends on proptest, and the existing tests are examples (qip-world-model tests/evidence_fabric.rs:97, :719). Changing the update changes a documented design and the REASON outputs on replay, so it needs a record first. Folding copies removes inflation from the correlated-evidence guard. A posterior can rise in one case only: when another origin's copies had been diluting an independent item, which the requirement forbids. Platform::sizing_confidence (platform.rs:18050) reads marks and the counterfactual multiplier and no reasoning posterior. The cap is kept, so this tightens.
decisions.adr_title: Copies of one origin count once wherever evidence is weighed: the reasoning engine's update folds each origin's items into one before applying them, and the fabric's two-origin corroboration cap stands
decisions.closure: Claim the ADR in docs/adr/README.md. It states how an origin's items combine (copies of one weight give that weight) and lists every reader of Hypothesis::effective_confidence with the direction each moves. Then in qip-reasoning-engine bayes.rs::update, fold each origin's EvidenceStrength items into one, drop the sqrt(distinct/items) discount, and keep MAX_LLR_PER_ITEM. Add seeded, bounded property sweeps with no new crate (ADR 0109). In qip-reasoning-engine tests: 'for 1..=N copies of one origin the posterior is identical, and a supporting item from a new origin moves it further from the prior'. In qip-world-model tests/evidence_fabric.rs: 'for 1..=N copies of one origin belief_weight and authenticity are identical, and each new independent origin up to MAX_CORROBORATING_ORIGINS strictly raises them'. Mutations: restore the sqrt discount, and the posterior grows with copies; credit others.len() in EvidenceFabric::admit, and the weight grows with copies. The row stays PARTIAL on the third-origin clause, and on its deployment clause until a connector feeds the fabric.
decisions.skeptic: The facts check out. MAX_CORROBORATING_ORIGINS = 2 is at fabric.rs:76 and :896. bayes.rs:119/:134 applies sqrt(distinct/items), with MAX_LLR_PER_ITEM at :109. hypothesis.rs calls update at :413 and :448. platform.rs:19155 calls reason. No crate depends on proptest. Keeping the cap and leaving the third-origin clause PARTIAL is right. The problem is the claim that tightens_only is true. The ruling admits a posterior can rise (an independent item no longer diluted by another origin's copies). It then judges that rise safe only because Platform::sizing_confidence (:18050) reads no posterior. But the red-team approval gate does read it. redteam.rs:568 takes effective_confidence, and :605 rejects below minimum_surviving_confidence. platform.rs:16537 then forms a proposal only for an is_actionable status. The tournament's detector vote also reads it (model_tournament.rs:812). So the change can flip a Rejected hypothesis to Approved, which loosens a guard on the decision path. Corrected ruling: same ADR, tighten-only. Fold each origin's items into one. Then never let a posterior move further from the prior than today's update would; take whichever of the folded and the current log-odds is nearer the prior. Single-origin copies stay invariant (min(x, sqrt(n)x) = x), and a new supporting origin still moves the posterior away from the prior, so the ruling's own sweeps still pass. The ADR's reader list must name the red-team approval gate and the tournament vote. The row stays PARTIAL on the third-origin clause, on mixed-origin dilution, and on deployment.

decisions.ruling: Requote layering is refused at the cell and at the desk, beside the cancel-before-fill gate and never in its place. Its bound is that gate's own: within 60 seconds, at least four requotes on one side of one book moved the order away from the touch and ended withdrawn unfilled, and they are more than three quarters of that side's requotes, while the same instrument filled on the opposite side at any venue. Momentum ignition is manipulation, not spoofing; it is graded under R12-RISK-4103's market-conduct domain, not dropped.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0155 section 13 defines the measure (away from the touch, withdrawn unfilled, against an opposite-side fill) and leaves the window, minimum and ratio as RISK under 'Not decided here'. Reusing qip-execution-engine src/conduct.rs::ConductPolicy::default (:94: 60 s, 4, 0.75) means no new number has to be argued (decision 7 of 2026-10-25). Two parts of the gap are stale. The desk path holds a ConductWatch (src/oms.rs:443, check at :822). qip-edge src/cell.rs::Cell::record_replacement counts every unfilled requote as a withdrawal and a placement since R12-GOV-6126, and Cell::replacement_conduct refuses under GATE_CONDUCT_SPOOFING (:222). conduct.rs's module doc (:22-23) still says requotes are not counted. That coarse count misses a layerer whose filled orders on the same side keep its cancel ratio at or under 0.75; the opposite-side-fill measure catches it. A per-venue key alone also misses layering on one venue against fills on another, so an opposite-side fill at any venue counts. This only adds a refusal and changes no existing value.
decisions.adr_title: Requote layering is refused beside the cancel-before-fill gate, at the cell and the desk, under that gate's own 60-second, four-withdrawal, three-quarters bound, with an opposite-side fill at any venue of the instrument counted

decisions.skeptic: Verified. conduct.rs now lives in qip-execution-engine (the qip-edge path in the row is stale). ConductPolicy::default at :94 is 60 s, 4 and 0.75. The module doc at :22-23 still says requotes are not counted. oms.rs:443 holds a ConductWatch, and the check runs at :827-830 (the ruling says :822, a minor drift). cell.rs:12078 record_replacement counts every unfilled requote as cancelled_unfilled plus placed (R12-GOV-6126). replacement_conduct (:6771) refuses under GATE_CONDUCT_SPOOFING (:222). A new ADR that amends it by a new record, with no edit to 0155, is the right form. The change only adds a refusal. It reuses existing values and leaves the current count unchanged, and counting an opposite-side fill at any venue only broadens what is caught. The test and its mutation are concrete. The measured residual we do have is the federation's: a subject on which its probability keeps resolving the wrong way against licensed readings. That spawns one branch, admitted as ADR 0149's temporary entrant and scored against its parent. It expires on its own date and sizes nothing.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/services/qip-world-model/src/spawning.rs::WorldModelSpawner has no caller outside spawning.rs, lib.rs:98 and its tests. ADR 0149 decision 12 forbids a caller until a measured residual exists, and it names P&L. The kernel's attribution residual is zero-or-refused by construction (central/plane.rs). The one priced residual the deep brain computes is qip-expansion src/detectors.rs::unexplained_residuals_priced over trade_error_bps (qip-deepbrain research.rs:1921). That is the twin against the simulated venue, which R12-MODEL-4004 refuses as a learning source. The residual that does exist is the federation's resolution against licensed readings, which R12-EXPAND-6067 tracks as a persistent discrepancy. So the ADR names that residual and amends only d12's P&L clause. Admission keeps d12's triple and services/qip-learning-engine/src/tournament.rs::MAX_FORECASTERS / ForecasterKind::Temporary, as R12-MODEL-3089 requires. Scoring follows R12-MODEL-6022: out of sample, and it gates nothing.
decisions.closure: Write the ADR first. After R12-EXPAND-6067's discrepancy PersistenceTracker lands in qip-deepbrain research.rs, pass each persistent subject's measured residual to WorldModelSpawner::should_spawn and propose_branch, with the federation as parent. The residual is the subject's excess Brier loss over the window, as a Decimal; its threshold comes from a committed measurement named in the ADR, not from a default. Register the branch with register_branch. Admit it as ForecasterKind::Temporary with id branch:<branch id>/<family>, under MAX_FORECASTERS and its own expiry. Journal its Brier score against its parent's on questions resolved after the spawn. Resolutions from the synthetic venue never count (ADR 0151 d10). Test: 'a subject the federation keeps missing spawns one branch that is scored against its parent, and a subject it resolves correctly spawns none'. Mutations: bypass should_spawn and the second half fails; delete the propose_branch call and the first half fails.
decisions.adr_title: A world-model branch is spawned only from the federation's measured forecast residual on a licensed subject, enters as ADR 0149's temporary entrant triple, is scored against its parent and gates nothing (amends ADR 0149 decision 12's residual clause)
decisions.skeptic: The ruling misreads the code. Its rationale says 'WorldModelSpawner has no caller outside spawning.rs, lib.rs:98 and its tests'. That is false. qip-kernel src/model_tournament.rs:86 imports it, and observe_outcome (:690, called from the LEARN resolution loop at :1257) calls WorldModelSpawner::new(SPAWN_RESIDUAL=0.6).propose_branch(STANDING_POPULATION, residual, ..). The residual is the probability the tournament aggregate left on the outcome that did not happen. It admits a Laplace outcome-frequency temporary for 14 days with id 'temporary:<subject>' and records the branch on TournamentReview.spawned. This landed under R12-MODEL-7198 (commits 1b8073ea and 161836ab, 2026-10-31) and runs from run_cycle in qip-fastbrain and qip-deepbrain. So the row's 'no caller' gap is stale. The ruling's closure would add a second spawn caller on a different residual: the federation discrepancy via 6067's PersistenceTracker, with a different id form. Meanwhile the built caller already departs from ADR 0149 d12 on three points: a forecast residual instead of P&L, the 'temporary:' id instead of 'branch:<branch id>/<family>', and a frequency model instead of a lattice ModelFamily member. No ADR ratifies those departures. Corrected: one ADR amends ADR 0149 d12. It either ratifies the tournament aggregate's measured residual as the only spawn trigger and brings the entrant to d12's triple, or orders that caller removed. Either way, no second spawner caller is added. Then build the benchmark the row lacks: journal each spawned branch's out-of-sample Brier against its parent's aggregate on questions resolved after the spawn, gating nothing (R12-MODEL-6022). Synthetic-venue resolutions never count (ADR 0151 d10). Test: 'a spawned branch's Brier is journaled beside its parent's on later resolutions and moves nothing'. Mutation: score the branch with the parent's forecast. Status stays PARTIAL.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0149 decision 6 already decided this, and I keep it. A promoted result's lane is read from its compiled form, and no latency-budget field is added. A result that compiles inside the reflex bounds is reflex-eligible and stays unsigned until the two-person publish signs it (R12-REASON-7203). Anything else stays research. WarmService is not built because nothing would occupy it, so the row stays PARTIAL on that lane.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0149 decision 6 says the lane is 'derived from its compiled form; no latency-budget field is added'. Its 'Rows unblocked' line for 6052 reads 'lane derived from compiled cost; no budget field; WarmService not built; publication still waits on the signer'. The gap and the triage closure ask for the budget field that decision refuses, so their text is older than the record. The code shortfall is real: apps/qip-deepbrain/src/research.rs::ResearchLoop::distil (:3845) compiles every promoted fill-bias correction through self.compiler.compile. On a refusal it only counts packages{outcome=refused}, and no lane record exists for either outcome. So 'the step's record is produced and its absence refused' is not met. The bounds are qip-contracts src/reflex_package.rs::MAX_RULES, MAX_CONDITIONS and MAX_ADJUSTMENT_BPS (500). Signing is R12-REASON-7203.
decisions.closure: In ResearchLoop::distil, record a PromotionLane for every promoted question on ResearchRound. The lane is Reflex when compile accepts the discovery inside MAX_RULES, MAX_CONDITIONS and MAX_ADJUSTMENT_BPS, and Research when it refuses. Only a Reflex record may carry a CompiledReflex. A promoted capability that reaches the round's close with no lane record fails the sweep. Add no budget field and no WarmService variant (ADR 0149 d6; d17 covers the added field). Test: 'a promoted correction inside the reflex bounds is recorded reflex and held unsigned, and one past MAX_ADJUSTMENT_BPS is recorded research and yields no package'. Mutation: record Reflex on the compile-refused arm and the test fails. Rewrite the gap to cite ADR 0149 d6. Status stays PARTIAL on WarmService.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. ADR 0149 d6 says the lane is 'derived from its compiled form; no latency-budget field is added' and that WarmService is not built. Its Rows-unblocked line for 6052 matches the ruling. research.rs:3845 ResearchLoop::distil calls self.compiler.compile (:3916). The refuse arm only counts packages 'refused' (:3919-3920), and no lane record exists anywhere (grep finds no PromotionLane or WarmService). MAX_RULES=16, MAX_CONDITIONS=4 and MAX_ADJUSTMENT_BPS=500 are in qip-contracts reflex_package.rs:41-43, and the contract refuses an over-bound total (:168). Holding the package unsigned matches R12-REASON-7203. The new lane record is a refusal, so it tightens. WarmService keeps the row PARTIAL, so the requirement is not read away.

decisions.ruling: The requirement stands, and the three missing kinds are recorded, not dropped. Open questions are the registry's Open entries. A benchmark is the one ADR 0192 already names for the capability's class, cited as a typed reference and never as free text. A contradiction the detectors raise is kept under its campaign id until a campaign on that question concludes, so no variable-to-subject map is invented.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-agents/src/research.rs::Verdict::Open and ResearchRegistry::record already hold open hypotheses. ResearchRegistry::record_concluded keys by campaign_id and holds experiment refs (ADR 0152 d11). ADR 0152 d11 refused two things: a free-text benchmark_suite, and a contradictions list that would need ADR 0151's variable-to-subject map. Since then, ADR 0192 (accepted 2026-10-31) names each class's benchmark and incumbent; for fill-bias that is Criterion::IncrementalValue against the uncorrected twin. qip-expansion src/detectors.rs::contradictions and theory_contradictions already raise GapTrigger::Contradiction on the deep brain's sweep (qip-deepbrain research.rs:1879, :2085), and their questions carry campaign ids, so keying by campaign id needs no map. The registry is already consulted on a running path at admission: qip-expansion desk.rs Bounds { research: &self.research }.
decisions.closure: Write the ADR first. Then, in qip-agents research.rs: add open_questions() over the Open entries. Give every concluded Supported or Null entry a typed BenchmarkRef (class, incumbent, criterion, per ADR 0192's table), and refuse an entry without one. Add record_contradiction(campaign id, evidence refs), refusing empty evidence; only record_concluded on the same campaign id resolves it; unresolved_contradictions() lists the open ones. In qip-expansion desk.rs, record a contradiction when a GapTrigger::Contradiction item is admitted, and pass the benchmark from the evaluation's criterion on conclude. Tests: expansion_registries 'an entry missing a declared field is refused' and 'a contradiction stays unresolved until a campaign on the same id concludes'; executor 'a contradiction observation on a sweep opens one registry contradiction'. Mutations: accept a Supported verdict with no benchmark; let record_concluded skip the resolution. Each must fail its test.
decisions.adr_title: The research registry declares six record kinds: open questions are its Open entries, a concluded verdict cites its class's ADR 0192 benchmark, and an unresolved contradiction is a record keyed by campaign id that only a concluded campaign closes, with no variable-to-subject map (amends ADR 0152 decision 11)
decisions.skeptic: Verified. qip-agents research.rs has Verdict::Open (:21), ResearchRegistry::record (:105) and record_concluded (:119). ADR 0152 d11 declines only a free-text benchmark_suite and a contradictions list that would need ADR 0151's variable-to-subject map. ADR 0192 is accepted 2026-10-31, and its table names fill-bias -> uncorrected twin -> Criterion::IncrementalValue. detectors.rs contradictions (:521) and theory_contradictions (:689) raise GapTrigger::Contradiction. The deep brain's sweep reaches them at research.rs:1879 and :2085. desk.rs:379-383 passes Bounds { research: &self.research }. Keying contradictions by campaign id avoids the map, so ADR 0151 is respected. The new fields are refusals, so this tightens. It is an ADR amending 0152 d11, which matches the delegation. It contradicts no ruling.

decisions.ruling: The in-tree half stands. RF3 is admitted only for P0 and P1 acknowledged through the managed log, and a killed leader loses nothing on the in-memory log. RF3 across zones counts only when a deployed fabricd acknowledges through a regional Spanner commit. Decision 5 keeps that bill unbought at $2,705 to $8,140 a month, and the cross-region mirrors wait on a second region (ADR 0119, ADR 0035). The row stays PARTIAL. When the bill is taken, the emulator proof comes first (R12-FABRIC-9118).
decisions.rationale: qip-events src/event_fabric/policy.rs::StreamPolicy::new (:419-449) admits RF3 only for P0/P1 managed_majority. qip-fabricd tests/managed.rs::a_killed_leader_is_replaced_by_its_follower_with_no_acknowledged_record_lost (:305) runs on MemoryManagedLog, not Spanner. enable_spanner = false in the dev (:368), test, stage and prod terraform.tfvars. The cost figure comes from decision 10 of 2026-10-31 and R12-LEDGER-7009. This is the same reading as R12-FABRIC-8091, 8073, 10178 and 9118 and R12-RES-9169. The mirror half follows R12-COVERAGE-7192 and R12-FABRIC-7038.
decisions.closure: No code now. The gap opens with this ruling, dated 2026-10-31, and the $2,705-$8,140 a month figure. The cross-region half closes with R12-FABRIC-7038 at a second region.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. The cost of $2,705-$8,140 a month comes from billed-plan-2026-10-19.md §7 and R12-LEDGER-7009. The ruling matches R12-FABRIC-8091, 8073, 10178 and 9118, which put the emulator first after funding. decisions.ruling: The module already places one broker per zone and refuses two in one zone, and its plan tests show three zones. A real environment renders three only beside the Spanner managed log. Decision 5 keeps that unbought at $2,705 to $8,140 a month, and the broker machines are unpriced with no boot image baked, so the row stays PARTIAL. There are no separate controller machines: under ADR 0111 the Spanner lease is the controller (R12-FABRIC-7037).
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/event-fabric-broker/main.tf:181 places each instance with zone = local.broker_zone[each.value] and carries the one-per-zone and in-region preconditions. variables.tf:170 refuses more than one broker without managed_log. modules/event-fabric-broker/tests/machine.tftest.hcl::three_brokers_are_placed_in_three_zones and terraform/tests/fabric.tftest.hcl::three_brokers_behind_the_spanner_lease_are_provisioned run in plan mode only. event_fabric_broker is null and enable_spanner = false in every infrastructure/environments/*/terraform.tfvars, which is a protected path. This is the same as R12-RES-9169 and R12-FABRIC-9118.
decisions.closure: No code now. The trigger is a priced ADR that funds the managed log and three brokers, plus a baked broker image. Then the owner sets event_fabric_broker in dev's terraform.tfvars with three addresses in three zones and managed_log; that tfvars file is protected, so the owner applies the change. decisions.skeptic: Verified. modules/event-fabric-broker/main.tf:180 sets zone = local.broker_zone[each.value]. variables.tf:170-172 refuses more than one broker when managed_log is null. machine.tftest.hcl:312 three_brokers_are_placed_in_three_zones and terraform/tests/fabric.tftest.hcl:184 run under command = plan. decisions.ruling: Brokers lead and follow through the managed log ADR 0111 chose. A follower that holds the committed log and takes over with nothing lost is proven, on the in-memory log and a fake Spanner transport. The row's check counts only on a deployed fabricd writing through a regional Spanner database. Decision 5 keeps that unbought at $2,705 to $8,140 a month, so the row stays PARTIAL, as R12-FABRIC-8073 does.
decisions.rationale: qip-streaming tests/event_fabric_managed.rs::a_follower_holds_the_committed_log_and_takes_over_with_no_committed_loss (:236) and qip-fabricd tests/managed.rs:305 run on the in-memory log. qip-fabricd src/spanner.rs::SpannerManagedLog is tested only through a fake transport (tests::a_commit_under_a_superseded_lease_epoch_rolls_back_as_fenced_and_inserts_nothing). config.rs:303 seats it only when QIP_EVENT_FABRIC_MANAGED_LOG=spanner. infrastructure/event-fabric/spanner.ddl is unapplied, and no google_spanner_database exists for the fabric. fabricd is tested in ci.yml but not deployed. This is the same as R12-FABRIC-8073 and 9118.
decisions.closure: No code now. Correct the register: implemented and tested become true, because the code and the in-memory tests exist; status stays PARTIAL. The trigger is an ADR with a measured need and a monthly ceiling, and the owner's funding. Then: declare the fabric Spanner database from spanner.ddl behind enable_spanner, and prove SpannerManagedLog against the emulator first (ADR 0111 Amendment 1 §4). Add fabricd to the image build through a lane-written docs/blueprint/lanes patch for the owner to apply. Deploy with QIP_EVENT_FABRIC_MANAGED_LOG=spanner and show a follower holding the identical log after the leader is killed.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. qip-streaming tests/event_fabric_managed.rs:236 holds the follower test. qip-fabricd spanner.rs tests use a Scripted transport (:729), and the test at :805 exists. config.rs:303 seats 'spanner' only when asked. The only google_spanner_database is modules/data 'positions' (:655), so the fabric has none. ci.yml:107 tests qip-fabricd but does not deploy it.
