decisions.ruling: ADR 0111 and its Amendment 1 stand. No Raft is written or admitted, and the metadata quorum is the regional Spanner database under lease-epoch checks. The requirement's 'no cloud database' clause is not read away, so the row stays PARTIAL by decision. The Spanner half waits with the managed log under decision 5, at $2,705 to $8,140 a month.
decisions.rationale: docs/adr/0111 (Amendment 1, decision E02) chose Spanner and did not take openraft. ADR 0109's table lists openraft as admissible but not chosen, and its Amendment 2 dissent explains why hand-written consensus fails silently. qip-fabricd src/config.rs:303 seats only 'spanner', and config.rs::tests::the_managed_log_is_local_by_default_complete_when_asked_for_and_refused_half_configured (:1063, 'raft' at :1087) refuses 'raft'. infrastructure/event-fabric/spanner.ddl holds only fabric_leases, fabric_batches and fabric_checkpoints. It has no tables for stream definitions, placement, broker epochs or ACLs. The precedents are R12-FABRIC-7054 (declined by ADR 0111 and billed, ruled STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY) and R12-OBS-9146.
decisions.closure: No code now. The trigger is the managed log funded by an ADR with a measured need and a ceiling. Then: add stream-definition, placement, broker-epoch and ACL tables beside fabric_leases in spanner.ddl. Write them only in read-write transactions that check the writer's lease epoch. Move qip-fabricd's per-broker catalogue file onto those tables. Prove it against the emulator, then run the game day: losing one of three zones keeps metadata writable. The 'no cloud database' clause reopens only through an ADR that supersedes ADR 0111 and admits a consensus crate under ADR 0109 with an allow-list patch.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. config.rs:1063 holds the test and :1087 inserts 'raft', which is refused. spanner.ddl has only fabric_leases, fabric_batches and fabric_checkpoints. ADR 0109's table row reads openraft 'Admissible ... not chosen by ADR 0111', and ADR 0111 Amendment 1 item 1 says the openraft fallback is not taken. The ruling keeps the 'no cloud database' clause and leaves the row PARTIAL, so the requirement is not read away. It defers the metadata tables until funding, consistent with R12-FABRIC-9118 and 7054 and R12-OBS-9146. A Raft admission is routed through a superseding ADR plus an allow-list patch.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0119 section 3 already decided this. The mirror is built and game-dayed now, on two fabricd processes on one host. It is deployed only when a record supersedes ADR 0035's one region. Build the remaining slices on one host, and let no committed catalogue select mirroring. The row stays PARTIAL until a second region exists.
decisions.rationale: services/qip-streaming/src/event_fabric/mirror.rs::plan_copy (slice 1) is the only mirror code. qip-events src/event_fabric/policy.rs:451-457 refuses spec.mirroring != Mirroring::None (C8), and Mirroring has only None, Selective and Full (policy.rs:243). qip-fabricd has no mirror role. ADR 0119 adds Mirroring::Async { targets } for P0, P1 and named P2 (§1), the lag series and stale state (§2), and the local build and game day (§3). Two earlier rulings bind this row. R12-OBS-9148 (IMPLEMENT) builds a mirror role with lag series on one host and relaxes no StreamPolicy refusal for any committed catalogue. R12-COVERAGE-7192 says 'the mirror itself is built under R12-FABRIC-7038'.
decisions.closure: Add Mirroring::Async { targets } to StreamPolicy, admitted for P0, P1 and named P2 only. Refuse it at catalogue load unless the composition root configures a mirror for every named target, so every committed catalogue still loads with None. Selective and Full stay refused. Build the qip-fabricd mirror role once and share it with R12-OBS-9148: the fabric's existing mTLS client to the source, and a producer into the region-qualified target stream that nothing else may write. Journal each MirrorGap as a Gap record. Put the checkpoint behind a port, file-backed locally, with Spanner fabric_checkpoints later. Add the typed stale state past the stream's bound, and replay from the source archive. Test: 'a mirror cut from its source leaves the source acknowledging, the target stale and lag growing, and on reconnect the target converges with no duplicate and no unexplained gap'. Mutations: drop the duplicate-by-source-position check, or make the source produce wait on the mirror; each fails the test. No environment starts the role.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. mirror.rs::plan_copy is the only mirror code. policy.rs:453 refuses mirroring != None (C8), and Mirroring is at :243. qip-fabricd has no mirror role; qip-edge-node's event_fabric/mirror.rs is the journal seam, not this. ADR 0119 (accepted) §1 adds Mirroring::Async { targets } for P0, P1 and named P2, and §3 says build and prove locally now and deploy at a second region. The ruling matches R12-OBS-9148 (shared role, one host, no committed catalogue relaxed) and R12-COVERAGE-7192, which says the mirror is built under 7038. The only production constructor of StreamPolicy::new is catalogue.rs:446; admission.rs:91 is test-only. So the catalogue-load refusal without a configured mirror keeps every committed catalogue at None. Selective and Full stay refused. No environment starts the role, and the row stays PARTIAL.

decisions.ruling: O08 is declined. prost is not admitted, as ADR 0109's table already says: the fabric codec is canonical JSON under hash chains, and no wire format outside this repository asks for protobuf. The descriptors are the schema lock computed from the Rust types. No Rust type is generated from a descriptor, because that would give one schema two sources. Both of the row's checks pass, and the row stays PARTIAL on 'generated Rust types', declined by decision and not read away.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0109's table row for prost reads 'Not admitted ... until a wire format outside this repository requires protobuf' (ADR 0100 §1). ADR 0156 decision 1 makes qip-events/schemas.lock.json the one descriptor source, held equal to the shapes of the Rust types by qip-acceptance tests/event_fabric_schema_lock.rs. qip-events tests/schema_compat.rs::removing_renaming_or_retyping_a_field_without_a_version_bump_is_refused_and_a_defaulted_addition_is_admitted (:54) and ::identical_content_gets_the_same_schema_id_and_different_content_never_does (:124) meet the verification. No prost appears in backend/Cargo.lock or scripts/dependency-allowlist.txt. The gap still files O08 as an open owner question, which is now decided.
decisions.closure: Rewrite the gap: 'O08 decided 2026-10-31: declined (ADR 0109 table, ADR 0100 §1, ADR 0156 d1); generated Rust types from descriptors are not built because the lock is generated from the Rust types'. Cite the two schema_compat tests and event_fabric_schema_lock as evidence. Status stays PARTIAL. The trigger to reopen is an external wire format that requires protobuf; then an ADR admits prost under ADR 0109 with a protected allow-list patch.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. ADR 0109's table row for prost reads 'Not admitted ... until a wire format outside this repository requires protobuf'. ADR 0156 §1 item 1 makes qip-events/schemas.lock.json the one descriptor source. The lock file and qip-acceptance tests/event_fabric_schema_lock.rs exist. schema_compat.rs:54 and :124 carry the two named tests that meet the check. Neither prost nor tokio nor opentelemetry is in Cargo.lock or the allow-list. The row stays PARTIAL on generated Rust types by decision, which is honest. The gap's open-O08 text is older than the decision, so REGRADE_TEXT fits.

decisions.ruling: O09 is declined. No OpenTelemetry exporter crate is admitted (ADR 0026 stands). No tokio goes on the fabric SDK path, which the edge node's drain reaches, until a committed measurement shows the thread-backed subscription falls short. The hooks are built in-tree on the producer and the consumer, and they leave through the existing OTLP drain. The row stays PARTIAL on a future-based async subscription and on a ring buffer inside the SDK; neither is invented here.
decisions.rationale: libs/qip-transport/src/event_fabric/consumer.rs::Consumer::subscribe (:495) is a bounded channel fed by one fetch thread (FABRIC-034). producer.rs::Producer::send (:358) carries idempotent sequencing agreed with the broker (qip-fabricd tests/broker.rs:573, 655, 1338), so the row's verification already passes. No tokio or opentelemetry appears in backend/Cargo.lock or scripts/dependency-allowlist.txt. libs/qip-observability/src/metrics.rs::Snapshot::to_otlp_metrics and services/qip-telemetry-drain already encode OTLP in-tree, and ADR 0156 gives the drain one home. ADR 0109 Amendment 2 condition 2 keeps tokio off qip-edge's decision path without a measurement. qip-edge-node src/event_fabric/drain.rs and outbox.rs use the SDK's Producer.
decisions.closure: Write the ADR first. Add a FabricHook trait in qip-transport event_fabric with a no-op default. It covers produced, acknowledged (stream, partition, base offset), fetched and committed events, each with elapsed time, and Producer and Consumer call it. An adapter in qip-fabricd and qip-edge-node records into qip-observability Metrics, which qip-telemetry-drain exports. Test: 'a producer and consumer with a hook against a real broker record one produce and one fetch per batch at the ack's base offset, and the drain's OTLP body carries both'. Mutation: remove the hook call from Producer::send's acknowledgement arm and the test fails. Status stays PARTIAL on async subscriptions and SDK ring-buffer integration.
decisions.adr_title: The fabric SDK's telemetry hooks are an in-tree trait exported only through the existing OTLP drain, its subscription stays thread-backed, and neither an exporter crate nor tokio reaches the SDK (declines O09)
decisions.skeptic: Verified. consumer.rs:495 subscribe uses a sync_channel fed by one spawned thread. producer.rs:358 is send. qip-observability metrics.rs:253 has to_otlp_metrics, and the qip-telemetry-drain crate exists. Neither tokio nor opentelemetry is in Cargo.lock or the allow-list. ADR 0109 Amendment 2 condition 2 is quoted correctly, and keeping tokio off the SDK path is a further tightening by the new ADR. One small misread does not change the decision: qip-edge-node has no event_fabric/outbox.rs. The outbox producer lives in writer.rs, and drain.rs is the file that names Producer. The row stays PARTIAL on async subscriptions and the ring buffer, so nothing is read away, and the ADR comes first.

decisions.ruling: O07 is not taken now. QUIC stays measured-only under ADR 0112 §4 and its Amendment 1, and I will not swap the cross-region measurement for a local or synthetic one. That measurement needs a second region, which ADR 0035 does not run and nobody has priced, so the row stays PARTIAL on 'traffic is QUIC'. The requirement is not restated.
decisions.rationale: The mTLS half is built: qip-transport src/tls.rs and server.rs::Server::bind_tls require a client certificate, and qip-fabricd src/lib.rs binds with it. Tests: qip-transport tests/mtls.rs::a_client_with_no_certificate_never_reaches_a_handler and ::a_certificate_from_another_authority_is_refused_at_the_handshake. qip-transport src/event_fabric/transport.rs::FabricTransport is still the seam C2's QUIC would swap, and HttpTransport is its only implementation. ADR 0112 §4 and Amendment 1 item 3 make the cross-region peer-mesh TCP+TLS-versus-QUIC measurement the gate. They admit quinn by its own allow-list record only if that measurement shows a cost the platform needs removed, and they list 'QUIC adopted without its measurement' under what would make the record wrong. ADR 0156 §4(a) holds the same rule. A second region is billed and unpriced (docs/blueprint/lanes/billed-plan-2026-10-19.md #13). Decision 4 of 2026-10-25 parks NCC until a second region is decided, and decision 5 declines new billed infrastructure. scripts/dependency-allowlist.txt has no quinn line and is protected.

decisions.ruling: O10 is declined. blake3 is not admitted, neither as a crate nor written in-tree, because ADR 0104 already rejected BLAKE3 for the batch chain and ADR 0043 keeps SHA-256 and HMAC as our only hash primitives. SHA-256 with CRC32C stays the content protection. The requirement names BLAKE3, so the row stays PARTIAL on that word and is not reworded to pass.
decisions.rationale: qip-events src/event_fabric/codec.rs::ContentHash has Sha256 and Blake3 variants (HASH_TAG_SHA256 and HASH_TAG_BLAKE3 at :158-159), and the codec refuses Blake3 on both encode and decode (:886-917). qip-storage src/segment/archive.rs:114,126 and segment/log.rs:248 refuse it too. The SHA-256 is in-tree: qip-core src/hash.rs::sha256, checked against FIPS 180-4 vectors in tests/hashing.rs::sha256_matches_fips_180_4_vectors. ADR 0104 'Alternatives rejected' declines BLAKE3 as unaudited for this class of use, and ADR 0043 §2 affirms in-tree SHA-256/HMAC as the primitives. The row's gap ('waits on O10, no ADR') and its evidence lines (codec.rs:145,686-707) are older than this ruling and the tree.

decisions.ruling: Nothing is pinned by default before a deployed node measures the need, as ADR 0082 says. The supervisor's CPUAffinity stays the only default placement. The opt-in QIP_SPOOL_WRITER_CPU pin stays opt-in and unset in every template. Pinning the decision thread from inside the binary is its own ADR under ADR 0082 decision 3, argued from R12-REFLEX-8066's replay on a funded node, so the row stays PARTIAL on 'a separate core'.
decisions.rationale: The handoff half of the check holds: the spool writer is its own thread behind try_send. qip-edge-node src/main.rs:1200-1208 pins it only when config.writer_cpu is Some, through event_fabric/placement.rs::pin_current_thread; otherwise it calls ::current_placement. The decision thread is never pinned. modules/execution-node/main.tf:100 sets first_isolated_cpu = 2, and the unit's CPUAffinity allows that one core, so pin_current_thread would refuse a second isolated core. ADR 0082 decision 3 reserves in-binary per-thread pinning for a new ADR argued from a measured second-thread requirement. Its reversal condition is a deployed node's measurement. R12-REFLEX-8066 (IMPLEMENT) builds that measurement harness, and its ruling says the row closes only on a funded, running node. execution_nodes_enabled = false in dev, and no node cost is named in docs/ops/runbooks/dev-redeploy-readiness.md.
decisions.closure: No code now. Trigger: dev's first execution node (2026-10-31 decision 5) runs R12-REFLEX-8066's tuned and untuned replay. If that run shows the writer sharing the decision thread's core costs latency, claim an ADR under ADR 0082 decision 3. It widens the unit's CPUAffinity to two isolated cores, pins the decision thread to the first and the writer to the second, and refuses to start with fewer than two. Its test in qip-edge-node tests/writer_placement.rs: the two threads run on different cores, and start-up is refused on one allowed core. Mutation: skip the decision-thread pin.
decisions.skeptic: The code matches the ruling. main.rs:1204-1207 calls pin_current_thread only when writer_cpu is Some and current_placement otherwise. placement.rs:130 pin_current_thread refuses any CPU the process is not already allowed. execution-node main.tf:100 sets first_isolated_cpu = 2, and startup.sh.tftpl:420 sets CPUAffinity to that one core (affinity.tftest.hcl pins 'CPUAffinity=2'). No infrastructure file sets QIP_SPOOL_WRITER_CPU. ADR 0082 decision 3 reserves in-binary per-thread pinning for a new ADR. Its title and its 'What would make this wrong' section make a deployed node's measurement the trigger. dev has execution_nodes_enabled = false. The ruling agrees with R12-REFLEX-8066, which closes only on a funded, running node. Nothing is loosened; the opt-in pin stays opt-in. The writer pin already runs taskset from inside the binary without an ADR of its own. That is an existing deviation the ruling does not widen.

decisions.ruling: No runtime verb creates a topic or changes a quota or a retention. A topic is a reviewed code change naming its retention class, and a stream's policy is the committed catalogue's. The broker keeps refusing to redeclare a stream under a different policy. Drain and partition move act on leases that exist only on the Spanner managed log, so they are built with that log once it is funded, with R12-RES-8103's caught-up refusal. The requirement text stands, and the row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: Topics are a closed enum: qip-events src/topic.rs::Topic::ALL is [Self; 92], under ADR 0089 §2 and ADR 0152. qip-streaming src/event_fabric/broker.rs::Broker::declare_stream refuses a different policy, quotas and retention included, because 'it would change what the stream's existing records were promised'. service.rs's module doc has Service::apply_catalogue refuse a catalogue that would change one. The only drain is qip-fabricd src/lib.rs::Running::drain (DRAIN_FILE), which calls Broker::relinquish_leases, and that hands over nothing without a managed log. lib.rs::open_managed_log is Spanner-only. R12-FABRIC-9118 and R12-RES-8103 hold drain to a funded log and keep it a person's act. The mTLS attribution is built: qip-fabricd tests/broker.rs::an_isolate_request_over_mutual_tls_is_attributed_to_the_certificate_name_and_refused_when_operator_differs. qip-cli src/event_fabric/admin.rs stays loopback-only, because remote operator access needs the CA Service operator template, which ADR 0156 lists as BILLED. ADR 0156 §4(c): nothing is built to satisfy a word.
decisions.closure: No code now. Open the gap with the ruling: create topic, set quota and set retention are refused as runtime verbs, so the row stays PARTIAL on them. Trigger: the managed log is funded (Spanner $2,705-$8,140 a month, billed-plan #7, declined under decision 5). Then a lane adds attributed drain and partition-move routes and CLI verbs. Each gets a qip-fabricd mTLS test: the action is recorded under the certificate name and refused to an identity without the admin grant. Mutation: skip the admin-grant check. The CLI gets a workload-certificate source only with the CA Service operator template (R12-SEC-10054's pool).

One citation should change: 'nothing is built to satisfy a word' is in §4(c), which is about a second consumer. This row's own section is §4(d), and the ruling should cite that.

A regional Spanner commit, three read-write replicas one per zone, is the RF3 majority, but it counts only once a deployed fabricd seated on it acknowledges through it, and decision 5 has not taken that bill. The kill tests, qip-fabricd tests/managed.rs::a_killed_leader_is_replaced_by_its_follower_with_no_acknowledged_record_lost and tests/chaos.rs, run on MemoryManagedLog. decisions.closure: No code now. Correct gap step (4) to cite ADR 0119 and R12-COVERAGE-7192. Trigger: decision 5's measured-need ADR funds the Spanner managed log. Then run the emulator proof of spanner.rs first (ADR 0111 Amendment 1 item 4), then seat fabricd on Spanner with streams.managed.json in one environment, and record a kill-the-leader drill losing no quorum-acked record. decisions.skeptic: The cited code exists. policy.rs StreamPolicy::new admits a replicated profile only for P0/P1 at MANAGED_REPLICATION_FACTOR and refuses any other RF (:423-449). broker.rs:1151 refuses a managed stream on a broker with no managed log. streams.managed.json declares P0/P1 managed_majority at RF3, and no environment references it. config.rs:303 accepts only "spanner". managed.rs:305's kill test and chaos.rs use MemoryManagedLog. decisions.ruling: O11 is declined for P2 for now. The market journal stays RF1 under ADR 0111 §2 until a committed measurement of P2 volume and loss from a running broker says it must survive a zone. Its escalation is then Managed Kafka for P2 alone, under its own record with a monthly ceiling. Throttled mirroring waits for ADR 0119's mirror at a second region, and the requirement text stands.

decisions.closure: No code now. Trigger: a deployed broker produces the committed P2 volume and loss measurement. Archive bucket $0.30-$6 a month (billed-plan #2).

decisions.ruling: P3 stays RF1 and is replayable from the archive under ADR 0111 §2. A configurable RF2/3 that no mechanism delivers would be the false claim that record forbids, so StreamPolicy keeps refusing it. Its lag half already holds. RF2/3 for P3 reopens only through an ADR that names the mechanism, a measured P3 need and a monthly ceiling, after the deploy. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: The lag half holds: qip-streaming src/event_fabric/admission.rs::refuses_for_lag exempts P3, and broker.rs:2229 skips the lag refusal for it. qip-events src/event_fabric/policy.rs::StreamPolicy::new refuses replication_factor != 1 for any stream outside P0/P1 managed_majority. ADR 0111 'What would make this wrong' names 'StreamPolicy admitting a replication claim for P2-P4 that no mechanism delivers'. The only replication mechanism is the Spanner managed log, which decision 5 declines. This is consistent with R12-FABRIC-7054 and R12-FABRIC-10178.
decisions.closure: No code now. Trigger: a running broker's committed P3 volume measurement, then an ADR amending ADR 0111 §2 that names the mechanism and its ceiling. Then add a policy test that RF2/3 is configurable for P3 only on that mechanism, and a fabricd test that a lagging P3 group on it is not refused. Mutation: let StreamPolicy::new admit P3 at RF3 without the mechanism, and the test must fail. Cost: Spanner floor $2,705 a month (billed-plan #7) before any P3 capacity; P3 capacity not priced.
decisions.skeptic: The lag half holds in code. broker.rs:2229 returns early unless admission.rs:69 refuses_for_lag is true, and P3's required overload policy is not RefuseProducer. policy.rs refuses replication_factor != 1 outside P0/P1 managed_majority. The ruling keeps that refusal and so avoids the false claim ADR 0111 warns against. Its quote is slightly off: ADR 0111 says 'honours', not 'delivers', and the meaning is the same. The ruling agrees with R12-FABRIC-7054 and R12-FABRIC-10178, and the Spanner floor of $2,705 a month is named.

decisions.ruling: Three brokers per production region, one per zone, on C4 or C4D, stands as ADR 0111 Amendment 1 and ADR 0156 §6(a) set it. The row stays PARTIAL until a broker runs from a baked image in a committed environment, and nothing in this ruling funds one.

No commitment is bought: R12-FINOPS-10137's refusal stands until a sizing record measured on a node exists. The row stays PARTIAL until a node and a broker are provisioned.

decisions.ruling: Job specs carry a queue, a capacity and a priority, and a critical job on Spot is refused; that stands. LocalTrainingProvider::submit (job.rs:412-431) counts only non-terminal jobs in the queue, and run_to_completion (job.rs:515) submits and polls one job to a terminal state before the next, so the active count at admit is always 0. backend/crates/apps/qip-deepbrain/src/learning.rs:2246 fits with LocalTrainer::new() in process. In the one region we have, the three networks and the controlled egress are built. The landing bucket waits on the storage switch and its first writer. ADR 0121 replaced a Cloud Run collector with the in-process push, and I do not count that push as a collector. The service plane is Cloud Run, not a cluster, and the row stays PARTIAL.

The registry, attestor and GitOps cluster stay in the environment project until the record that supersedes ADR 0035 names that region (R12-GCP-8035). The split is then made under an organisation I hold (R12-GCP-10001), as an amendment to ADR 0118.
decisions.rationale: docs/adr/0113 §4 (Accepted 2026-10-11) says 'Now: nothing changes. One project per environment', with the trigger being a second execution region. Its other trigger, real-money preparation, never applies under ADR 0003. docs/adr/0118 decision 2 makes that trigger a change of shape inside one folder. infrastructure/foundation/main.tf declares only google_project.seed (:280) and google_project.environment (:309). modules/registry, modules/binaryauthorization and modules/gitops-control-plane are instantiated in the environment project. The second region waits on a running shadow node's measurements (R12-GCP-8035, STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY). The folder exists only in org mode (foundation/main.tf::google_folder.platform, count on local.org_mode), the same external dependency R12-GCP-10001 named. Moving state and re-running the bootstrap now buys isolation for a plane with one region and no live path.
decisions.closure: Nothing is built now. Record in the row that O17 is answered by ADR 0113 §4. decisions.skeptic: The deferral is right. ADR 0113 §4 says 'Now: nothing changes. ADR 0113 §4 places the Binary Authorization attestor in the security project, not engineering, and puts per-concern projects inside a folder per environment, not directly under google_folder.platform. (2) It contradicts R12-GCP-10001's closure, which makes the plane split by wiring modules/resource-hierarchy into foundation under an ADR amending 0118. At the trigger, under an org the owner holds (R12-GCP-10001), the ADR amending 0118 extends modules/resource-hierarchy with engineering and security planes. It wires that module into foundation and uses moved blocks to put registry and gitops-control-plane in engineering and the attestor in security, inside each environment's folder. The tftest asserts each project's parent folder and contents. Mutation: plan the attestor in the engineering project.

decisions.ruling: The platform creates resources only in the United States and the European Union, the two places its committed environments already name. The folder enforces that with gcp.resourceLocations, so no project owner can step outside it, and compute.requireShieldedVm moves up to the folder beside the key policies. Each environment's project narrows further, to the locations its own tfvars name. nam-eur-asea, which reaches Asia, goes with R12-LEDGER-8136's move to nam3.
decisions.rationale: No gcp.resourceLocations exists in infrastructure/ at any scope. infrastructure/foundation/main.tf local.boolean_policies (:91-103) lacks compute.requireShieldedVm. That policy exists only as infrastructure/terraform/main.tf::google_org_policy_policy.require_shielded_vm at project scope, with count = var.project_key_policies_enabled, which is false in dev tfvars :332. dev tfvars sets region us-east4, while test, stage and prod set europe-west2. infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf::bucket_location defaults to "EU" and no tfvars overrides it, so the row's 'archive bucket is multi-region US' is stale. modules/data/main.tf::google_spanner_instance.global sets config nam-eur-asea (:623), which R12-LEDGER-8136 moves to nam3. Every VM template (modules/execution-node, ledgerd, event-fabric-broker) declares shielded_instance_config, so the folder copy refuses nothing the root plans. A residency set is a contract, hence an ADR. variables.tf and the tfvars are protected, so the project-scope half ships as a lane patch.

(2) In infrastructure/foundation/main.tf, add "compute.requireShieldedVm" to local.boolean_policies, plus a google_org_policy_policy.resource_locations list policy whose allowed_values are the ADR's set (in:us-locations, in:eu-locations). Each value must be checked against Google's value-group page in the same change, and 'global' is listed only if a committed resource needs it. Gate both on local.policies_applied and name both in output controls_not_applied for no-org mode. (3) Add foundation.tftest.hcl runs: 'org mode plans requireShieldedVm and resourceLocations with exactly the ADR's list on the folder' and 'no-org mode plans neither and names both'. Mutations: delete the shielded entry, and add in:asia-locations. (4) Add a qip-acceptance infrastructure.rs test asserting each folder policy inside its own resource body in foundation/main.tf; deleting either resource fails it. decisions.skeptic: Most citations check out. No gcp.resourceLocations exists anywhere. boolean_policies (:91-103) lacks requireShieldedVm, and main.tf:1457 require_shielded_vm is gated on project_key_policies_enabled, false at dev tfvars:332. dev's region is us-east4; test, stage and prod are europe-west2. bucket_location defaults to "EU" and is passed at main.tf:663. Spanner config is nam-eur-asea at data/main.tf:623. The VM modules declare shielded_instance_config. The ruling rests on a misread: committed resources use location "global", which is in neither the US nor the EU set. One is ungated: modules/observability/logging.tf:15-18 google_logging_project_bucket_config.workloads, location = "global", which holds every environment's workload logs. The others are security.tf:104 (PAM entitlement) and public-edge/main.tf:385 (Certificate Manager). By the closure's own condition, 'global' must therefore be admitted. That passes any global resource, including the log bucket's data, while the ruling reads 'only in the United States and the European Union' as met. Corrected closure: keep steps (1)-(5), plus the following. The ADR names the three committed global resources. The same change moves the workloads log bucket to a location inside the set: var.region, or the matching us/eu log-bucket location. 'global' is admitted only for config-only resources that cannot be regional (PAM, Certificate Manager), and the ADR says so. A qip-acceptance infrastructure.rs test asserts that no data-bearing resource (storage bucket, log bucket, BigQuery dataset, Spanner instance or database) names location "global" or a location outside the set. Mutation: set the workloads log bucket back to "global".

decisions.ruling: I do not grant foundry lineages one by one. A lineage is evo-{subject}, minted per sweep at run time, and a register entry per lineage would be written to pass whatever the roots happen to run. A promotion is judged on the alpha family the sweep declared, one of the ten that ADR 0155 §24 already grants on paper, and a sweep that declares none is refused. Every root that builds a CentralConfig arms the register from the committed paper seed baked into its image, and fails closed when it cannot read it.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/central/factory.rs::StrategyFactory::promote calls register.admit_deployment(candidate.family()). That family is StrategyFamily::new(lineage) (central/foundry.rs::StrategyFoundry::new :153). apps/qip-deepbrain/src/evolution.rs passes format!("evo-{subject}"), and its config.alpha_family defaults to None (:128). data/datasets/paper-eligibility.json records the ten alpha families (market_making ... execution_alpha), venues XLON/XNYS/XPAR and jurisdiction paper only, so no lineage can match it. central/plane.rs::CentralConfig::promotion_eligibility defaults to None, and neither apps/qip-api/src/main.rs:1227 nor apps/qip-deepbrain/src/main.rs:172 sets it. infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile already COPYs infrastructure/trust/ to /etc/qip/trust from the repo-root context, so the row's 'build context is backend/ only' is stale. Arming adds a refusal where today there is none. Changing the strategy subject amends ADR 0155 §23, hence an ADR.
decisions.closure: After the ADR: (1) StrategyFactory::promote judges the strategy subject by candidate.alpha_family(), refusing None with a message naming the sweep's lineage. The lineage stays the trial-book key. (2) infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile COPYs data/datasets/paper-eligibility.json to /etc/qip/eligibility/paper-eligibility.json. qip-api and qip-deepbrain read that fixed path in any deployed environment, and the repo copy only under QIP_DEPLOYMENT=local. Either refuses start-up with exit 78 when the file is unreadable or empty. No variable can disarm the register or point it elsewhere. (3) Venues and products come from the root's own committed configuration, and any the seed lacks is refused. The ADR may add records only for simulated subjects a root actually names (for example XSIM), paper jurisdiction only, under §24's existing grant, listed one by one. (4) Tests: a kernel test 'a candidate whose sweep declared no alpha family is refused promotion naming its lineage, while one declared momentum_and_trend on a recorded venue promotes' (mutation: fall back to the lineage key). A qip-deepbrain test 'the composed central plane is armed from the committed seed' (mutation: leave promotion_eligibility None). Every assertion in qip-kernel tests/central.rs::a_family_cleared_in_the_product_catalogue_but_unrecorded_in_the_compliance_register_cannot_be_promoted is kept. The row is re-graded on the lane's mutation report.
decisions.adr_title: Promotion is judged against the compliance register by the sweep's declared alpha family, a sweep that declares none is refused, and every root that promotes arms the register from the committed paper seed baked into its image
decisions.skeptic: Verified. factory.rs:577 calls admit_deployment(candidate.family().as_str(), ...). foundry.rs:153 uses StrategyFamily::new(lineage). evolution.rs:1099 passes format!("evo-{subject}"), and alpha_family defaults to None (:128). The seed holds the ten strategy families, the venues XLON, XNYS and XPAR, and only the paper jurisdiction. plane.rs:217 defaults promotion_eligibility to None. qip-api main.rs:1227 and qip-deepbrain main.rs:172 use ..CentralConfig::default(). Dockerfile:129 COPYs infrastructure/trust/ from the repo-root context (COPY backend/ at :72). qip-deepbrain already exits with EX_CONFIG=78. Arming adds refusals where none exist today, which tightens. ADR 0155 §22's own reason for keying by family (minted ids cannot be recorded ahead) applies equally to evo-* lineages. One fix: the strategy subject is defined in ADR 0155 §22, not §23, so the new ADR amends §22 (and §23 only for its consultation points).

decisions.ruling: qip-ledgerd's balances are the platform's book of record for cash and positions. The kernel's desk book stays as a working copy for admission and is compared with the ledger's balance for the desk chain after every acknowledged ship. Any difference is a reconciliation break that refuses new desk orders until a person records a correction, and neither side is overwritten. A cell keeps its own book because it must trade with no centre (ADR 0214). The centre reconciles that book under ADR 0208 and never reads it as a balance.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/desk_ledger.rs ships an OutcomeRecord copy and reads nothing back. Platform::observe_ledger_obligations (platform.rs:12358) has callers only in qip-kernel tests (tests/survival_gate.rs), none in any apps/* main. apps/qip-ledgerd/src/read_api.rs serves /api/v1/ledger/balance and /obligations. Platform::ledger_lagging (platform.rs:7222) already refuses region shares while the ledger trails, which is the precedent for halting on the ledger's state (cf. the R12-RES-7099 ruling). Desk shipping runs only when QIP_FABRIC_URL is set (apps/qip-api/src/main.rs via qip_desk_ship::build), and no committed deployment sets it. Which of two books is authoritative is a contract, hence an ADR. The halt adds a refusal and moves no money.
decisions.closure: After the ADR: once each desk ship is acknowledged, the qip-api root reads /api/v1/ledger/balance for the desk chain. It uses a client its existing dependencies already provide; a new crate needs ADR 0109. It hands the reading to a new Platform method that compares it per unit with the kernel's desk book and journals a desk-ledger break record. While a break is open, desk order intake refuses, naming the break. The break clears only on a recorded correction followed by agreement, never because a later read happens to agree. Tests: a vertical slice 'a desk posting the ledger drops halts new desk orders with a named reconciliation break' (mutation: skip the comparison), and a kernel test 'a later agreeing read does not clear an open desk-ledger break'. Positions and grants for R12-LEDGER-8007 ride this path. The row then waits on deploy (ledgerd, fabric broker and desk token).
decisions.adr_title: qip-ledgerd's balances are the book of record for cash and positions: the kernel's desk book is a working copy checked against them after every acknowledged ship, and a disagreement refuses new desk orders until a recorded correction, never by overwriting either side
decisions.skeptic: The authority ruling is sound, and the facts are verified. desk_ledger.rs only emits OutcomeRecord. observe_ledger_obligations (platform.rs:12358) is called only from tests/survival_gate.rs. ledger_lagging is at platform.rs:7222, read_api serves /balance and /obligations, and qip_desk_ship::build is in qip-api main.rs:319. The closure rests on a misread of the acknowledgement. qip-desk-ship lib.rs:13-27 acknowledges once the broker has archived the batch, not once qip-ledgerd has booked it; ledgerd consumes asynchronously. read_api.rs:140-146 handle_balance returns a bare number for one account and unit, with no applied position. A read straight after each ack therefore sees a trailing ledger, records a 'break', and by this ruling only a person's correction clears it, so normal lag would halt the desk on every ship. Corrected closure: the ADR adds the applied desk-chain position to the ledgerd read, a contract change. The root compares only once that position has reached the acknowledged ship's sequence, for the named desk accounts per unit. decisions.ruling: I choose no relief method under the delegation. FIFO, average cost or specific identification is a tax method for a jurisdiction, and ADR 0153 decision 7 holds that such a method is a legal fact this repository has never been shown. A lot relieved by a method I picked would sit in the ledger of record and read as booked. OperationKind::TaxLot stays bookable and readable, with no producer. The row stays PARTIAL until a person with the facts declares the jurisdiction and its relief method in a committed record.

decisions.ruling: O07 is decided as in R12-MESH-10075: ADR 0112 §4 stands, with no QUIC now and no quinn admitted. decisions.ruling: The requirement names collectors and the text stands. ADR 0121 and my R12-OBS-10059 ruling push metrics and spans from the process on a bounded thread that counts and drops a failed push. A collector, vendored or hosted, and its ingestion are billed under ADR 0156's BILLED list and unpriced, so nothing is bought before dev runs and the row stays PARTIAL.

decisions.ruling: IBM Quantum is reached by one identity only: a gateway workload of its own in the optimisation zone. It alone may hold a connected hosted provider, the qip-quantum-token mount and ibm-quantum egress. The deep brain stays in cognition with no IBM route and submits through QuantumGateway. Nothing is deployed for that identity until a vendor is contracted, so the row stays PARTIAL. The guard that refuses a second caller is built now.
decisions.rationale: The queue and transport exist: libs/qip-quantum/src/gateway.rs::QuantumGateway (submit/poll on a worker) and provider.rs::HostedProvider::connected. solver.rs refuses a synchronous solve on a non-simulator. qip-acceptance/tests/runtime_reachability.rs::EXPECTED_UNWIRED lists HostedProvider::connected, so no binary builds one. modules/trust-zones/main.tf::sanctioned_egress_purposes sanctions ibm-quantum only for 'optimisation'. infrastructure.rs::the_trust_zones_deny_by_default_and_only_optimisation_may_reach_ibm pins that. But catalogue.tf places qip-deepbrain, which runs the gateway through qip-optimization-engine router.rs:778 QuantumGateway::new, in trust_zone 'cognition', and no workload sits in optimisation. external_egress = {} in every environment, and the qip-quantum-token slot (infrastructure/terraform/main.tf) is mounted nowhere. No identity is therefore 'the gateway identity'. Giving cognition IBM egress would widen the deep brain, which already holds the model-vendor route. This narrows where R12-QUANT-9007's ComputeSettings may admit hosted, and does not contradict it. Under 9007 and R12-QUANT-7016 the account, key and transport stay unbought (STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL).

decisions.ruling: I decline O13. ADR 0082 stands: no libc, nix or unsafe code enters the workspace to lock memory or busy-poll. The row asks for both only where measurement justifies them, and no running node has measured anything. Pinning and huge pages are in, and a node boots without neither. Memory locking and busy polling wait on R12-REFLEX-8066's tuned-against-untuned replay on the first funded node. If that replay shows a need, busy polling enters as a sysctl in the startup template. Memory locking enters only through an ADR that amends ADR 0082 with the measurement. The row stays PARTIAL.

No mlock call exists in backend/crates. ADR 0082 decision 1 refuses libc, nix and unsafe, and decision 3 has the supervisor pin. Admitting libc would also need an ADR 0109 allow-list entry. The R12-REFLEX-8066 ruling built the timing harness and closes only on a funded node. dev terraform.tfvars keeps execution_nodes_enabled = false, and docs/ops/runbooks/dev-redeploy-readiness.md section 5 names no node cost. decisions.ruling: The requirement stands as written, and the row stays PARTIAL on three clauses. First, the binary locks no memory: I decline O13, ADR 0082 stands, and the boot refusal of swap does that job meanwhile. Second, local scratch SSD needs a billed -lssd shape. ADR 0211's allow-list refuses that shape, decision 5 declines it, and nobody has named its cost. Third, IRQ, RPS and XPS steering is a host tuning. R12-REFLEX-8066 requires every tuning to pass a replay before it is adopted, so this one is written and measured with that replay on the funded node, not before.
decisions.rationale: startup.sh.tftpl:67, :74 and :84 refuse a host without isolcpus, with swap, or with too few huge pages. :420 pins with CPUAffinity, and :431-435 set CAP_IPC_LOCK and LimitMEMLOCK, but nothing calls mlockall (ADR 0082 decision 1). A grep finds no smp_affinity, rps_cpus, xps_cpus or irqbalance in startup.sh.tftpl or infrastructure/images/execution-node/provision.sh. modules/execution-node/variables.tf:161-166 admits only c4/c4d-highcpu-8 and -16, with no -lssd shape (ADR 0211). The R12-REFLEX-8066 requirement reads 'Each host tuning choice must be validated under replay before adoption', and its ruling says a host tuning is adopted only after a replay shows it helps. Decision 5 of owner-decisions-2026-10-25.md declines new billed infrastructure, and dev-redeploy-readiness.md section 5 names no SSD or node cost. No #[global_allocator] exists in backend/crates, so the allocator is the system allocator.
decisions.closure: Nothing lands before R12-REFLEX-8066's run on the first funded node. For that run, a lane adds a step to startup.sh.tftpl. It moves every IRQ's smp_affinity_list to housekeeping cores 0-1, sets RPS and XPS masks on the same cores, and refuses to boot if the masks do not read back. infrastructure.rs gains an acceptance assertion for the step, and the step ships only if the tuned-against-untuned replay favours it. mlockall reopens only through an ADR amending ADR 0082. Local SSD reopens only through an ADR that names its monthly cost. Until then, gap opens with this ruling.
decisions.skeptic: The citations hold. The refusals are at :67/:74/:84 and the pin at :420. LimitMEMLOCK is set with no mlockall call. No smp_affinity, rps_cpus, xps_cpus or irqbalance appears in the template or in provision.sh. modules/execution-node/variables.tf admits only c4/c4d-highcpu-8/16, with no -lssd shape. There is no #[global_allocator], and dev-redeploy-readiness section 5 names no node or SSD cost. Deferring IRQ/RPS/XPS until the replay matches R12-REFLEX-8066 ('a host tuning is adopted only after a replay shows it helps'). The new step only adds a boot refusal, so it is a tightening. One overstatement should be fixed in the text: 'the boot refusal of swap does that job meanwhile'. Refusing swap does not stop file-backed pages from being evicted, or the first touch of a page from faulting. The text should say it narrows the gap, not that it fills it. The clause stays PARTIAL either way, so the decision does not rest on this sentence.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0137 stands, and this row closes the way I ruled R12-REFLEX-9114: only on a fenced standby deployed in a second zone. That standby is a second billed node. No environment enables it, and decision 5 keeps it unbought. The GCS lease store, the node's scheme selection and the module's lease bucket may be built now. The root passthrough comes to me as the one protected patch 9114 already asked for, with standby_enabled false. One lane builds this once for both rows.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/standby.rs:107 and :117 hold MemoryLeaseStore, and :154 and :230 hold FileLeaseStore. The doc at :44-55 says FileLeaseStore is not a cross-zone store. SimulatedSessions at :271-287 answers for the in-process simulator only, and main.rs refuses a standby on any other adapter. tests/standby.rs:313::at_most_one_fence_admits_at_any_instant_over_every_interleaving already meets the property check. qip-storage gcp/storage.rs:333 and :447 put_if_absent send only ifGenerationMatch=0, so no compare-and-swap on update exists (the 9114 skeptic). modules/execution-node/main.tf:486 and :985 pass fencing_lease_path, and startup.sh.tftpl:271-276 writes QIP_FENCING_LEASE. The row's claim that the template 'sets no QIP_FENCING_LEASE' is therefore stale. modules/execution-node/variables.tf:567 admits only /var/lib/qip paths. Root infrastructure/terraform/main.tf passes no standby_enabled. ADR 0137's Rows section keeps the row PARTIAL until a node exercises it.
decisions.closure: This is lane L5's slice, shared with R12-REFLEX-9114 and built once. (1) Build GcsLeaseStore under ADR 0137 decision 1. load returns the object's generation. swap(None) writes with ifGenerationMatch=0 and swap(Some(g)) with ifGenerationMatch=g. A 412 is Ok(false), and any other failure is an error. A generation-match write added to qip-storage cites ADR 0137. (2) main.rs selects the store by gs:// or file path and refuses an unknown scheme. (3) variables.tf:567 admits gs:// only beside the module's lease bucket. That bucket gets object IAM for the two node accounts only, is gated on execution_nodes_enabled, and is covered by a tftest. Test: two keepers sharing one object through an in-process GCS double never both hold the fence. Mutation: treat a 412 as a won race, and the test fails. Write the root passthrough as 9114's lanes patch, with standby_enabled defaulting to false. Correct current's lease-variable text. The row closes only on a deployed pair.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. standby.rs:107/117 holds MemoryLeaseStore, :154/:230 holds FileLeaseStore, and the doc at :44-55 says FileLeaseStore is not a cross-zone store. SimulatedSessions is at :286-290, and main.rs:914-922 wires only the file store and SimulatedSessions. tests/standby.rs:313 exists. qip-storage gcp/storage.rs:333 sends only ifGenerationMatch=0 (put_if_absent at :447). main.tf:486/985 pass fencing_lease_path, and startup.sh.tftpl:276 writes QIP_FENCING_LEASE, so the row's text is stale. variables.tf:567 admits only /var/lib/qip paths. The root main.tf passes no standby_enabled. The ruling matches R12-REFLEX-9114: the store may be built now, the root passthrough comes as a protected patch with standby_enabled false, and the row closes only on a deployed pair. Admitting gs:// for the module's own bucket follows ADR 0137 decision 3 and loosens no safety guard. The no-lease refusal stays.

decisions.ruling: A shard is a node, and Terraform does not record which books a node owns. ADR 0136 makes that the centre's signed assignment. The execution_nodes key is the shard, and each node already carries its own specific reservation. So I add no shard key to the protected variables. A second node is a second billed reservation that ADR 0035 and decision 5 do not fund, so the row stays PARTIAL. The ownership slot, the cell's refusal and the centre's one-owner check are built under R12-EXEC-1067, the row ADR 0136 names.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/execution-node/main.tf:325-343::google_compute_reservation.node sets specific_reservation_required = true and sizes the reservation to node_count. qip-acceptance gcp_placement.rs::every_machine_group_the_repository_defines_consumes_a_specific_reservation_sized_to_its_target holds every group to that rule. infrastructure/environments/dev/terraform.tfvars:246 declares one node, newyork-1, and prod, stage and test hold execution_nodes = {}. A grep for BookOwnership in backend/crates finds nothing. ADR 0136 decisions 2-5 put ownership in a centre-signed books slot, and its Rows section names R12-EXEC-1067. ADR 0035 and the R12-GCP-8035 ruling keep one node until a superseding record names a monthly ceiling. The requirement carries the MULTI_REGION and COST flags.
decisions.closure: This row gets no shard work. EXEC-1067's lane builds ADR 0136's slot, the cell refusal and the kernel's one-owner check, each mutation-tested. The row closes when four things hold. A record superseding ADR 0035 (R12-GCP-8035) funds a second node and names its monthly cost. The owner declares that node in tfvars, a protected path. A plan shows two nodes, each consuming its own specific reservation. The centre's signed payloads give the two nodes disjoint books.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. main.tf:325-343 sets specific_reservation_required = true with a count of node_count. gcp_placement.rs:373 exists. dev tfvars:246 declares only newyork-1, and prod, stage and test hold execution_nodes = {}. No BookOwnership exists in backend/crates. ADR 0136's Rows section names R12-EXEC-1067, and that row is CODE_NOW in the wave1031 triage, so routing the slices there is consistent. The row stays PARTIAL until a record superseding ADR 0035 funds a second node, as R12-GCP-8035 rules. Nothing is spent and no protected path is edited. Calling each node a shard is not a restatement to pass, because closure still needs two nodes with disjoint books.

decisions.ruling: 'Other regions may cover eligible functions' is a permission, and I read it as one. Cover is allowed, not owed. With one region under ADR 0035, there is no other region to cover. If another region ever covers, it does so under its own grant and never extends authority to the cut-off cell. The row is graded on what it obliges and on its own check. That check is a cut-off cell that keeps placing inside its envelope, shrinks as inputs age and stops at expiry, and those tests drive production code. This ruling does not promote the row. It moves only after a mutation is recorded against each degraded.rs test and an independent skeptic re-grades it.
decisions.rationale: The requirement's verification check names no cross-region clause. backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/tests/degraded.rs:260::a_cell_cut_off_from_everything_keeps_placing_paper_orders_inside_its_envelope_and_journals_that_it_is_degraded and :395::a_cut_off_cells_orders_shrink_a_step_as_each_input_ages_and_stop_when_its_envelope_expires drive qip_edge_node::assemble and run_pass. tests/decision_loop.rs:1671::a_cell_whose_centre_has_gone_silent_keeps_journaling_its_orders_to_the_fabric_spool asserts that policy_sequence is unchanged. The row's notes record a mutation only for Cell::flush in DecisionLoop::turn, so degraded.rs has no recorded mutation yet. Decision 11 of 2026-10-25 makes the requirement text authoritative, and the text says 'may'. Reading it as an obligation would add a second-region duty that ADR 0035 and R12-GCP-8035 decline.
decisions.closure: Rewrite gap: drop 'deployment work' and record that cross-region cover is permitted, not owed, under this ruling. A lane then records one mutation per degraded.rs test and restores the code byte for byte. Halting the cell on a lost centre must fail :260. Removing the step narrowing in run_pass, or admitting past envelope expiry, must fail :395. Only then may an independent skeptic promote the row to COMPLETE. Until then it stays PARTIAL.
decisions.skeptic: The requirement statement says 'other regions may cover eligible functions'. Its integration check names only a cut-off cell that keeps placing orders, shrinks as inputs age and stops at expiry. Reading 'may' as permissive is the literal text, not a restatement. The ruling also refuses to promote the row until each degraded.rs test has a recorded mutation and an independent skeptic re-grades it, which meets the earlier triage skeptic's condition. degraded.rs:260/:395 drive assemble and run_pass. decision_loop.rs:1671 asserts policy_sequence is unchanged. The R12-G3 notes record a mutation only for Cell::flush. The ruling does not contradict R12-GCP-8035, because it adds no second-region duty. REGRADE_TEXT on the gap text fits.

decisions.ruling: No regional-loss game day is run with one region. ADR 0035 authorises one execution region, so removing it is an outage, not a test that other regions continue. The local region-isolation drill hangs one cell's link; it does not lose a region. The quarterly schedule begins with the record that supersedes ADR 0035 for a second region, as R12-GCP-8035 ruled, and that record names the monthly cost. The row stays MISSING until a scheduled run record exists.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0035 (docs/adr/0035-one-execution-node-in-shadow-mode.md) authorises one execution region. The R12-GCP-8035 and R12-GCP-8057 rulings keep a second region and its hub parked until a superseding record names a ceiling, and decision 4 of 2026-10-25 parks the hub. scripts/game-day/scenarios/region-isolation.json SIGSTOPs qip-fabricd under one cell, and docs/ops/game-days/results/2026-10-11-region-isolation.json is that local baseline. docs/ops/game-days/README.md:129 lists the quarterly regional drill as 'not run' for the same reason. backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/tests/cross_region.rs:1308::a_dark_region_leaves_a_cell_whose_venues_are_all_at_home_trading_exactly_as_before is in-process only.
decisions.closure: No lane work now, and the status stays MISSING. After a record supersedes ADR 0035 with a second execution region and names its monthly cost, deploy both regions. Then add a region-loss scenario that removes one region from service and control networking. Each quarter, commit docs/ops/game-days/results/<date>-region-loss.json recording three things: the healthy region continued, mirror and recovery behaved, and no cross-region arbitrage leg assumed the missing peer.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. ADR 0035 authorises one region. scripts/game-day/scenarios/region-isolation.json SIGSTOPs qip-fabricd. The 2026-10-11-region-isolation.json result exists. game-days/README.md:129 lists the quarterly drill as 'not run'. cross_region.rs:1308 runs in-process only. The ruling matches R12-GCP-8035 and R12-GCP-8057, which park a second region until a superseding record names its cost. Nothing is spent, and a local drill is not passed off as a region-loss run.

decisions.ruling: The monthly zonal drill runs against a deployed node pair or a deployed quorum, and neither exists. It must prove fencing and quorum, so it needs both halves. The Reflex half waits on the cross-zone lease store and a standby in a second zone (R12-REFLEX-9114, R12-REFLEX-9117). The Fabric half waits on the Spanner managed log, which decision 5 still declines (R12-RES-9169). I will not have a drill record written against machines that do not exist. The row stays MISSING.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/execution-node/main.tf:807 counts the standby only when standby_enabled is set, and no root passes it. standby.rs has no cross-zone LeaseStore. enable_spanner is false in every tfvars (R12-FABRIC-10027), and the R12-RES-9169 ruling puts the managed log's floor at about $2,705 a month and leaves it unfunded. docs/ops/game-days/README.md:128 lists the monthly drill as 'not run' with no node deployed. The R12-REFLEX-9117 and R12-RES-8038 rulings already hold zone-loss and rollout drills until a deployed pair exists.
decisions.closure: No lane work now, and the status stays MISSING. Two things come first: the first execution node runs, and the standby pair (after 9114's lease store) and the managed log (after its pricing ADR) are funded. Then add a monthly zonal-kill scenario beside scripts/game-day/scenarios. Each month, commit docs/ops/game-days/results/<date>-zonal.json recording four things: the old primary's fence lands before the standby activates, quorum-acked records are retained, failover time is measured, and the outcome loss is bounded and measured.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. main.tf:807 gates the standby on standby_enabled, and no root passes it. enable_spanner is false in all four tfvars. README.md:128 lists the monthly drill as 'not run'. The ruling is consistent with R12-REFLEX-9117 and R12-RES-8038 (no drill against machines that do not exist), with R12-RES-9169 (managed log unfunded, $2,705 a month floor) and with R12-REFLEX-9114. Requiring both halves is the conservative reading of 'proves fencing, quorum, failover'.

decisions.ruling: Broker failover closes on a game day against a provisioned Spanner managed log, as I ruled for R12-FABRIC-9118, and decision 5 has not taken that bill. The in-memory kill test and the chaos run are prerequisites, not the evidence. When the bill is taken, the emulator proof of ADR 0111 Amendment 1 comes before any instance. The game day must then record four things: no committed loss, producers retrying by epoch, consumers resuming from committed offsets, and the reflex thread never waiting.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-fabricd/tests/managed.rs:305::a_killed_leader_is_replaced_by_its_follower_with_no_acknowledged_record_lost runs on MemoryManagedLog. tests/chaos.rs::seeded_kills_and_partitions_lose_no_acknowledged_record_and_never_split_an_epoch is in-process. qip-acceptance event_fabric_core_path_exclusions.rs:159::the_reflex_decision_thread_reaches_the_fabric_only_through_a_handoff_it_never_waits_on covers the reflex clause. Consumer resume is proven only across a restart, in qip-ledgerd tests/fabric.rs:916::after_a_restart_the_broker_group_checkpoint_names_the_batch_the_store_cursor_resumes_past, not across a failover. enable_spanner is false in every tfvars and infrastructure/event-fabric/spanner.ddl is unapplied. The R12-FABRIC-9118, R12-FABRIC-8073 and R12-RES-9169 rulings hold the same line.
decisions.closure: A lane may land one prerequisite now. A qip-ledgerd test drives a consumer across a leader kill on a MemoryManagedLog pair and shows it resumes past its committed checkpoint on the promoted follower, with no gap and no duplicate. Mutation: reset the checkpoint on failover, and the test fails. That moves no status. After an ADR prices the managed log and the owner funds it, prove spanner.rs against the emulator, deploy fabricd with the managed log, and run a leader-kill game day. Commit its record, showing no committed loss and consumers resuming from committed offsets.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. managed.rs:305 runs on MemoryManagedLog. chaos.rs:244, event_fabric_core_path_exclusions.rs:159 and qip-ledgerd fabric.rs:916 (restart only) all exist. enable_spanner is false everywhere. The ruling matches R12-FABRIC-9118 and R12-FABRIC-8073: the game day runs on a provisioned Spanner log, with the emulator proof first. The prerequisite test can be built: Broker::tend_leases and MemoryManagedLog are in the qip-streaming library, which is already a dev-dependency of qip-ledgerd, so no app dependency is needed. It moves no status and spends nothing.

decisions.ruling: This row takes R12-RES-8038's ruling. Zone loss is proven on a standby in a second zone, with a lease store it can trust, and on RF3 replicas. None of that is bought before the first node is up. The quorum is the regional Spanner commit (R12-FABRIC-8091), and decision 5 still declines it. The standby's promotion waits on ADR 0137's GCS lease and a second node. The row stays PARTIAL until a zone-loss drill keeps every quorum-acked record and promotes the standby.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/apps/qip-fabricd/src/spanner.rs::SpannerManagedLog implements ManagedLog, and the quorum is delegated under ADR 0111. Nothing provisions the managed log, since enable_spanner = false in every tfvars. standby.rs has only MemoryLeaseStore and FileLeaseStore, and its own doc at :44-55 says no cross-zone store exists. qip-events event_fabric/policy.rs::StreamPolicy::new keeps P2-P4 out of managed_majority. The R12-RES-8038, R12-FABRIC-8091 and R12-REFLEX-9114 rulings set the same conditions.
decisions.closure: No new lane work; the GcsLeaseStore slice is already 9114 and 8069's. The row closes when an ADR prices the managed log and the owner funds it, and the first execution node and a standby in another zone are deployed. A zone-loss game day must then show that every quorum-acked P0/P1 record survives and that the standby promotes over the GCS lease after the old holder's fence lands. Commit that record.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. spanner.rs:364/:492 has SpannerManagedLog implementing ManagedLog. policy.rs keeps managed_majority for P0/P1. standby.rs has only the memory and file stores. The ruling is consistent with R12-RES-8038 and R12-FABRIC-8091 (the RF3 quorum counts only when deployed and funded) and with R12-REFLEX-9114 (the GCS lease is built once in that lane). It adds no lane work and spends nothing.

decisions.ruling: Deployment identity gets its writer and its producer now. A node's identity is the SHA-256 of the qip-edge-node binary its unit starts. The startup script writes it to a read-only file the unit names, and refuses to start if it cannot. The centre's acceptable set is the digest the attested image payload records. qip-api reads it from a declared file. An unset file leaves the item unproduced, as ADR 0155 section 14 says. A file that is named but unreadable stops qip-api. A cell whose clock runs ahead of every venue it measures reads its clock as unavailable. That check uses the existing max_clock_skew and adds no new limit value. Credential expiry stays unreachable on paper (ADR 0155 section 15). No credential is minted to measure it: a real venue credential is a live surface ADR 0003 refuses. The row stays PARTIAL on that clause and does not count 'unreachable' as a measurement.
decisions.rationale: Nothing produces the set. backend/crates/apps/qip-api/src/mesh.rs:904 builds every payload with PolicyPayload::unproduced, and nothing sets acceptable_builds. The consumer is built: qip-edge cell.rs:2924::Cell::deployment_halted and tests/policy_rollback.rs:502::a_cell_whose_build_is_absent_from_a_produced_build_set_takes_no_new_exposure_while_an_unproduced_set_changes_nothing. qip-edge-node main.rs:116 and :593 read QIP_BUILD_IDENTITY_FILE, but startup.sh.tftpl's node.env block at :203 never writes it. infrastructure/images/execution-node/provision.sh:160-183 already checks the payload sha256 and MANIFEST.sha256 before installing /usr/local/bin/qip-edge-node, so the digest is attested. Carrying that digest to the centre needs .github/workflows/image.yml, a protected path (ADR 0155 'Not decided here'). In cell.rs:4318::observe_clock_lead, venue_time.since(capture_time) is clamped at zero, so a cell clock running ahead looks like latency. clock_row at :4352 reads only venue lead. DEFAULT_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW at :503 is 500 ms. SimulatedGateway holds no secret, and ADR 0155 section 15 records credential expiry as unreachable.
decisions.adr_title: A node's build identity is the digest of the binary its unit starts, the centre's acceptable set is the digest the attested image payload records, a cell whose clock runs ahead of every venue reads its clock unavailable under the existing skew bound, and credential expiry stays unreachable on paper (completes ADR 0155 sections 14 and 15)
decisions.closure: After the ADR, lane L1 builds three slices. (1) startup.sh.tftpl writes the sha256 of /usr/local/bin/qip-edge-node to a 0444 file, puts QIP_BUILD_IDENTITY_FILE in node.env, and refuses to boot on failure. Acceptance test in infrastructure.rs: the template writes the digest and names the file. Mutation: drop the line. (2) qip-api reads a declared build-set file into PolicyPayload::acceptable_builds. Test: a declared set is signed into the payload, an unset file leaves it unproduced, and an unreadable file stops start-up. Mutation: ignore the file. (3) qip-edge records the signed lead. clock_row reads Unavailable when every measured venue's stamp trails the cell's receive instant by more than max_clock_skew. Test: a cell whose clock runs ahead of every venue takes no new exposure. Mutation: restore the clamp at zero. The lane must also show that replaying the committed spools is unchanged. The lane writes docs/blueprint/lanes/l1-risk-4101-build-set-protected.patch, in which image.yml publishes the payload's qip-edge-node digest for qip-api. The row stays PARTIAL until a deployed node halts on an absent build and on the credential clause.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. qip-api mesh.rs:904 builds PolicyPayload::unproduced, and nothing sets acceptable_builds. cell.rs:2924 holds deployment_halted, and policy_rollback.rs:502 exists. qip-edge-node main.rs:116/:593 read QIP_BUILD_IDENTITY_FILE, which the node.env block at startup.sh.tftpl:203 never writes. provision.sh:160-173 checks the payload hash and the manifest. observe_clock_lead at cell.rs:4318 clamps the lead at zero, clock_row is at :4352, and DEFAULT_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW is 500 ms at :503. The design follows ADR 0155 sections 14 and 15. Every change narrows: an unreadable file stops qip-api, an absent build halts the cell, and a clock running ahead reads Unavailable under the existing bound. No limit value changes and no credential is minted (ADR 0003). image.yml goes through a lanes patch, and the edited template and crates are unprotected. The row stays PARTIAL until a deployed node halts, so this is not IMPLEMENT dressed over a deployment.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0155 section 19 stands, and the committed universe stays equities. No derivative hedge candidate is declared. Platform::derivative_gate refuses every derivative order until a trading entity holds a jurisdictional permission. That permission is a legal entity's licence, and I cannot grant it under the delegation. A vendor sensitivity feed is a billed subscription I have not bought. I do not commission an in-tree option pricer or a simulated derivatives listing for classes no entity may trade. I also do not read 'permitted' as whatever the empty table permits so that the row passes. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: backend/crates/libs/qip-risk/src/hedge_search.rs:59-71::InstrumentClass names all nine classes. Unit tests cover naming and sizing: every_class_can_be_named_and_a_linear_class_with_convexity_is_refused and an_option_is_sized_through_its_multiplier_and_delta. qip-kernel src/config.rs:840::paper_hedge_candidates declares only CommonStock, as CorrelatedAsset with Greeks::linear. data/datasets/universe.json holds six common_stock records. qip-financial src/derivative_permissions.rs::DerivativePermissions::none starts empty and refuses every derivative type, as blueprint section 13 requires. qip-kernel platform.rs:24196::Platform::derivative_gate refuses a derivative when no derivative_desk is set. Platform::authorise_derivatives (:24184) is called only from tests/asset_classes.rs. A grep finds no option pricer in backend/crates. The R12-COVERAGE-5104 ruling's skeptic notes and the R12-MODEL-4003 licence gating hold the same line.
decisions.closure: No lane work now. gap opens with this ruling. The row reopens only when two things hold. First, a trading entity holds a derivatives permission for a jurisdiction, and the owner records it. Second, an ADR names the admitted classes, and each has a catalogue record under ADR 0155 section 19, with a price printed on the simulated exchange and a sensitivity its record states or an in-tree pricer computes. Then paper_hedge_candidates declares those classes. A kernel test sizes each one through its multiplier and delta. Mutation: drop the multiplier, and the test fails.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. hedge_search.rs:59-71 names nine classes, and the tests are at :1207/:1228. config.rs:840 holds paper_hedge_candidates, and universe.json has six common_stock records. platform.rs:24196 derivative_gate refuses an order when no derivative_desk is set. authorise_derivatives (:24184) is called only from tests/asset_classes.rs:364/368. DerivativePermissions::none refuses everything, as blueprint section 13 requires. No option pricer exists. The ruling is consistent with ADR 0155 section 19 and R12-TICK-1175 (derivative data waits on a licence record). It does not contradict R12-COVERAGE-5104, whose skeptic keeps the committed universe to equities. A jurisdictional permission is a legal-entity matter, so STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL fits.

decisions.ruling: Workforce access through IAP is by Cloud Identity group only. The three IAP lists admit group: and refuse user:, so nobody can write a shared account in as a literal. No-org mode has no Cloud Identity, so there the lists admit nobody, and every committed tfvars already holds empty lists. I add no domain-suffix route for consumer accounts. PAM keeps individual user: principals. Its self-approval refusal compares principals, so a group on both sides would hide one person approving their own grant, and that refusal stays as R12-SEC-8062 left it.
decisions.rationale: Four lists still admit ^(user|group): today: infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf:1684 (gitops_iap_members), modules/iap-run/variables.tf:108, modules/gitops-gateway/variables.tf:73 and PAM at variables.tf:1902. infrastructure/environments/dev/terraform.tfvars:753 sets gitops_iap_members = [], and main.tf:1311 keeps the console's iap_members = [], with operators granted out of band. modules/iap-run/tests tftest.hcl:213 admits user:operator@example.com. qip-acceptance identity_separation.rs:501::every_workforce_access_list_admits_only_managed_cloud_identity_users_and_groups pins the (user|group) pattern. variables.tf:1872 refuses self-approval by setintersection(requesters, approvers), which compares strings and cannot see group membership. infrastructure/foundation/variables.tf::org_id admits null (no-org mode). infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf is a protected path.
decisions.closure: Lane L6 writes docs/blueprint/lanes/l6-sec-10002-group-only-protected.patch. It changes infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf:1684's condition to ^group:[^@:[:space:]]+@[^@:[:space:]]+$ and its error message to 'Cloud Identity group only'. In its own commit, outside protected paths, the lane makes four changes. modules/iap-run/variables.tf:108 and modules/gitops-gateway/variables.tf:73 get the same regex. The iap-run tftest run at :213 becomes an expect_failures run on a user: member, and a new run admits a group:. identity_separation.rs's expected pattern becomes ^group:. decisions.ruling: D12 and ADR 0110 Amendment 1 stand. Every signing key is HSM in every environment. CMEK keys are HSM in stage and prod and may stay SOFTWARE in dev and test. The attestor moves to HSM as a new key beside the old one, never by replacing it: the old key carries prevent_destroy, and replacing it would wedge dev's apply. The old key keeps verifying until every running image is re-attested. Then it is disabled, never destroyed.
decisions.rationale: variables.tf:1100 variable kms_protection_level defaults to SOFTWARE and feeds seven sites: main.tf:249, :605, :632, :875 and :934, build-pool.tf:52 and audit-logs.tf:72. modules/binaryauthorization/main.tf::google_kms_crypto_key.attestor sets version_template.protection_level = var.kms_protection_level and has lifecycle prevent_destroy. billed-plan-2026-10-19.md finding 2 and §4 record that a level change is a replacement, and the replacement stops the apply. The decision is owner-decisions-2026-10-11.md D12 and docs/adr/0110 Amendment 1 item 1. No signing_key_protection_level or cmek_protection_level exists, and no patch for this row exists under docs/blueprint/lanes. variables.tf, build-pool.tf and environments/** are protected. The patch adds validations and an HSM key and loosens nothing, so it is the decision-3 class.
decisions.closure: The lane writes the patch with these changes. variables.tf replaces kms_protection_level with signing_key_protection_level (default and only value HSM) and cmek_protection_level (SOFTWARE or HSM, default HSM, SOFTWARE only when var.environment is dev or test). main.tf passes the signing level to module.binaryauthorization and the CMEK level to secrets, registry, backup and evidence. build-pool.tf:52 and audit-logs.tf:72 take the CMEK level. outputs.tf:379 becomes one output per level. Dev and test tfvars set cmek_protection_level = "SOFTWARE", so no CMEK key is replaced. modules/binaryauthorization adds an HSM attestor key and lists both public keys on the attestor during the overlap. tests/kms-protection.tftest.hcl gains runs that refuse SOFTWARE signing in every environment and SOFTWARE CMEK in stage and prod, and that admit SOFTWARE CMEK in dev and test. Mutation: drop the environment validation and show the stage run fail. The parent applies the patch. The owner applies dev with its billing on, adding one HSM EC key version at about $2.50 a month (the per-key price in billed-plan §3), and re-attests running images before the old key is disabled.
decisions.skeptic: Checked. variables.tf:1100 has kms_protection_level, default SOFTWARE. It reaches seven sites: main.tf:249 (secrets), :605 (registry), :632 (evidence), :875 (binary_authorization) and :934 (backup), plus build-pool.tf:52 and audit-logs.tf:72. Only binaryauthorization's attestor is ASYMMETRIC_SIGN; evidence, backups, build-pool staging and asset_feed are encryption keys, so the split is right. The attestor has prevent_destroy (:77). billed-plan finding 2 and §4 say a level change replaces the key and wedges dev. D12 (owner-decisions-2026-10-11:49) and ADR 0110 Amendment 1 item 1 match the ruling. The §3 price of $2.50 per HSM key version is named, and no existing patch covers this, so WRITE_PATCH is right. Caveat the lane must handle: the closure says main.tf passes the signing level to module.binaryauthorization. Wired naively into the existing attestor key, that replaces it and causes the wedge the ruling forbids. If instead the old key is pinned to SOFTWARE everywhere, test, stage and prod would create a new SOFTWARE signing key on first apply, against D12. So the old SOFTWARE key must be pinned and must exist only in dev, where it is applied, behind a dev-only input. The HSM key must be the only attestor key elsewhere. kms-protection.tftest.hcl must also assert that no SOFTWARE ASYMMETRIC_SIGN key is planned outside dev, not just check the variable. The current default algorithm is RSA_SIGN_PKCS1_4096_SHA512, so the new EC key is a deliberate algorithm change.

decisions.ruling: O18 is declined as written. No agent session gets a Workload Identity pool or a per-run cloud credential, because issuing credentials to agents widens what an agent can reach. The one agent identity the platform declares stays grantless. Every federation that can mint a write-capable identity refuses an agent actor and is bound to the named workflows that run the dispatch judge. An agent that pushes as its person with no marker cannot be told apart. The ADR names that limit openly and does not hide it.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/cicd/main.tf:68 attribute_condition admits every refs/heads/ ref of the repository and maps no actor. github_impersonation (:84) and infra_impersonation (:224) bind principalSet attribute.repository, so any workflow in the repository may impersonate the ci or infra account. main.tf::google_service_account.agent_identity is grantless, held by infrastructure.rs::the_agent_identity_holds_no_run_deploy_or_actas_role (:14231) and ::the_autonomous_agent_service_account_has_no_roles_on_capital_or_custody_resources (:13263). Shells are IAP-only (infrastructure.rs:5419, :13206). Agents are recognised only by scripts/agent-policy.json agent_markers, whose own comment says an unmarked agent push is invisible. This programme's agent branches (ccr-*) match no branch_prefixes entry. This is consistent with R12-CICD-9103, where the refs/heads/ bound stands, and with R12-OBS-9165, where no new credential is issued. A new federation term and narrower bindings change a security contract, so the ADR comes first.
decisions.adr_title: Agent sessions get no cloud principal and no per-run credential; write-capable federation refuses agent actors and is bound to named workflows, and an unmarked agent push is a stated residual
decisions.closure: Lane L6 claims the ADR first. Then in modules/cicd/main.tf it maps attribute.actor, adds to attribute_condition a refusal of every agent_markers.actor_patterns entry, and narrows github_impersonation and infra_impersonation from attribute.repository to the workflows that dispatch_refused_for_agents names. The model-pack publish provider at artefact-signing.tf:372 gets the same actor term. Add workload_identity.rs::every_federation_a_write_capable_account_trusts_refuses_an_agent_actor_and_no_binding_admits_the_whole_repository. Mutations: remove the actor term and show the test fail, then widen one binding back to attribute.repository and show it fail. The row stays PARTIAL until a hosted run shows an agent-actor token refused, and until agents push under a GitHub identity of their own, which the owner creates.
decisions.skeptic: Checked. modules/cicd/main.tf:68 admits any refs/heads/ ref and maps repository, ref and workflow, with no actor mapped. github_impersonation (about :84) and infra_impersonation (about :224) bind principalSet attribute.repository. main.tf:1378 agent_identity has no grants, and infrastructure.rs:14231 and :13263 hold that. The agent_markers comment states that an unmarked agent push is invisible. branch_prefixes are 'claude/' and 'worktree-agent-', so ccr-* matches neither. The model_pack_publish provider is at artefact-signing.tf:364, with its condition at :372. Declining O18 is the conservative reading. It agrees with R12-CICD-9103 (refs/heads/ stands and agent actors never get the credential) and with R12-OBS-9165 (no new credential). The row stays PARTIAL, so nothing is restated to pass. Notes for the lane: (1) attribute.workflow maps the workflow name, not the file, so bind narrowly with workflow_ref or exact names. (2) The CEL refusal of 'claude*' must be case-insensitive, as the markers are. (3) CICD-9103's future plan workflow must be in the named set.
