decisions.ruling: ADR 0112 already decided this: on a Compute Engine hop, the certificate's SAN, mapped to the workload's service account, replaces the bearer token for authorisation. Build it on every fabric route, not only the admin routes. On a mutual-TLS link a bearer token never authorises by itself, and a certificate whose SAN maps to no identity is refused. The CA pool is funded under R12-SEC-10054 and the KMS-held policy keys under R12-SEC-9137, so the row stays PARTIAL until both are deployed.
decisions.rationale: services/qip-streaming/src/event_fabric/service.rs::Service::handle (:384-411) uses the peer name only when the route is AdminIsolate or AdminRelease. On every other route it authorises with auth::verify over the bearer token. ::admission_class (:465) also reads the bearer first. libs/qip-tls/src/lib.rs:47-55 says the replacement is the broker's change. docs/adr/0112 (:43, :78-79) makes the SAN mapped to a service account the identity. ADR 0215 keeps plaintext for the local deployment only. Clause (1) of the gap is stale: libs/qip-transport/src/cas.rs exists, and modules/execution-node/templates/startup.sh.tftpl:220 writes QIP_TLS_MODE=cas. apps/qip-fabricd/tests/broker.rs::an_isolate_request_over_mutual_tls_is_attributed_to_the_certificate_name_and_refused_when_operator_differs covers the admin routes only.
decisions.closure: Change qip-transport event_fabric::auth::IdentityTable so each identity carries its service-account SAN. On a TLS listener, Service::handle and ::admission_class take the identity from the peer SAN on every route. They refuse with 401 when the SAN maps to no identity, and refuse a bearer token that names a different identity. The bearer path remains only on a plaintext local link. Test in apps/qip-fabricd/tests/broker.rs: a produce over mutual TLS whose certificate SAN maps to no identity is refused even with a valid bearer token, and one whose SAN maps to the producer is admitted under that identity. Mutation: restore the admin-only filter in Service::handle and show the first case admitted. Correct clause (1) of the gap in the same change.
decisions.skeptic: Checked. In qip-streaming event_fabric/service.rs, Service::handle uses peer_identity only when the route is AdminIsolate or AdminRelease; every other route goes through auth::verify on the bearer token (around :398-411). admission_class (:465) reads the bearer first. qip-tls/src/lib.rs:47-55 says replacing the bearer is the broker's change. ADR 0112, accepted 2026-10-11, says the SAN mapped to the service account replaces the bearer token (:43, and the Consequences at :78-79). qip-transport/src/cas.rs exists, and startup.sh.tftpl:220 writes QIP_TLS_MODE=cas. IdentityTable is in qip-transport event_fabric/auth.rs:192. broker.rs:1193 covers only the admin routes. The change can be built and tested in process with test certificates, as broker.rs already does. No deployment is needed for it, so IMPLEMENT is right, and the row stays PARTIAL on the CA pool and the keys. Caveat: on a TLS data route, a caller with a mapped SAN and no bearer token is refused today and would be admitted after the change. That is ADR 0112's owner-accepted replacement, not a pure tightening. The lane should cite ADR 0112 for it and keep both new refusals: an unmapped SAN, and a bearer token that names a different identity. The 401 test at broker.rs:868 runs on plaintext and is not weakened.

decisions.ruling: ADR 0113 §4 stands: the scouts' own project comes with the second region, not before, and node pools stay refused under ADR 0114 D4. What I take now is the network. The ingestion-discovery zone gets its own VPC, with no peering, VPN or route to any other network, and it reaches Google APIs only by private access. Its one sanctioned path to cognition goes through a Google-managed API under the zone's own identity, never through a route. Information-source egress leaves through its own router and NAT, which is planned only when a source entry is declared. The row stays PARTIAL on the project half.
decisions.rationale: modules/trust-zones/main.tf local.zone_network (:39-53) puts ingestion-discovery on var.service_network_id together with ten other zones, ledger and treasury-write among them. local.sanctioned_egress_purposes (:141) gives it the only information-source egress, and core_paths 'ingestion-discovery->cognition' (:108) is a firewall path. google_compute_router.egress (:503) refuses egress zones on more than one network (:518), so a separate scout network needs one router per network. Dev declares no ingestion-discovery zone and sets external_egress = {} (dev tfvars:129), so nothing is billed today. billed-plan-2026-10-19.md §5 prices a NAT at $5-$6 a month. This is consistent with R12-GCP-8116 (no node pools, scout job not applied). Moving a zone off the three-network model changes the zone contract, so the ADR comes first.
decisions.adr_title: The scout zone gets its own VPC network with no peering or route to any other network, and its own project waits for the second region

decisions.ruling: O18 is decided once, under R12-SEC-10201's record: no agent identity pool and no per-run cloud credential. An agent run holds the sandbox's contents:read token and nothing else. Every workflow that can mint a Google credential refuses an agent before it authenticates. model-pack-publish.yml mints one and is missing from that list, and I close that gap by patch.
decisions.rationale: .github/workflows/model-pack-publish.yml:94 grants id-token: write and has no agent-guard dispatch step. scripts/agent-policy.json dispatch_refused_for_agents lists deploy, infra, fleet, image, vendor, branch-cleanup and drift, but not model-pack-publish.yml. scripts/agent-guard.test.mjs 'every workflow refused to agents runs the dispatch judge on itself before authenticating' (:466) checks only the listed workflows. Its protected environment's required reviewers are a person's gate, so the patch adds a refusal and repairs nothing that was open. agent-sandbox.yml holds contents:read only, judgeSandboxWorkflow refuses id-token, and R12-SEC-10157 holds the drill. scripts/agent-*, .github/** are protected.
decisions.closure: The patch makes three changes. It adds model-pack-publish.yml to dispatch_refused_for_agents.workflows in scripts/agent-policy.json. It adds the agent-guard.mjs dispatch step (--actor "$who" --workflow model-pack-publish.yml) before google-github-actions/auth in .github/workflows/model-pack-publish.yml. It adds a test to scripts/agent-guard.test.mjs that every .github/workflows file granting id-token: write is listed in dispatch_refused_for_agents. Mutation: remove model-pack-publish.yml from the list and show the new test fail. The parent applies the patch under decision 3, since it adds a refusal. The row stays PARTIAL until R12-SEC-10201's ADR and federation change land, and until agents push under a GitHub identity of their own.
decisions.skeptic: Checked. Only these workflows grant id-token: write: deploy, drift, fleet, image, infra, model-pack-publish (:94) and vendor. Every one except model-pack-publish.yml is in dispatch_refused_for_agents, so the proposed 'every id-token workflow is listed' test passes once the patch lands and breaks no other workflow. ci.yml has no id-token. model-pack-publish.yml authenticates at :254 and has no agent-guard step. agent-guard.test.mjs:466 iterates only the listed workflows. judgeSandboxWorkflow (:556) refuses id-token (:566). The guard step form, --actor "$who" --workflow <file>, matches drift.yml. No existing lanes patch adds this, so WRITE_PATCH is right. It adds a refusal (decision 3 class) and agrees with R12-SEC-10201 and R12-SEC-10157. The lane should order it against R12-MODEL-10084's l2-model-pack-upload.patch, which edits the same workflow.

decisions.ruling: Agents reach models only through the gateway, and only models on a committed approved list. A custom base URL is refused. So that a direct call fails, the gateway runs as its own identity and holds the only model grant, and the worker holds none. No provider key is approved for agents unless it is a Secret Manager secret mounted into the gateway alone. The Vertex preset uses the metadata token and stores no key, and it is the one approved route today. The gateway's identity writes each request's ledger line to a place the worker cannot write.
decisions.rationale: scripts/model-gateway.mjs:204-216 accepts any ALGORIK_WORKER_BASE_URL, and :312 labels it provider 'custom'. No approved-model list exists. run() (:566) appends the ledger with appendFileSync (:571) to the local LEDGER file (:82). infrastructure/fleet/main.tf local.worker_project_roles (:58-61) gives google_service_account.worker roles/aiplatform.user while worker_may_call_models is true (the default), so the worker process can call Vertex directly, around the in-process gateway. The sandbox already refuses every model host (agent-policy.json sandbox.egress_allow, checked by agent-egress.test.mjs). Moving the model grant to a separate identity splits custody under ADR 0102, so the ADR comes first.
decisions.adr_title: Agents reach a model only through a gateway that holds the only model grant under its own identity, admits only a committed model list, and writes a ledger the worker cannot touch
decisions.closure: Now, as a tightening: model-gateway.mjs refuses any provider and model pair that is not in a committed approved list. Test in model-gateway.test.mjs: a custom base URL is refused before anything is sent. Mutation: admit 'custom' again and show the test fail. After the ADR: the gateway runs as its own service account in infrastructure/fleet holding aiplatform.user, and the worker's binding is removed. fleet.tftest.hcl asserts that the worker holds no aiplatform role and that only the gateway identity writes ledger/. The ADR names the gateway service's monthly cost before the fleet apply, which the owner runs.
decisions.skeptic: Checked. model-gateway.mjs accepts ALGORIK_WORKER_BASE_URL (:204-216) and returns provider 'custom' (:312). The ledger is appendFileSync (:571) to LEDGER (:82). In fleet/main.tf, worker_project_roles adds roles/aiplatform.user when worker_may_call_models is true, which is the default (fleet/variables.tf:126). The fleet worker uses the vertex preset (worker.mjs:775), so refusing 'custom' now breaks nothing and only tightens. No test asserts that custom is admitted. Neither model-gateway.mjs nor infrastructure/fleet is a protected path. Moving the model grant to its own identity is a custody change under ADR 0102, so the ADR comes first. The ruling spends nothing now and requires the gateway's cost to be named before the owner's fleet apply. This agrees with R12-CICD-10116, where no model provider enters the sandbox.

decisions.ruling: Every Cloud Armor policy in Terraform carries WAF, adaptive protection and a per-address rate ban, and that stays tested. The one internet-facing surface, the console on run.app, has no policy. It stays on IAP under ADR 0095 until I own and delegate a domain (R12-API-8054). The load balancer and Cloud Armor are billed and unpriced, and the project's Cloud Armor quota is zero. So the row stays PARTIAL, and no other service may go public meanwhile.
decisions.rationale: modules/public-edge/main.tf::google_compute_security_policy.edge (:59, with rules at :68, :98, :109 and :130) and modules/iap-edge/main.tf::google_compute_security_policy.edge (:130) are held by security_controls.rs::every_internet_facing_cloud_armor_policy_enables_layer_7_adaptive_protection (:27) and ::every_internet_facing_cloud_armor_policy_bans_a_client_over_its_rate_with_429_counted_per_address (:600). gitops/envs/dev/portal.yaml:66 sets INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL with no Armor in front. public_edge is commented out at dev tfvars:596. infrastructure/CLAUDE.md:78 records the Cloud Armor quota as 'Limit: 0.0'. admin_surfaces.rs::every_cloud_run_service_in_every_environment_is_internal_or_behind_iap (:124) keeps INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL to the portal alone. dev-redeploy-readiness.md names no LB or Armor cost.
decisions.closure: Correct the gap to name qip-dev-portal as the uncovered surface. The row closes after all of these: the owner delegates a domain, obtains Cloud Armor quota, and names the LB and Armor monthly cost. Then a protected tfvars change sets gitops_portal_hostname (or public_edge) in dev, so the portal sits behind a Cloud Armor policy, and portal.yaml ingress becomes INGRESS_TRAFFIC_INTERNAL_LOAD_BALANCER. A real plan must show this.
decisions.skeptic: Checked. public-edge/main.tf has the policy at :59, adaptive_protection at :68, the WAF sqli and xss rules at :98 and :109, and rate_based_ban with deny(429) at about :120-131. iap-edge/main.tf:130 is the second policy. security_controls.rs:27 and :600 exist. portal.yaml:66 sets INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL with no Armor in front. public_edge is commented out at dev tfvars:596. infrastructure/CLAUDE.md:78 records 'Limit: 0.0'. admin_surfaces.rs:124 limits public ingress to qip-<env>-portal. dev-redeploy-readiness.md gives no LB or Armor cost. This is consistent with R12-SEC-10019 and R12-API-8054. A domain and a quota are external, so STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL is right, and naming the portal as the surface with no policy is honest rather than a restatement.

decisions.ruling: I do not buy the Security Command Center tier. Premium or Enterprise is a billed activation made at the organisation, and it stays declined under decision 5 of 2026-10-25, as R12-GCP-9086 already ruled. Nothing in the repository names its cost. The repository can assert what it already declares at no cost, so the two detectors and the mute configs get a plan test now. The row stays PARTIAL, because aggregation, threats and response integration exist only once the organisation activates a paid tier.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/scc/main.tf declares ::google_scc_management_project_security_health_analytics_custom_module.binary_authorization (:41), .private_endpoint (:80) and ::google_scc_v2_project_mute_config.muted (:114). Each is counted on var.enable_security_command_center. That variable is false in dev tfvars:378 and in test:118, stage:118 and prod:121. modules/scc/ORGANISATION-SCOPED.md says custom Security Health Analytics modules evaluate only under an organisation-activated Premium or Enterprise tier, and that a project cannot activate one. No test asserts the module: modules/scc has no tests directory, and grep finds no tftest and no qip-acceptance test naming it. So the row's plan check ('asserted by a test or plan') fails today, while the parallel SDP control has security.tftest.hcl. dev-redeploy-readiness.md and billed-plan-2026-10-19.md name no SCC cost. A mock-provider plan bills nothing and touches no protected path.
decisions.closure: Add infrastructure/terraform/modules/scc/tests/detectors.tftest.hcl with a mocked google provider. Run 'the two detectors plan only when switched on and watch Binary Authorization and the private endpoint'. With enable_security_command_center = true, it asserts that both custom modules plan with enablement_state ENABLED and resource type container.googleapis.com/Cluster, and that their predicates read binaryAuthorization.evaluationMode and privateClusterConfig.enablePrivateEndpoint. With false, it asserts that no detector and no mute config plans. Mutations: drop either count guard, or change a predicate field; the run must fail on each. Rewrite the gap to name what remains: organisation activation at a paid tier with its monthly cost named first (the organisation administrator's act, declined for now), then the protected dev tfvars flip and a check that findings appear for the project. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. modules/scc/main.tf:41 and :80 are count-gated on var.enable_security_command_center. The mute config at :114 is for_each over var.muted_findings when the switch is on. All four tfvars set the switch false (dev:378, test:118, stage:118, prod:121). modules/scc has no tests directory, and no tftest or qip-acceptance file names scc. A mocked-provider plan bills nothing and touches no protected path. The ruling keeps SCC Premium declined, which is consistent with R12-GCP-9086, and the row stays PARTIAL. The predicates at :64 and :99 match the closure. One caveat for the lane: muted_findings defaults to {}, so 'no mute config plans when false' is vacuous as written. Both runs should set one muted_findings entry, and a mutation should drop the for_each guard.

The inspect template is at :420, the de-identify template at :442 and discovery_config.lake at :463. tests/security.tftest.hcl sets sensitive_data_protection = {} at :92, asserts RUNNING at :149 and holds a_discovery_scan_for_nothing_is_refused at :305. decisions.ruling: I do not grant the tick desk qip-simulated-depth. Simulator output is not a training source (R12-MODEL-4007, R12-MODEL-4004), and this desk trains fill-probability and volatility models. It stays off until a market dataset is admitted under an ADR 0157 licence record. The invariant is not read down to the tick desk alone: the deep brain's replayed-bar fit also trains on replayed market data, and its rows carry no sequence, so it gets the same guard now.
decisions.rationale: The tick desk side is built. qip-training microstructure.rs::MicroExample carries sequence (:148), and qip-deepbrain tests/tick_desk.rs:489 every_training_row_carries_its_venue_sequence_and_entitlement tests it. The desk is off: tick_desk.rs:73 EVERY_VARIABLE, and qip-acceptance manifest_wiring.rs:2470 THE_TICK_DESK_IS_OFF_UNTIL_ENTITLED. Dev deepbrain.yaml sets no QIP_DEEPBRAIN_TICK_* variable and runs QIP_STORAGE_TARGET=memory. The triage's grant would be qip-edge-node feed.rs:128 SIMULATED_DATASET, granted at :132 because 'nothing was licensed'. That contradicts R12-MODEL-4007 and R12-MODEL-4004. The other path is qip-deepbrain main.rs:508-570, which composes the evolution engine over ReplayAdapter under QIP_DEEPBRAIN_REPLAY_PATH. There learning.rs::fit (:2158) calls TrainingDataset::new(name, names, rows, targets, times), and qip-training dataset.rs:25 holds no sequence. features.rs::source_digest does not hash the bar order beyond close time.
decisions.closure: In qip-deepbrain learning.rs::fit, keep one lineage entry per row beside the TrainingDataset. Each entry holds Bar.venue, the bar's order key (open_time and interval within its venue and instrument), and the round's entitlement: the StandingAdmission's source, or the synthetic exchange's generated source. Refuse the fit when two rows share an order key or run backwards. Record the first and last order key in ModelCard::parameters. TrainingDataset's shape and source_digest stay unchanged. Test 'a replayed bar fit carries its sequence on every row and refuses a repeated or backward bar'. Mutation: accept a repeated order key; the test must fail. The row stays PARTIAL until a licensed dataset turns the tick desk on in a deployment. Lane L3b; the same change carries R12-TICK-1050 and R12-TICK-1051.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. MicroExample.sequence is at microstructure.rs:148 and the test at tests/tick_desk.rs:489. EVERY_VARIABLE is at tick_desk.rs:73 and THE_TICK_DESK_IS_OFF_UNTIL_ENTITLED at manifest_wiring.rs:2470. Dev deepbrain.yaml sets no TICK_* variable and sets QIP_STORAGE_TARGET=memory. feed.rs:128 has SIMULATED_DATASET. main.rs:508-570 runs ReplayAdapter under StandingAdmission. learning.rs::fit at :2158 builds TrainingDataset::new at :2203 with no lineage, and source_digest hashes no venue. The requirement's own check says 'a training dataset built from replayed market data', so extending the guard to the bar fit follows the text and is not scope creep. Refusing simulated depth for training matches R12-MODEL-4007 and R12-MODEL-4004. It does not contradict R12-WORLD-3046 (a non-training read) or ADR 0181 (raw retention only). Notes: dataset.rs already refuses backward times, so the new part is the duplicate-key refusal. learning.rs:453 is a field doc; the door refusal is at :619.

decisions.ruling: As on R12-TICK-1049: no simulated depth is granted to the tick desk, and it waits for a market dataset admitted under ADR 0157. The deep brain's replayed-bar fit is market-data training too. Its rows lose the venue that every Bar carries, so each row now keeps it, and a bar with no venue is refused.
decisions.rationale: MicroExample.venue (qip-training microstructure.rs:147) is set on every tick-desk row. tests/tick_desk.rs:489 asserts venue == XLON. The desk stays off for the reason given on R12-TICK-1049 (R12-MODEL-4007, R12-MODEL-4004). In the bar path, qip-market bar.rs::Bar has a venue field (:70). But learning.rs::fit puts only rows, targets and times into TrainingDataset (dataset.rs:25). features.rs::source_digest omits venue, and learning.rs records no venue on the card. So a dataset built from replayed bars (main.rs:508-570, QIP_DEEPBRAIN_REPLAY_PATH) loses venue identity.
decisions.closure: Use the same lineage entries as R12-TICK-1049 in learning.rs::fit. Refuse the fit when a row's venue is empty or differs from the first row's, and record training_venue in ModelCard::parameters. Test 'a replayed bar fit carries its venue on every row and refuses a bar with none or a second venue'. Mutation: drop the venue check; the test must fail. The row stays PARTIAL until a licensed dataset turns the tick desk on in a deployment.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. Bar.venue is at bar.rs:70. features.rs:140 source_digest hashes close time and OHLCV only. TrainingDataset (dataset.rs:25) and learning.rs record no venue. The empty-venue refusal will not stop dev fits, because synthetic bars set venue (synthetic/mod.rs:597, book.rs:196). The change is a refusal added on the same lineage entries, so it only tightens. The row stays PARTIAL on the licence, consistent with R12-MODEL-4007 and R12-MODEL-4004.

decisions.ruling: As on R12-TICK-1049: qip-simulated-depth is not granted, and the tick desk's entitlement waits for a licence record under ADR 0157. The deep brain's replayed-bar fit already asks the connector's admission every round, but nothing about it reaches the rows or the card. From now on each row carries the entitlement it was read under, and a round with none trains nothing.
decisions.rationale: MicroExample.entitlement (microstructure.rs:149) is set on every tick-desk row, and an unentitled observation is refused. tests/tick_desk.rs:489 asserts entitlement == vendor-depth. The desk refuses to start without QIP_DEEPBRAIN_TICK_ENTITLEMENTS (tick_desk.rs:153-165). In the bar path, main.rs:536-570 holds a StandingAdmission per round for a replay that names its connector, and learning.rs:453 refuses a door that is neither admitted nor generated. Still, grep finds no entitlement or licence in learning.rs, so the fitted card and rows do not say what terms the data was read under.
decisions.closure: Use the same lineage entries as R12-TICK-1049 in learning.rs::fit. Each row carries the round's entitlement (the admission's source, or the generated synthetic source). Refuse the fit when the round has none, and record training_entitlement in ModelCard::parameters. Test 'a replayed bar fit names the entitlement it was read under on every row and on its card, and a round with none fits nothing'. Mutation: fit with no entitlement; the test must fail. The row stays PARTIAL until a licensed dataset turns the tick desk on in a deployment.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. MicroExample.entitlement is at microstructure.rs:149, and the refusal of an observation with no venue or entitlement is at :198. main.rs:536-570 opens a StandingAdmission per replay that names its connector. A grep for entitle or licen in learning.rs finds nothing, so neither the card nor the rows record terms. The refusal itself is at learning.rs:619, not :453, which is a doc comment. Recording training_entitlement in ModelCard::parameters (registry.rs:256) and refusing a fit with no entitlement are both tightenings.

decisions.ruling: The guard stands as built, and the desk stays off. I do not grant it simulated depth (my ruling on R12-TICK-1049), so the row waits for a market dataset admitted under an ADR 0157 licence record. Its verification names two crates that do not hold the guard, and that text is corrected now.
decisions.rationale: qip-deepbrain tick_desk.rs::TickDesk::round (:560) excludes ticks with knowable_at < event_time from replay and training, and counts them. tests/tick_desk.rs:549 a_tick_received_before_it_happened_is_excluded_from_replay_and_counted is that guard's test. The deep brain's bar fit has its own as-of guard: learning.rs::audit_features_as_of (:2454) refuses any feature that reads a bar after its decision instant. MARKET_PREFIX is read only at tick_desk.rs:597, and the desk is off in every committed deployment (manifest_wiring.rs:2470). The register's verification is 'cargo test -p qip-simulation-engine; cargo test -p qip-execution-engine', and neither crate holds this guard. Granting simulator depth would contradict R12-MODEL-4007.
decisions.closure: Replace the verification with 'cargo test -p qip-deepbrain --test tick_desk', and cite tests/tick_desk.rs:549 and learning.rs::audit_features_as_of in the evidence. The gap opens with: a market dataset admitted under an ADR 0157 licence record, and the desk switched on over it in a deployment. Nothing is coded before that.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. TickDesk::round is at tick_desk.rs:560, and the knowable_at < event_time exclusion is at :634. The test a_tick_received_before_it_happened_is_excluded_from_replay_and_counted is at tests/tick_desk.rs:549. audit_features_as_of is at learning.rs:2454. MARKET_PREFIX is used only at tick_desk.rs:597. The register's verification really is 'cargo test -p qip-simulation-engine; cargo test -p qip-execution-engine' (assessment/R12-M1.json), and neither crate holds the guard. Correcting it is text. STAY_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL on a licensed dataset matches 1049-1051 and R12-MODEL-4007.

decisions.ruling: No vendor is chosen now for options chains, Greeks, futures curves, basis, borrow or funding. Each enters only as an ADR 0157 licence record, and options stay refused under ADR 0050. A free public-record curve enters the same way, as a record that quotes its terms, never by an agent reading the terms in my name. I ruled the same on R12-TICK-1175 and R12-TICK-2046, and it holds here. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: qip-market src/volatility.rs and src/curve.rs are typed and tested (tests/volatility.rs). Nothing calls them from a feed. qip-market-ingestion connector_feed.rs::KNOWN_SOURCES holds no options, futures, borrow or funding source. ADR 0157:362 lists 'R12-TICK-2045 - BILLED vendor choice, as TICK-1175'. ADR 0157:402 records four option publishers read and refused. ADR 0157:390 lists public-record curve series as candidates whose terms are unread. R12-RISK-4096 keeps borrow fail-closed until a licensed borrow source is admitted. The row's verification, 'cargo test -p qip-twin --test twin', tests none of these types.
decisions.closure: Now: replace the verification with an inspection test that maps each named type to its typed record and capture path. It carries a named pending list of the unlicensed types and fails when the list and the tree disagree, so it never lands red (the R12-TICK-1175 skeptic's form). After the owner commits a licence record per source under ADR 0157: an adapter in qip-market-ingestion behind the licence gate fills VolatilitySurface or Curve, with a capture test per type.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. qip-market src/volatility.rs, src/curve.rs and tests/volatility.rs exist. KNOWN_SOURCES (connector_feed.rs:51-59) holds no options, futures, borrow or funding source. ecb_key_rates and nyfed_effr are policy rates, as the R12-TICK-2046 skeptic noted. ADR 0157 has the row at :362, unread candidate curve series at :390, and refused option publishers at :402-404. The register's verification is 'cargo test -p qip-twin --test twin', and it tests none of these types. The decision is consistent with R12-TICK-1175 and R12-TICK-2046, and the inspection test with a named pending list never lands red. Kernel valuation.rs reads TermStructure, but no feed fills it, so 'nothing calls them from a feed' holds.

decisions.ruling: The immutability is built and tested, and the row waits only for a durable store. Cloud Storage stays off until the change that lands its first writer, after the dev deploy, because the archive's seven-year lock cannot be undone (R12-DATA-8125). The four dev buckets cost about $0.30 to $6 a month, and this ruling funds nothing. When the store is on, the lake writes to the bucket that R12-TICK-2056's record names.
decisions.rationale: qip-storage lake.rs::Lake::write_segment seals through BlobStore::put_if_absent (:328, raw bytes at :321). tests/lake.rs:240 two_writers_racing_one_segment_id_seal_exactly_one and tests/gcp.rs:1089 a_cloud_storage_put_if_absent_asks_for_generation_zero_and_reads_412_as_already_there test it. The only lake writer is qip-edge-node's LakeSink (main.rs:1289, over config.storage.blobs(LAKE_NAMESPACE)), and no node is enabled in dev. Dev deepbrain.yaml runs QIP_STORAGE_TARGET=memory. enable_cloud_storage = false in dev:364, test:109, stage:109 and prod:112, all protected tfvars. billed-plan-2026-10-19.md prices the switch as item 2 ($0.30 to $6) and warns in finding 3 that the 2557-day archive lock is irreversible.
decisions.closure: The gap opens with: no durable Cloud Storage lake. Its cost is $0.30 to $6 a month (billed-plan-2026-10-19.md item 2). The trigger is the owner setting enable_cloud_storage = true in dev tfvars, after the dev deploy, in the change that lands the first writer. In that change the lake namespace points at the market bucket from R12-TICK-2056. The row closes on deployed evidence: a second seal refused against the real bucket (412 read as already there), and a manifest re-materialised from it to matching checksums.
decisions.skeptic: The outcome (off until the first writer, $0.30 to $6, billed-plan item 2, irreversible lock) is right. The closure, though, moves irreplaceable history out of the lock. The closure says 'the lake namespace points at the market bucket from R12-TICK-2056'. But qip-storage maps every namespace of a process into one bucket: provider.rs:443-450 uses one QIP_CLOUD_STORAGE_BUCKET (gcp/mod.rs:99) with the namespace as a key prefix. One Lake namespace holds both RecordClass::Market and RecordClass::Internal (lake.rs:74, :177). qip-api main.rs:123 and deepbrain main.rs:105 seal internal outcomes into that same lake through with_outcome_lake. The deep brain also writes model-artifacts, knowledge-packs, reflex-packages and tick-desk output through the same storage config. Pointing the lake, and so the process, at the unlocked market bucket would take internal history out of the seven-year locked archive. The archive's own lifecycle rules keep lake/class=internal/ there (modules/data/main.tf:226). That loosens the irreplaceable class and contradicts R12-TICK-2056's own 'the locked archive keeps the classes that never delete'. Corrected closure: in the R12-TICK-2055 switch change, only market-class lake partitions reach R12-TICK-2056's bucket, through the class routing the corrected R12-TICK-2056 builds. Internal-class partitions and every other namespace stay on the locked archive. The deployed evidence then also shows an internal segment sealed in the archive.

decisions.ruling: The row's 'not built' is stale: the lifecycle rules and the entitlement-scoped reads exist. But the market-class delete is declared on the event-archive bucket, and its retention is locked for seven years. Cloud Storage does not delete an object a retention policy still holds, so market history would be kept for seven years, longer than its entitlement allows. Market-class lake partitions go to their own bucket with no locked retention, keeping the same 30-day Coldline move and 90-day delete. The locked archive keeps only the classes that never delete. Storage stays off, so this bills nothing until the R12-TICK-2055 switch.
decisions.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/modules/data/main.tf::google_storage_bucket.archive (:161) sets retention_policy is_locked = true for var.archive_retention_days, which defaults to 2557 (modules/data/variables.tf:215). The same resource carries the lifecycle_rule Delete at age 90 on lake/class=market/ (:210-217). tests/retention_classes.tftest.hcl market_data_lifecycle_plan asserts that rule on that bucket with archive_retention_days = 2555. qip-acceptance data_infrastructure_guards.rs:175-208 checks only the text. The entitlement half is built: qip-storage lake_history.rs::HistoryQuery withholds ungranted entitlements, tested by tests/lake_history.rs:195 a_segment_under_an_ungranted_entitlement_is_withheld_and_never_read. Prior rulings agree: R12-DATA-8019 keeps the archive transition-only, and R12-DATA-8125 keeps storage off until a writer lands. Splitting the bucket changes the data module's layout and where the lake lives, so it needs a record.
decisions.adr_title: Market-class lake partitions live in their own bucket with no locked retention so their ninety-day delete fires, and the locked event archive holds only classes that never delete
decisions.closure: Claim the ADR in docs/adr/README.md. In modules/data/main.tf, add google_storage_bucket.lake_market behind enable_cloud_storage. It has uniform access, enforced public-access prevention, the archive KMS key and no locked retention. Move the lake/class=market/ 30-day Coldline rule and 90-day Delete rule into it unchanged. The archive keeps the lake/class=internal/ and lake/ transitions. Retarget market_data_lifecycle_plan at the new bucket and keep every assertion. Add run 'a delete rule never sits on a bucket whose locked retention outlasts it': it iterates every bucket and fails when a Delete's age is shorter than a locked retention period. Add the same check to data_infrastructure_guards.rs. Mutation: move the market Delete back into the archive; both must fail. Correct the gap to name only this split and the R12-TICK-2055 switch. The row stays PARTIAL until a deployed lake shows a market object deleted and an internal one kept.
decisions.skeptic: The diagnosis is right and the split is the right reading. archive (main.tf:161) is locked at var.archive_retention_days (default 2557, variables.tf:215), and the market Delete at age 90 (:210-217) sits inside it. GCS does not delete an object its retention policy still holds. The closure is Terraform-only, though, and the code cannot use the new bucket. Each process has one QIP_CLOUD_STORAGE_BUCKET, and every namespace is a prefix in it (provider.rs:443-450). The lake is one namespace holding both classes (lake.rs:74, :177). The deep brain reads market history (tick desk) and seals internal outcomes (main.rs:105, :1017) on the same lake. So google_storage_bucket.lake_market would plan, the retargeted test would pass, and market segments would still land in the locked archive. That makes the requirement pass on paper only. The new invariant is also mis-specified: GCS blocks a Delete under any retention policy, locked or unlocked, so 'fails when a Delete's age is shorter than a locked retention' misses an unlocked long policy. Corrected closure: keep the ADR, the bucket and the moved rules. In qip-storage, route a lake partition by RecordClass: market to a market-class bucket setting, internal to the archive. Lake::write_market_segment and HistoryQuery use the market store, and seal_internal_outcomes uses the archive store. Test 'a market segment and an internal segment from one lake land in different stores, and history reads market segments from the market store'. Mutation: one store for both. The tftest and data_infrastructure_guards.rs check compare every Delete age against any retention_policy period, locked or not. Give lake_market an unlocked retention shorter than its Delete, as segments (:317, 7 days under a 30-day Delete) and simulation (:356, 30 days under 90) already do, so a market segment stays write-once during its life. Storage stays off, consistent with R12-DATA-8125 and R12-DATA-8019.

decisions.ruling: No automatic channel carries a deep-brain promotion to the policy issuer. A distillate the deep brain promotes reaches qip-api's trained_models slot only through the two-person release. Its signed pack names the promotion, and qip-api admits the promotion only from a verified pack, so an unreleased model never enters a manifest. The model bytes still ride in the compiled plan baked into the node image (R12-MODEL-1083), and activation stays the pack's (R12-MODEL-10180). The row stays PARTIAL until a deployed cell installs one.
decisions.rationale: qip-training distill.rs:311 distil states fidelity, and the deep brain's learning desk distils and journals its ModelPromotion into its own log. qip-kernel model_serving.rs::resume_model_promotions (:716) reads only the process's own EventLog (platform.rs:6324). qip-api main.rs:265-270 says the process 'trains and promotes no model'. model_serving.rs::model_manifest_targeted (:1366) already withholds a promotion that has no matching release pack. qip-contracts policy.rs:406 ModelPack carries artifact_digest, inline_model, budget_microseconds and publication inside its signed bytes. Outside qip-kernel, grep finds ModelPromotion only in qip-deepbrain, and no fabric topic or shared store carries it. A shared store is billed, and fabricd is undeployed. The pack route adds neither and fails closed. It changes the pack's signed contract, so it needs a record, in line with R12-MODEL-10180's extension of signing_payload.
decisions.adr_title: A deep-brain distillate reaches the policy issuer only inside its two-person signed pack, and the issuer names no model a verified pack has not released
decisions.closure: Claim the ADR. Then qip-cli model-pack takes the deep brain's journaled ModelPromotion by artifact digest and puts its distilled entry and permitted locations into the pack's signed bytes. It refuses a promotion with no permitted locations. In qip-api, qip-kernel admits a promotion into model_promotions from a verified pack (model_trust.rs) and from nothing else. Acceptance test 'a deep-brain distillate reaches the trained_models slot only through a verified two-person pack, and the cell installs it'. The deep brain distils and promotes. The slot is empty before release and names the model by the cell's digest after. The cell installs a plan carrying it. Mutations: admit a promotion without a verified pack; drop the hand-off. Each must fail. Any model-pack-publish.yml change is written as docs/blueprint/lanes/<lane>-*.patch. Depends on R12-MODEL-10180 and R12-MODEL-1083. Deployment evidence follows the owner's node switch.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. resume_model_promotions is at model_serving.rs:716 and model_manifest_targeted at :1366. qip-api main.rs:265-270 says the process 'trains and promotes no model'. ModelPack (policy.rs:406) carries artifact_digest, budget_microseconds, publication and inline_model in signing_payload. model_trust.rs and qip-cli model_pack.rs exist, and ModelPromotion appears only in qip-kernel and qip-deepbrain. The route bills nothing, fails closed, and depends on R12-MODEL-10180 and R12-MODEL-1083 without contradicting them. The plan with its inline model is baked into the image, per the 1083 decision. The workflow change goes out as a lanes patch. One correction: the rationale overstates the current gate. model_manifest_targeted withholds an unreleased distillate only when release_packs is Some (:1397). With None, every promotion is named. The closure's 'admits a promotion only from a verified pack' fixes that, so it is load-bearing, not a restatement.

decisions.ruling: Each kind of mismatch gets one paper-only consumer, named before anything carries it (ADR 0151 decision 1). An Investigation opens a question in the deep brain's research backlog. An EvidenceQualityChallenge becomes a discovery target asking for better evidence, and it may only lower the weight of the evidence it challenges. A RelativeValueHypothesis enters falsification as a proposed hypothesis, charged to its family's trial budget, and sizes nothing until it climbs the whole promotion ladder. None reaches an order. The row stays PARTIAL until the tick desk runs on a licensed dataset.
decisions.rationale: qip-kernel fusion.rs:226 Mismatch has Investigation, RelativeValueHypothesis and EvidenceQualityChallenge, and FusedState::mismatches is at :722. qip-deepbrain tick_desk.rs:859 only counts them into TickRound.mismatches: usize (:331), and grep finds no Mismatch:: consumer in qip-deepbrain src. qip-kernel falsification.rs has no mismatch intake. qip-data-finder discovery_targets.rs is not called from the cycle. ADR 0151 decision 1 requires a named consumer, and ADR 0125 lets an advisory stage only veto or narrow. The desk is off until entitled (manifest_wiring.rs:2470), and my R12-TICK-1049 ruling keeps it off until a licensed dataset exists.
decisions.adr_title: A world/market mismatch has one paper-only consumer per kind: an investigation opens a research question, an evidence challenge asks discovery for a better source and may only lower that evidence's weight, and a relative-value hypothesis enters falsification as proposed and sizes nothing
decisions.closure: Claim the ADR. Then carry the mismatches themselves on TickRound, not a count, and dispatch them in node.rs after tick_pass. An Investigation becomes a research-backlog entry. An EvidenceQualityChallenge becomes a discovery_targets target plus a narrowing of that evidence's weight. A RelativeValueHypothesis goes to the falsification intake as Proposed, charged to its TrialLedger, with no size. Integration test over a recorded world event and its tick reaction: 'a recorded world/market mismatch reaches its named consumer, and a relative-value hypothesis sizes nothing'. Mutations: drop each consumer's dispatch, one at a time; the test must fail on each.
decisions.skeptic: Verified. The Mismatch variants are at fusion.rs:226, and FusedState::mismatches at :722. tick_desk.rs:859 only counts them into TickRound.mismatches: usize (:331). No Mismatch consumer exists in qip-deepbrain src, falsification.rs has no mismatch intake, and ResearchBacklog (cognition.rs) and TrialLedger exist. Each consumer is paper-only and narrow-only, and the relative-value hypothesis sizes nothing, which is consistent with decision 7 and ADR 0125. One misread does not change the outcome: discovery_targets is called from the cycle. qip-kernel source_discovery.rs:140 Platform::discovery_targets calls it, platform.rs:24358 reads it, and deepbrain discovery.rs uses it. The EvidenceQualityChallenge consumer should feed that existing path, and the rationale's 'not called from the cycle' should be dropped.

decisions.ruling: The Asset, Capital and Risk brains are not new components. The Asset brain is the foundry's per-subject search, and a posterior may change only how many candidates a round proposes, each one charged to the trial ledger. The Risk brain is REASON's OutsidePrior seam, which only narrows (ADR 0151 decision 3). Capital does not read a fused posterior, because nothing new is sized under decision 7 of 2026-10-25. That clause and the specialist brains' clause stay unmet and are written down as unmet. The row stays PARTIAL.
decisions.rationale: qip-deepbrain node.rs:685 calls platform.set_outside_priors(desk.outside_priors()), and node.rs:728 calls engine.set_priors(desk.posteriors()). Neither hand-off has a test: grep finds neither set_priors nor outside_priors in qip-deepbrain/tests or node.rs tests. qip-kernel central/foundry.rs::search_with_prior (:252) proposes count x (0.5 + prior), refuses a non-probability, and counts the draws in the trial ledger. It is tested by tests/foundry.rs:527 and by evolution.rs:3043 a_fused_posterior_handed_to_the_engine_sizes_the_round_it_runs. qip-kernel tests/outside_prior.rs pins the REASON seam. qip-deepbrain brains.rs registers no asset, capital or risk brain. Posteriors are keyed by watch-graph instrument names, and evolution subjects by ObjectId. R12-CAPITAL-4085 keeps capital proposers unable to widen a grant. A posterior-driven capital input would be a new sizing input, which decision 7 declines.
decisions.adr_title: The fused posterior's Asset and Risk consumers are the foundry's per-subject search and REASON's narrowing seam, and Capital and the specialist brains do not read it while nothing new is sized
decisions.closure: Claim the ADR. Add a qip-deepbrain test 'a tick round's posteriors reach the next evolution round and its outside priors reach REASON'. Mutations: delete node.rs:728 set_priors, then delete node.rs:685 set_outside_priors; the test must fail on each. Make a posterior whose watch-graph instrument names no evolution subject counted and reported on the round line, never silently neutral. Test 'a posterior keyed by a name no subject carries is counted, and one keyed by the subject's own id sizes its round'. Mutation: match on a display name; the test must fail. The gap records Capital and the specialist brains as unmet by decision 7, and the desk as off until a licensed dataset exists (R12-TICK-1049).
decisions.skeptic: Verified. node.rs:685 calls set_outside_priors and node.rs:728 calls set_priors, and qip-deepbrain/tests tests neither. foundry.rs:252 is search_with_prior, tested by tests/foundry.rs:527 and by evolution.rs:3043. tests/outside_prior.rs exists. Platform::set_outside_priors (platform.rs:12125) caps the priors. brains.rs registers no asset, capital or risk brain. Keeping Capital off the posterior matches decision 7 (2026-10-25) and R12-CAPITAL-4085. The new tests and the counted unmatched-key report only tighten, and recording the unmet clauses does not restate the requirement so that it passes.

decisions.ruling: The tick archive stays where R12-DATA-8125 left it. enable_cloud_storage stays off until the change that lands the first archive writer, because the archive bucket's seven-year lock cannot be undone; its bill of about $0.30 to $6 a month is not the reason to wait. Compression follows ADR 0113 Amendment 1 and nothing else: zstd becomes the default only in the change that commits the bytes-per-day and drain-thread measurement (R12-TICK-2057), and it stays Identity if that measurement shows spool pressure rising. The row stays PARTIAL until a deployed bucket holds a compressed, manifested, entitled partition.
decisions.rationale: Manifests and entitlements are built and refuse at read: qip-storage src/lake.rs::Lake::write_manifest/read_manifest/verify, tests/lake.rs::a_partition_without_an_entitlement_cannot_be_formed, tests/tick_capture.rs::an_entitlement_without_a_retention_right_is_refused_and_counted. Compression exists but is off: qip-storage src/lake_codec.rs::SegmentCodec (Zstd variant), and qip-edge-node src/event_fabric/drain.rs::CODEC_VARIABLE documents identity as the default. qip-edge-node main.rs parses it with an empty default. The measuring tool exists: qip-deepbrain src/tick_desk.rs::MEASURE_CODEC_VARIABLE with lake_codec::measure_partitions. ADR 0113 Amendment 1 makes zstd the default only together with a committed measurement, and voids the flip if spool pressure rises. Storage is off: infrastructure/environments/dev/terraform.tfvars:364 enable_cloud_storage = false (protected), and modules/data/main.tf google_storage_bucket.archive has is_locked = true (:189) for archive_retention_days. infrastructure/gitops/envs/dev/deepbrain.yaml:76-77 sets QIP_STORAGE_TARGET=memory. docs/blueprint/lanes/billed-plan-2026-10-19.md §2 prices it at $0.30-$6 and says 'Defer until a writer lands'; neither the runbook nor the row names a cost, so FUND is unavailable. This matches R12-DATA-8125 ('Storage stays off until the change that lands the first writer') and R12-TICK-2057's gap.
decisions.closure: Nothing is built under this ruling. The row reopens in this order. (1) R12-TICK-2057's change commits the bytes/day and drain-thread measurement and flips the CODEC_VARIABLE default to zstd at a fixed level. It also sets QIP_TICK_LAKE_CODEC explicitly in the execution-node template, or keeps Identity if spool pressure rises. (2) R12-DATA-8125's first archive writer lands with its plan assertions. (3) The owner flips enable_cloud_storage in the protected dev tfvars, which accepts the seven-year lock, then plans and applies. (4) An integration run on dev reads back one archived partition that is compressed, carries a manifest and an entitlement, and refuses a copy stripped of either.
decisions.skeptic: All citations check out. lake.rs has write_manifest:419, read_manifest:431 and verify:441. tests/lake.rs:42 and tests/tick_capture.rs:126 exist. lake_codec.rs has SegmentCodec:53 with Zstd:59 and measure_partitions:248. drain.rs:615 CODEC_VARIABLE documents identity as the default, and edge-node main.rs:1273 parses it with unwrap_or_default. tick_desk.rs:81 MEASURE_CODEC_VARIABLE exists. dev tfvars:364 has enable_cloud_storage = false, and the flag is false in all four tfvars. modules/data/main.tf:189 has is_locked = true. gitops dev deepbrain.yaml:76-77 sets QIP_STORAGE_TARGET=memory. billed-plan §2 says '$0.30 to $6' and 'Defer until a writer lands', and says the lock, not the cost, is the reason to wait. ADR 0113 Amendment 1 (:175-192) says zstd becomes the default only with the measurement committed in the same change, the default stays Identity if spool pressure rises, and the execution node's template sets the variable explicitly. The ruling matches this and the R12-TICK-2057 gap. It is consistent with R12-DATA-8125 ('Storage stays off until the change that lands the first writer'). The cost is not named in the runbook or the row, so STAY_PARTIAL_DEPLOY is right. The tfvars flip is left to the owner, and the execution-node template under modules/execution-node/templates is not a protected path. Nothing is loosened.

decisions.ruling: Replay shards run as a Cloud Run Job, as D4 of 2026-10-11 and ADR 0114 Amendment 1 already decided, and it is the same job R12-TICK-7020 funds, not a second one. It comes after dev runs and after I fund that job at its ceiling of about $105 a month; decision 5 stands until then. A shard re-scores the declined and filled paths from the tape with the corrected twin. It never compares against a regret journaled before decision 9's direction fix. The row stays PARTIAL until a plan and an apply show the job.
decisions.rationale: Replay and counterfactual scoring exist only in-process: qip-kernel src/session_replay.rs::replay, ReplayOutcome and from_archive (archived segments are already readable), and qip-edge-node src/replay.rs::replay. infrastructure/terraform/catalogue.tf has no replay entry, and no google_cloud_run_v2_job exists under infrastructure/terraform (R12-TICK-7020's skeptic verified this; the only job is in infrastructure/fleet). R12-TICK-7020 was ruled FUND_THEN_DEPLOY at $105: the runbook's figure (dev-redeploy-readiness.md §5, qip-dev-fastbrain min 1, 2 vCPU/2Gi) behind an enable_replay_pool switch that ships off. docs/blueprint/lanes/billed-plan-2026-10-19.md §10 estimates sharded runs at $0-$15 and needs the segments bucket from §2, which stays off under R12-DATA-8125. Decision 5 of 2026-10-25 declines 'new replay and solver pools' before the deploy. Decision 9 of 2026-10-31 records that DeclinedScore/FillScore regret written before the twin fix is inverted. root variables.tf and the dev tfvars are protected.
decisions.closure: After dev runs and the owner funds R12-TICK-7020's job, one replay-job module serves both rows. It is gated by TICK-7020's enable_replay_pool, with the variables.tf declaration and the dev tfvars line in one protected patch. Each shard runs a replay entry point that reads archived segments through session_replay's from_archive, recomputes declined and filled scores with the corrected twin, and journals one live-versus-counterfactual comparison per shard. A lane may land that entry point earlier as code, proven against an archive directory, with this test: 'two shards over disjoint segments together reproduce the single-process replay's comparison'. Mutation: drop one shard's segments. A tftest checks the job shares no service or identity with serving, then a real plan and apply follow. It needs enable_cloud_storage on (R12-DATA-8125) for archived segments.
decisions.skeptic: The decision class is right, but the rationale and closure misread the code. (1) There is no from_archive in qip-kernel src/session_replay.rs; a grep finds only qip-edge-node src/replay.rs:166 RecordedSession::from_archive(reader: &ArchiveReader, ..). That is the edge node's own session type, and it re-drives node passes (run_pass, journal compare). (2) session_replay.rs:119 replay takes &[&qip_execution_engine::session::RecordedSession], and its doc says no constructor exists outside the recorder. So 'archived segments are already readable' is false for the kernel path. (3) qip-kernel does not depend on qip-storage (Cargo.toml), and no ArchiveReader appears in qip-kernel or qip-deepbrain. (4) The scoring the shard must re-run is in private Platform::score_declined and score_filled (platform.rs:25573/25738), not in any replay module. The closure tells a lane to 'read archived segments through session_replay's from_archive', a symbol that does not exist, so the code slice is larger than stated and crosses a crate boundary. Corrected closure: keep everything else (one job shared with R12-TICK-7020 behind enable_replay_pool; the variables.tf and dev tfvars lines in one protected patch; the tftest showing no shared service or identity; the decision 9 cut-off; and the dependency on R12-DATA-8125's enable_cloud_storage). Replace the entry-point step with this: an architecture review (skill architecture-review) settles which crate reads qip-storage's segment ArchiveReader into the kernel's scoring inputs, and a public scoring seam over score_declined and score_filled is added. Only then may a lane land the shard entry point as code, with the test 'two shards over disjoint archived segments together reproduce the single-process replay's live-versus-counterfactual comparison'. Mutation: drop one shard's segments. Cost and trigger are unchanged (about $105 under R12-TICK-7020, after dev runs, decision 5).

decisions.ruling: Evidence reaches the NOW Brain only as a typed observation of a variable its catalogue already declares. The observation is mapped from an admitted, uncontested knowledge delta, at the delta's own instant, with its provenance as the manifest. A contested delta, a retraction or a delta that names no declared variable moves nothing and is counted. Raw source bytes never enter. The scout stays as R12-DATA-8112 rules, nothing new is billed, and the row stays PARTIAL until a deployed scout's record reaches the NOW stage.
decisions.rationale: The record is schema-closed: qip-contracts src/knowledge_delta.rs::KnowledgeDeltaFields with ChangeOp::Assert{key,value}/Retract and MergePolicy. qip-kernel src/evidence_intake.rs::Platform::absorb_evidence and knowledge_delta_for journal one KnowledgeDeltaRecord per admitted claim, ReviewRequired when contested. That evidence lands in WorldModel's evidence fabric (qip-world-model world.rs::WorldModel::absorb_evidence), not in its features. qip-kernel src/now_stage.rs::NowInputs takes only instruments, macro_surprises, company_features and causal_parents. qip-world-model now.rs::macro_surprises/company_features read features only, so no evidence ever reaches qip-world-model now.rs::NowBrain, whose Observation needs a VariableKey, partition, known_at and manifest. Admitting a new UNDERSTAND input with a named producer and consumer is what ADR 0151 decision 1 governs, so it needs a record. The NOW stage stays advisory: platform.rs::Platform::sizing_confidence reads the mark's confidence, not the NOW Brain. The consumer is in-process, so ADR 0199's confirmation of ADR 0151 d4 (one cross-brain exchange) stands. No scout exists yet: qip-deepbrain main.rs has no scout entry and catalogue.tf has no scout job (R12-DATA-8112).
decisions.adr_title: The NOW Brain reads an admitted, uncontested knowledge delta as a typed observation of a variable its catalogue declares, at the delta's own instant with its provenance as the manifest, and a contested delta, a retraction or an undeclared key moves nothing
decisions.closure: After the ADR (lane L2), Platform::understand_now reads the KnowledgeDeltaRecords absorbed since the last pass. It maps each MergePolicy::FastForwardOnly ChangeOp::Assert whose key names a declared NOW variable and whose value parses finite into a qip_world_model::now::Observation: source from originating_brain, known_at from created_at, manifest from the doc: provenance. It passes these in a new NowInputs field. Every other delta is counted on the NowReview detail and dropped. Test: 'an absorbed claim on a declared variable moves the NOW Brain's latent state at the next pass, and a contested, retracted or undeclared one moves nothing'. Mutations: ignore merge_policy, which must fail the contested case; drop the field, which must fail the moving case. R12-DATA-8112's scout follows separately. The row stays PARTIAL until a deployed scout's record is absorbed and reaches the NOW stage.
decisions.skeptic: The citations verify. knowledge_delta.rs has ChangeOp::Assert/Retract:31-33, MergePolicy:39 and provenance/originating_brain/created_at:62-69. evidence_intake.rs:194 knowledge_delta_for sets ReviewRequired when contested, and absorb_evidence is at :349. NowInputs:96-113 has no evidence field. now.rs Observation:538 needs key, partition, source, valid_at, known_at and manifest. But the claim 'The NOW stage stays advisory' rests on sizing_confidence alone, and that misses a real path into DECIDE. now_stage.rs:275-280 puts every Instrument-scope surprise into last_surprised. platform.rs:14794 passes that set to LatticeStage::run, which re-issues every horizon of a surprised subject out of turn (lattice_stage.rs:560-573) and resets current[slot] = (now, expires) (:617). DECIDE reads that slot through tactical_staleness at platform.rs:17956 (veto) and :18412 (the cap narrows by the share of life left). So an evidence claim on an instrument-scope declared variable ('return', 'realised_volatility' or 'spread_ratio') can surprise the NOW Brain, refresh that instrument's tactical forecasts, and lift the cap from below 1 to 1: a new external input enlarging a size bound. This contradicts R12-WORLD-3046's 'may only narrow, never enlarge'. The path is live in the execution brain: qip-fastbrain node.rs calls admit_world_records(feed.drain_evidence()) before run_cycle (:176-178), and its Connector arm drains evidence (feed.rs:599-605). Corrected ruling: keep the ruling and ADR as written, and add this clause: 'an evidence-derived observation never wakes the lattice: it is excluded from the surprised set, so it cannot re-issue a forecast out of turn or move a tactical slot DECIDE reads'. Add a second test: 'an absorbed claim on an instrument-scope declared variable moves the NOW latent state and leaves that instrument's tactical slots and DECIDE's staleness cap exactly as without it'. Mutation: let evidence surprises into last_surprised. Note also that originating_brain is the constant 'qip-kernel' (evidence_intake.rs:106), so 'source' collapses every evidence observation into one source. This is conservative for diversity, and the ADR should say so.

decisions.ruling: The seconds-minutes flow member reads the same signed aggressor flow R12-WORLD-3046's member reads: the paper feed's own trades, labelled simulated. A licensed tape later replaces the source, not the member. A trade with no aggressor contributes nothing. Where synthetic data is barred, the map stays empty and the member states the level. The lattice stays advisory, so no thesis, size or order reads a median the flow moved. Liquidity distributions and propagation speed are not invented from bars, and the row stays PARTIAL on them; the requirement text is not read down to pass it.
decisions.rationale: The member is built and mutation-tested: qip-world-model lattice.rs::ModelFamily::OrderFlow, FLOW_SHIFT_PER_SD (:264) and the project OrderFlow arm (:746), with tests/forecast_lattice.rs::the_seconds_row_holds_a_flow_member_whose_distribution_moves_with_the_imbalance. It has no input: qip-kernel lattice_stage.rs::signals_from_world builds flow_imbalance as BTreeMap::new() (:188), and LatticeStage::set_signals (:340) has no caller outside lattice_stage.rs and tests/lattice_specialists.rs (grep). ADR 0151 decision 6 says set_signals 'stays uncalled' and names a licensed tape as the source. R12-WORLD-3046 is already ruled ADR_THEN_IMPLEMENT: the simulated tape's aggressor side (qip-market-ingestion synthetic/book.rs Trade{aggressor: Some}) feeds an order-flow member labelled simulated, amending d6. This row uses that source and does not contradict it. qip-world-model order_flow.rs::FlowObservation::imbalance_ratio gives the [-1,1] figure the lattice refuses outside of. The lattice_stage.rs module doc says nothing reaches the order path, and DECIDE reads only LatticeStage::tactical_staleness (platform.rs, R12-WORLD-9024). One call site is shared with R12-WORLD-3086/3088, so one ADR covers it.
decisions.adr_title: The forecast lattice's row signals are set every UNDERSTAND pass from what the world model holds at the pass: a catalyst or a live causal claim may only widen its row, and the flow map reads only R12-WORLD-3046's signed aggressor flow labelled simulated (narrows ADR 0151 decision 6's uncalled clause)
decisions.closure: Lane L2 does this after R12-WORLD-3046's record and this ADR. decisions.ruling: Wire the catalyst. Every UNDERSTAND pass hands the lattice the macro surprises the world model holds at that instant, so a recent release widens the hours-days row without moving its median. ADR 0151 decision 6's 'uncalled' clause is narrowed to the flow map by a new record, not by editing it. The row stays PARTIAL: options and hedge-demand specialists wait on a licensed options source I have not bought (ADR 0157, R12-TICK-1175), and the company specialist and a ReactionEpisode holder are not built. The 3087 precedent does not read them away.
decisions.rationale: The member and the reader exist and are tested: qip-world-model lattice.rs::ModelFamily::EventReaction and CatalystExpectation, tests/forecast_lattice.rs::a_pending_catalyst_widens_the_hours_row_without_moving_its_median, qip-kernel lattice_stage.rs::signals_from_world (CATALYST_WINDOW, MACRO_PASS_THROUGH, MAX_CATALYST_MOVE), and tests/lattice_specialists.rs::a_recent_macro_surprise_is_the_pending_catalyst_and_an_old_or_future_one_is_not. R12-TICK-3097's synthetic drivers are never read in UNDERSTAND as evidence.

decisions.ruling: Spanner Graph stays declined, as R12-AMBIENT-9001 already decided O02: BigQuery is the one evidence store agents read, and Bigtable, Spanner Graph and Knowledge Catalog wait for an ADR that states a measured need and a monthly ceiling. No graph writer is written against a store ADR 0113 does not admit. The edge-isolation half is already proven. The row stays PARTIAL until that record exists and a funded instance runs.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0113:57 says 'Bigtable, AlloyDB and Spanner Graph are not admitted by this record'. qip-mesh src/provider.rs::MeshTarget::SpannerGraph has only a description and a required_configuration of 'the same ... Spanner instance and database with a property graph'. It therefore bills as the Spanner instance. modules/data/main.tf::google_spanner_instance.global sits behind enable_spanner = false in all four tfvars. billed-plan-2026-10-19.md item 7 prices it at $2,705-$8,140 a month ('Do not turn on'). The isolation half holds: backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/architecture.rs::no_edge_cell_can_reach_a_historical_data_reader keeps qip-world-model in READERS (:816-824). The row depends on R12-DATA-8015.
decisions.closure: The row reopens only after dev runs, through an ADR under ADR 0113 §1 that admits Spanner Graph with a measured need and a monthly ceiling, superseding R12-AMBIENT-9001's decline for this store. decisions.ruling: O24 is decided without a new service. The deep brain, already its own Cloud Run service, is the strategic forecast service. It alone serves the weeks-months and quarters-years rows, and the fast brain, which runs the paper execution cycle, never asks a strategic question. While the deep brain is lost, its strategic questions wait in the lattice's bounded backlog (ADR 0214). Stopping it leaves the fast brain's cycles exactly as they were. No new image, identity or minimum instance is bought (decision 5, ADR 0191).
decisions.rationale: Backlog semantics exist: qip-kernel lattice_stage.rs::LatticeStage::run backlogs a strategic slot when !strategic_available (:576), proven by tests/now_lattice.rs::with_the_strategic_service_down_its_questions_wait_and_every_stage_still_runs. Only qip-deepbrain src/node.rs::gate_strategic_service (:201-207) sets availability, from ADR 0214's cognition::ai_platform_lost. qip-fastbrain src/node.rs:178 runs platform.run_cycle with strategic_available at its default of true (lattice_stage.rs:329), so today the execution brain serves the strategic rows in-process, and the separation is only a flag. infrastructure/terraform/catalogue.tf declares fastbrain (:435) and deepbrain (:545) as separate services. A third service would add a billed minimum instance: the runbook §5 prices the two brains at about $105 and $280. ADR 0191 keeps world-model services in the central brains and refuses a split before deployment. Nothing in DECIDE reads a strategic row: the lattice_stage.rs module doc says it is advisory, and the platform's decide path reads only LatticeStage::tactical_staleness (R12-WORLD-9024). Removing the rows from the fast brain therefore loosens no guard.
decisions.adr_title: The deep brain is the strategic forecast service: only it serves the weeks-to-years lattice rows, the fast brain never asks one, and no separate strategic service is deployed (decides O24, under ADR 0191 and ADR 0214)
decisions.closure: Lane L2 does this after the ADR. The backlog is at lattice_stage.rs:575-580 (strategic && !strategic_available), proven by now_lattice.rs::with_the_strategic_service_down_its_questions_wait_and_every_stage_still_runs. set_strategic_available is called only by qip-deepbrain node.rs::gate_strategic_service (:201-207) and tests, and it is driven by cognition::ai_platform_lost. qip-fastbrain node.rs:178 calls run_cycle with the default strategic_available: true (lattice_stage.rs:329). catalogue.tf declares fastbrain (:435) and deepbrain (:545). deepbrain node.rs:218 runs run_cycle, so it already serves the strategic rows. ADR 0191 refuses a world-model split before deployment, so no new billed service is created and decision 5 is respected. The claim that removing strategic rows from the fast brain loosens nothing holds. tactical_staleness reads only SecondsMinutes and HoursDays (lattice_stage.rs:405), the lattice inconsistencies are metrics only (platform.rs:14837-14850), and DECIDE reads no strategic forecast. This is consistent with R12-RES-10130, which builds on gate_strategic_service in the deep brain. The test and mutation are concrete, and the existing backlog test is left unchanged.
